• src/test-setup.js initializes i18n synchronously with lng: 'vi' and the real resources. Most existing Vietnamese assertions keep working. Assertions on English chrome ("Home") are updated to the Vietnamese value or switched to role/key-based queries.
  • CI guards:
    • A key-parity test: vi and en have identical key sets per namespace, and no value is empty.
    • The same check for messages.properties against messages_vi.properties in JUnit.
  • Each switched component gets at least one test that renders in en.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive

  • Every user-facing string lives in one place per language.
  • Adding a language means adding JSON and properties files only.
  • Errors and emails match the user's language.

Negative / costs

  • Three new frontend dependencies, about 20 KB gzipped, plus an update to tech-strategy.md.
  • Touches about 40 components and 21 test files, so the diff is large. It is phased by area to keep PRs reviewable.
  • ResultErrorInfo gains a field. This is additive, so existing clients are unaffected.

Risks

  • Cloudflare caching. If any API error or GET response is edge-cached, the language would leak between users. Mitigation: send Vary: Accept-Language on localized responses, and verify that /api JSON is not cached at the edge (QA-1).
  • Missing keys at runtime. Mitigated by the parity tests. Set saveMissing: false and returnNull: false, and fall back to en.
  • Admin-only strings are lower value. They are translated last (FE-5) and can be deferred without blocking the rest.

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text:
• Spring MessageSource and LocaleResolver are part of Spring Boot, so the backend stays on the Golden Path.
  • One Liquibase migration (D5); no ddl-auto.
  • No secrets and no new infrastructure.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-10-15) · Date: 2026-10-15 · Deciders: nguyenhuuca · Tags: history, privacy, data-model, api-contract Supersedes: ADR-0013, ADR-0014. Both were written on 2026-06-01, before collections, i18n, the view counter and the History page existed, and neither was implemented. Related: PRD-watch-history-v2 · plan-watch-history-v2 · ADR-0020 (i18n)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• The History page (nav key history) exists, but it only holds "My suggestions". The Stitch design ("History & My Suggestions") adds a watch-history tab: entries grouped by day, a watched-progress bar, "pause history", "clear all" and search.
  • The player already reports real playback. VideoPlayer calls POST /videos/{id}/view once 3 s of real, visible playback have been watched; seeks are ignored. VideoViewServiceImpl dedupes per viewer for 30 min and increments video_sources.view_count. The request carries the JWT, so the server knows the user.
  • user_settings.incognito_enabled exists, and Settings shows it as "Incognito Mode — watch history won't be recorded while active". Nothing reads it yet.
  • Per-user tables in this schema (video_reactions, video_collection_items) use a composite primary key and native INSERT … ON CONFLICT.
  • Prod runs on a 1 vCPU VM with Postgres on the same host. Writes must stay cheap, with no fan-out.

docs.title: Decision Drivers
docs.text:
• One trigger, one threshold: a "watch" means the same thing as a counted view (≥ 3 s of real playback), with no second client timer.
  • No extra requests on play start: zero new requests for the common case.
  • Privacy:
    • Owner-only access, derived from the JWT and never from a client userId.
    • Incognito really records nothing, including progress.
    • The user can delete one entry or everything.
  • Bounded storage: at most 500 entries per user, enforced on write.
  • Convention fit: composite primary key and native upsert, like video_reactions. Liquibase SQL. No new infrastructure.

docs.title: D1. Record history inside the existing view endpoint
docs.text:
• In POST /videos/{id}/view, an authenticated caller who is not in incognito also gets a history upsert.
  • This is independent of the 30-minute view dedupe: a re-watch inside the window still moves the entry to the top. It does not count a second view.
  • Guests (IP viewer key) get no history.
  • Rejected: a separate POST /watch-history on play start (ADR-0013/0014). It costs an extra request per play and duplicates the threshold logic. It would also record 1-second skips.

docs.title: D2. Table watch_history, composite primary key (user_id, video_id)
docs.text:
watch_history(
  user_id      BIGINT      NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  video_id     BIGINT      NOT NULL REFERENCES video_sources(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  watched_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  position_sec INT         NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (position_sec >= 0),
  duration_sec INT                      CHECK (duration_sec > 0),
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, video_id))
INDEX (user_id, watched_at DESC)
  • One row per user per video. A re-watch updates watched_at.
  • The upsert inserts through INSERT … SELECT … FROM video_sources WHERE id = ? AND is_hide = false AND status = 'PUBLISHED', the same public-visibility rule as the feed. An unknown or hidden id therefore writes nothing, and no foreign-key error escapes. This replaces ADR-0014's "store null video_id" approach.
  • Rejected: a BIGINT surrogate key or a UUID. The pair is the identity, and no entry id is ever exposed.

docs.title: D3. 500-entry cap, enforced in the upsert transaction
docs.text:
• After the upsert, run DELETE FROM watch_history WHERE user_id = ? AND video_id IN (SELECT video_id … ORDER BY watched_at DESC OFFSET 500).
  • This is self-healing under concurrency: a concurrent writer can only leave the table transiently over the cap.
  • There is no time-based retention job. The cap bounds storage at 500 × users.

docs.title: D4. Progress is a separate, update-only call
docs.text:
• PUT /watch-history/{videoId}/progress {positionSec, durationSec} updates the existing row only. It never inserts, so it cannot bypass the 3 s threshold.
  • It is a no-op in incognito.
  • The client sends it on pause, on switching video, on tab hide and every 30 s while playing. It uses fetch with keepalive. sendBeacon is not usable because it cannot send the Authorization header.
  • The server clamps values: position ≤ duration, duration ≤ 6 h.
  • A video counts as completed at ≥ 90 % or within 10 s of the end. Completed videos show "Watched" and resume from 0.

docs.title: D5. Read API, owner-scoped and paged
docs.text:
• GET /watch-history?q=&page=&size= returns entries newest first, joined to video_sources in one query (no N+1). q is a case-insensitive title match.
  • GET /watch-history/summary returns at most 500 entries as {videoId, positionSec, durationSec}. It drives the "Watched" badges and resume without a request per card.
  • DELETE /watch-history/{videoId} and DELETE /watch-history return 204.
  • The client groups entries into Today / Yesterday / Earlier in the user's local time zone.

docs.title: D6. "Pause history" is user_settings.incognito_enabled
docs.text:
• The History page toggle and the Settings "Incognito Mode" toggle edit the same flag through the existing PATCH /user/settings. They are two entry points for one setting, with no new column.
  • While it is on, D1 and D4 write nothing. Existing entries remain readable and deletable.

docs.title: D7. Account deletion clears history
docs.text: UserSettingsServiceImpl.deleteAccount soft-deletes the user (ADR-0016). It now also deletes that user's watch_history, because viewing history is personal data with no audit value. The cascade covers hard deletes.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive:

  • No new request on play start.
  • History and view counts share one definition of a watch.
  • Incognito finally does what Settings says.
  • Storage is bounded.

Negative:

  • History depends on the view call. A blocked or dropped view request means no history entry. This is the same best-effort contract as view counts, and it is acceptable.
  • Progress heartbeats add about 1 small PUT per 30 s per active logged-in viewer. On 1 vCPU this is fine at current traffic; revisit if traffic grows ten times.
  • The title search is accent-sensitive (ILIKE). The unaccent extension is a later option (see open questions in the PRD).

Reversibility: a two-way door. The table and endpoints are additive. Rollback drops the table and removes the upsert call from the view path.

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text:
• @RateLimited:
    • GET list: 60/min
    • summary: 30/min
    • progress: 120/min
    • deletes: 20/min
  • All endpoints are authenticated and use the JWT user id only.
  • Tests cover:
    • owner isolation
    • incognito
    • the cap
    • a hidden or unknown video
    • re-watch inside the dedupe window
    • clamping

docs.title: ADR-0022: Headless Autopilot on GitHub Actions
Metadata
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-10-19, after the first end-to-end run: issue #26 → PR #27 merged) · amended by ADR-0025 (opt-in auto gates) · Date: 2026-10-19 · Deciders: nguyenhuuca · Tags: ci, agents, security, workflow Related: plan-autopilot (the local skill) · plan-autopilot-headless · Claude Code GitHub Actions docs

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• /autopilot runs plan → review → build → QA → land with two human gates. It only runs inside an interactive terminal session, and the gates use AskUserQuestion.
  • Goal ("Level 5"): hand work to the agent from GitHub, without opening a terminal, and keep both gates.
  • anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 runs Claude Code in a GitHub Actions job:
    • automation mode with a prompt, which can be a skill invocation such as /autopilot …;
    • auth: claude_code_oauth_token (subscription) or anthropic_api_key;
    • trigger check: on issue and PR events, the triggering user must have write access, and bots are rejected unless listed.
  • Repo facts:
    • nguyenhuuca/assessment is public, with 1 collaborator (the owner). Anyone can open issues and comment.
    • CI deploys on push to main (and VID-*). Other branches run no CI and deploy nothing.
    • The repo convention is "commit on main, ask before every push".

docs.title: Decision Drivers
docs.text:
1. Both gates stay human. The agent never pushes to main.
  2. Untrusted input: on a public repo, issue and comment text from anyone except the owner must not start a run or steer one.
  3. Least privilege: the job gets only the secrets and token scopes it needs. The deploy secrets (SSH, Docker) are never visible to it.
  4. Bounded cost and time per run.
  5. Reuse the local skill. The headless path is one mode of the same SKILL.md, not a second workflow to maintain.

docs.title: D1. Gates on GitHub: branch + PR, merge = Gate 2
docs.text:
• Start: the owner adds the label autopilot to an issue.
  • Plan job:
    • runs /autopilot --headless plan --issue <N>;
    • writes the plan and TASKS.md section on branch autopilot/issue-<N>;
    • opens a draft PR with the plan summary and the plan-review verdict;
    • comments on the issue.
  • Gate 1: the owner comments /approve on the PR. /revise <notes> re-runs the plan job with the notes.
  • Build job:
    • runs /autopilot --headless build --pr <N>: implement ⇄ review, QA ×2, full gates;
    • commits and pushes to the PR branch only;
    • writes the run report, then marks the PR ready for review with the report in its body.
  • Gate 2: the owner merges the PR. The merge is the push to main and triggers the normal deploy, followed by the owner's smoke check.
  • Exception to "commit on main": headless runs use a branch + PR, because a merge is the only gate GitHub can offer. Local runs keep committing on main.

docs.title: D2. Who can trigger
docs.text:
Each job runs only when both checks pass:

  • the action's built-in write-access check;
  • an explicit workflow if: github.event.sender.login == github.repository_owner (label or comment author).

The build and revise jobs also require:

  • the PR head branch starts with autopilot/;
  • the comment starts with /approve or /revise.

docs.title: D3. Untrusted content
docs.text:
• The issue title and body are data: the request to plan. Instructions inside them that try to change the workflow, permissions, secrets or gates are ignored and quoted in the PR as a finding.
  • Paths a headless run refuses to touch: .github/, .claude/, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, **/*.env*, scripts/claude-*, and migrations that drop or rewrite data. A request that needs them is refused at the scope guard.

docs.title: D4. Auth and least privilege
docs.text:
• Auth: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (subscription), created by the owner with claude setup-token and stored as a repo secret by the owner.
  • GitHub token: the workflow passes github_token: ${{ github.token }} with job permissions contents: write, pull-requests: write, issues: write, so the broad Claude GitHub App is not needed. Pushes made with this token start no workflows. That is fine here, because autopilot/* branches have no CI.
  • No other secrets are referenced by the job.
  • The Bash allowlist is a guardrail, not a boundary. node, mvn, npm, awk and sed can all run arbitrary code, and the build job needs them. The OAuth token is present in the job, so a determined prompt injection could reach it. The real boundaries are:
    • only the owner can trigger (D2);
    • both gates are human;
    • the job has no deploy secrets;
    • the token can be revoked by running claude setup-token again.
    • curl and wget are not allowed, which keeps casual exfiltration harder.

docs.title: D5. Limits
docs.text:
• Workers run in the foreground: settings: {"env":{"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS":"1"}}. In -p mode the session ends with the turn, so a background worker's result is lost. This was found on the first run for issue #26: the plan job ended "waiting for the review" without a PR.

  • Each job has timeout-minutes: 60.

  • One run at a time, first come first served: a queue job waits until every older active run of the workflow is done, and plan / build need it. Amended 2026-10-22: it replaces concurrency: autopilot (cancel-in-progress: false), because GitHub keeps only one pending run per group and cancels it when a newer one queues, so the middle of three issues labeled at once was lost.
  • --max-turns per job.
  • The skill's round caps (3) still apply. After each job, scripts/claude-autopilot-cost.sh (run from main, so a PR branch cannot change it) posts the job's cost from the action's result and appends it to the run report on the PR branch.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Positive:
    • Work can be started and approved from a phone, and every run leaves a PR with its plan, verdicts, report and diff.
    • Deploy secrets stay out of reach.
  • Negative:
    • Plan and build run in separate jobs, so the build job re-reads the plan from the branch. There is no shared conversation context, which may cost a little more per run.
    • Merging from GitHub skips the local "ask before push" prompt. The merge button is that prompt.
    • The subscription token is tied to the owner's account, so its usage counts against the owner's plan limits.
  • Risks:
    • A prompt injection inside an issue the owner labels. Mitigations: D3 path denylist, both human gates, and the diff is reviewed before merge.
    • Action behaviour changes upstream. Mitigation: pin @v1 and review on upgrade.

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text:
The decision holds if:

  • autopilot.yml contains the owner check from D2;
  • no job references secrets other than CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN;
  • no job pushes to main;
  • SKILL.md keeps the D3 denylist in headless mode.

docs.title: ADR-0023: Dynamic Cron Jobs (DB-backed schedule, admin API)
Metadata
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-10-19) · Date: 2026-10-19 · Deciders: nguyenhuuca · Tags: scheduling, admin, api-contract, data-model Related: plan-dynamic-cron-jobs

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Every recurring job lives in jobs/AppScheduler.java with a hardcoded @Scheduled (AppScheduler.java:69, 79, 91, 107, 117, 127). Changing a schedule, or turning a job off, needs a code change and a deploy.
  • Two annotations are already wrong against their own comments: the log at :71 says 10:10 but the cron is 10:45, and the comment at :91 says 20 minutes but the cron is every 15. cleanUpOldVideos (:127) uses 0 0 3 30 2 * (30 February), so it never fires, and its body is a no-op (:130-132).
  • @EnableScheduling is at FunnyApp.java:17. No custom TaskScheduler or SchedulingConfigurer exists, and virtual threads are on (application.yaml:46), so Spring Boot's auto-configured TaskScheduler bean is the one to use.
  • Prod runs one replica (HPA 1-1, tech-strategy.md Infrastructure) on a 1 vCPU VM.
  • tech-strategy.md forbids synchronized and does not list Quartz or ShedLock.
  • Admin pattern to follow: AdminDriveSyncController.java:30-56. ADMIN reads, and only SUPER_ADMIN plus the ADMIN permission may mutate (:55), with @AuditLog and @RateLimited. /v1/funny-app/admin/** is role-guarded at WebSecurityConfig.java:54, and PATCH is already allowed in CORS (WebSecurityConfig.java:139).

docs.title: Decision Drivers
docs.text:
• Change a job's cron, zone or on/off state without a deploy, and see it take effect immediately.
  • No new library and no new infrastructure.
  • Safe on 1 vCPU:
    • a job can never run twice at the same time;
    • an admin cannot schedule a job every second.
  • Destructive or costly controls are restricted to SUPER_ADMIN.

docs.title: D1. Table scheduled_job is the source of truth for schedules
docs.text:
scheduled_job(
  name        VARCHAR(64) PRIMARY KEY,   -- stable key, e.g. 'notification-digest'
  cron        VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,      -- Spring 6-field cron
  zone        VARCHAR(64),               -- NULL = JVM default zone (today's behavior for jobs without zone)
  enabled     BOOLEAN     NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  description VARCHAR(255),
  updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
)
  • The Liquibase SQL migration seeds one row per job with today's cron and zone. logStats moves from fixedRate 5 min to 0 */5 * * * *, so its runs now line up with the clock. cleanup-old-videos is seeded with enabled = false, which matches today's "never fires".
  • The job code stays in AppScheduler. Only the schedule moves. A row without code is ignored with a WARN at startup, and code without a row is not scheduled, also with a WARN.
  • Last run time and result are kept in memory only. That means no DB write per run, and they reset on restart.

docs.title: D2. JobRegistry maps a name to code
docs.text: JobRegistry is a @Component holding a Map<String, Runnable>, built from AppScheduler method references. Names are constants in one place. @Scheduled is removed from the six methods.

docs.title: D3. DynamicJobScheduler uses Spring's TaskScheduler + CronTrigger
docs.text:
• On ApplicationReadyEvent, it loads all rows and schedules the enabled ones.
  • It keeps a ConcurrentHashMap<String, ScheduledFuture<?>>.
    • reschedule(job) runs inside map.compute(name, …), which is atomic per key: cancel the old future (cancel(false)), then schedule a new one if enabled.
    • Two concurrent PATCHes therefore cannot leave two schedules for one job. No synchronized is used.
  • Overlap guard: a ConcurrentHashMap<String, AtomicBoolean> per job.
    • A run starts only if compareAndSet(false, true) succeeds; otherwise it is skipped and logged.
    • This covers a scheduled fire, a "run now", and a slow previous run alike.
  • Each run is wrapped in try/catch, so one failing job does not affect the scheduler. The result goes to the in-memory status.

docs.title: D4. Admin API under /v1/funny-app/admin/jobs
docs.text:
Method Path Who Notes GET /admin/jobs ADMIN (@HasPermission ADMIN) List of name, description, cron, zone, enabled, nextRunAt (from CronExpression.next), lastRunAt, lastResult, running PATCH /admin/jobs/{name} SUPER_ADMIN + ADMIN perm (same expression as AdminDriveSyncController.java:55) Body {cron?, zone?, enabled?}, @AuditLog, @RateLimited(permit = 10) POST /admin/jobs/{name}/runs SUPER_ADMIN + ADMIN perm 202 when started, 409 when already running, @AuditLog, @RateLimited(permit = 5)

Validation, with errors as CustomException + i18n keys:

  • cron: must pass CronExpression.isValidExpression. Its seconds field must also be a single number (0–59), which means at most once per minute and prevents * * * * * *.
  • zone: must pass ZoneId.of.
  • name: an unknown name gets 404.

docs.title: D5. One replica → no distributed lock
docs.text:
• A schedule change applies to the pod that served the PATCH, and it persists to the DB for the next start. With one replica, that is all pods.
  • When HPA max > 1, a new ADR must add one of two options:
    • ShedLock (JDBC provider, one lock row per job), which is enough for "run once across pods";
    • Quartz with a JDBC job store, if clustered misfire handling or run history is needed.
  • At the same time, schedule changes must reach the other pods, e.g. through a DB poll of updated_at.
  • Until then, a rolling deploy can briefly run two pods. That is the same exposure as today's @Scheduled, so it is unchanged.

docs.title: D6. Out of scope
docs.text:
These are infrastructure timers, not business jobs:

  • the SSE heartbeat (InMemorySsePublisher.java:89);
  • the import poll (VideoImportWorker.java:110);
  • the one-off thumbnail runner (AppScheduler.java:63-67).

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text: Option Runtime change New dependency Effort Verdict Cron in application.yaml + env (${…} in @Scheduled) No (restart) No XS Rejected: does not meet "without a deploy" DB table + TaskScheduler (this ADR) Yes No S Chosen Quartz JDBC store Yes Yes (Quartz, ~11 tables) M Rejected for now: off tech strategy, oversized for 1 replica (see D5)

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Positive:
    • Schedules can be edited, paused or run on demand from the Admin UI, and every change is audit-logged.
    • The wrong comments disappear.
  • Negative:
    • A bad but valid cron (e.g. 03:00 vs 15:00) now takes effect without code review. Mitigations: the change is audit-logged and restricted to SUPER_ADMIN, and the UI shows nextRunAt before and after the change.
    • Last-run state is lost on restart.
  • Reversibility: Two-way door. Putting @Scheduled back and dropping the table restores today's behavior.

docs.title: ADR-0024: cronstrue for Human-Readable Cron Text
Metadata
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-10-19) · Date: 2026-10-19 · Deciders: nguyenhuuca · Tags: frontend, dependency, scheduling Related: ADR-0023

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The Admin → Scheduled jobs tab (ADR-0023) needs two things:

  • a tooltip on each cron;
  • a crontab.guru-style editor that says in words what a cron means ("Every 15 minutes", "Mỗi 15 phút").

Writing a cron-to-text describer by hand means:

  • covering every Spring cron form (lists, ranges, steps, MON-FRI, L…);
  • translating every phrase into en and vi.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Library: use cronstrue in webapp/ (MIT, zero dependencies).
    • It understands 6-field crons with seconds.
    • It ships vi and en locales.
    • Only cronstrue + cronstrue/locales/vi are imported, not the all-locales cronstrue/i18n bundle.
  • Version: pinned exactly (3.29.0), the newest release that was at least two weeks old when it was added. 3.33.0 had been published the same day.
  • Text only: cronstrue gives the description, nothing else.
  • Validation and next runs stay on the server:
    • GET /admin/jobs/preview uses Spring CronExpression and the same rules as PATCH, so there is one source of truth for "is this cron valid and when does it fire".
    • The FE only pre-checks the shape (6 fields, seconds = one number) to avoid useless requests.

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text: Option Verdict cronstrue (text) + server preview (validation, next runs) Chosen Hand-written describer (BE or FE) Rejected: weaker text for complex crons, two translations to maintain cron-parser in the FE for next runs Rejected: a second library whose semantics may differ from Spring (e.g. day-of-week 0/7)

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• webapp gains one small runtime dependency (~25 KB min). It appears in .claude/rules/tech-strategy.md.
  • If cronstrue ever mis-describes a cron, the impact is cosmetic only. The next-run times come from the server.

docs.title: ADR-0025: Opt-in Auto Gates for Headless Autopilot
Metadata
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-10-20) · Date: 2026-10-20 · Deciders: nguyenhuuca · Tags: ci, agents, security, workflow Related: amends ADR-0022 D1 (both gates human) and D4 (only one secret)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Headless autopilot (ADR-0022) stops twice for the owner: /approve at Gate 1 and a merge at Gate 2.
  • The owner wants small issues to go through when they are busy, with no approval.
  • Two GitHub limits shape the design:
    • Comments posted with the job token start no workflows, so a bot /approve cannot start the build job. workflow_dispatch is the exception: the job token can start it.
    • A merge made with the job token does not start the push-to-main deploy CI. The merge needs another token.
  • The repo is public, so the checks that decide a merge must not depend on what the model says.

docs.title: D1. Opt-in labels on the issue
docs.text:
Label (added with autopilot) Gate 1 Gate 2 none /approve owner merges autopilot:auto-merge /approve automatic autopilot:auto automatic automatic
  • The labels only change gates. autopilot is still the only label that starts a run.
  • The issue author check from ADR-0022 D2 still applies. In this repo only the owner can add labels.

docs.title: D2. Auto Gate 1: the workflow dispatches the build
docs.text:
• Marker: the plan job writes <!-- autopilot:plan-review=approve --> in the PR body, and only when the plan review returned approve.
  • Workflow step: after the plan job, a workflow step checks two things:
    • the issue has autopilot:auto;
    • the open autopilot/issue-<N> PR has the marker.
  • If both hold: the step runs gh workflow run autopilot.yml -f pr=<N> and comments on the PR.
  • If the marker is missing: it comments that Gate 1 stays manual.
  • Scope: only a first plan (the issues event) dispatches. A /revise always waits for /approve.
  • Who can start the build: the dispatched build accepts the actor github-actions[bot] or the owner. allowed_bots: "github-actions[bot]" is set only on the build step.

docs.title: D3. Auto Gate 2: a deterministic merge script
docs.text:
scripts/claude-autopilot-merge.sh is always run from origin/main, never from the PR branch. It merges only when every check passes; otherwise it comments the reason and leaves the PR for the owner. The checks:

  1. The head branch is autopilot/issue-<N>.
  2. The issue or PR has autopilot:auto-merge or autopilot:auto.
  3. The PR is open and not a draft. The model marks it ready only after a code-review approve and green gates.
  4. No protected paths changed:
    • .github/, .claude/, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, scripts/claude-*;
    • Liquibase migrations (api/src/main/resources/db/changelog/);
    • .env* files.
    • A schema change always gets a human.
  5. At most 400 changed lines outside tests and docs (AUTOPILOT_MAX_LOC).
  6. The gates are re-run by the script, not taken from the model's report:
    • mvn verify when api/ changed;
    • vitest run, lint and build when webapp/ changed.
  7. The merge: gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit <sha> with the secret AUTOPILOT_MERGE_TOKEN. Its push starts the normal deploy CI.

docs.title: D4. The merge token
docs.text:
• Token type: a fine-grained PAT (or GitHub App token) created and stored by the owner. Scope: this repo only, with Contents: read/write and Pull requests: read/write.
  • Exposure: only the auto Gate 2 step sees it, through the step-level env. The Claude step never does.
  • If the secret is missing: the script comments and skips. Everything else keeps working.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Code reaches prod without a human read. The limits on that are:
    • the opt-in label;
    • two model reviews;
    • the re-run gates;
    • no migrations and no workflow or agent-config changes.
  • The smoke check after the deploy stays manual (./api/mock-test.sh). Smoke tests are read-only, so write paths are not covered.
  • ADR-0022 D4's "both gates are human" no longer holds for labelled issues. A prompt injection in a labelled issue body could now reach prod without anyone seeing it. The owner-only issue check (ADR-0022 D2) is what keeps that out.
  • Rolling back = git revert the squash commit on main and push.

docs.title: ADR-0026: In-App Report Creates GitHub Issues With the Owner's Token
Metadata
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-10-20), amended 2026-10-21 (D7 webhook) · Date: 2026-10-20 · Deciders: nguyenhuuca · Tags: api, integration, security, agents Related: PRD-in-app-report · amends the trust model of ADR-0022 D2 · works with ADR-0025

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• What the PRD asks for: a Report menu where an admin sends a bug, an enhancement or an issue. The server turns it into a GitHub issue labelled autopilot, so headless autopilot picks it up.
  • The workflow's owner-only check: .github/workflows/autopilot.yml starts only when the label sender is the repo owner (ADR-0022 D2). A server that creates issues with any identity other than the owner's does not start autopilot.
  • The repo is public, so issue text is public.
  • Existing building blocks:
    • External HTTP: java.net.http.HttpClient, for example client/HttpRedirectProbe.java:31-34. There is no Spring RestClient or WebClient in api/.
    • Rate limiting:
      • @RateLimited keys the limit by user name plus request URI (aop/RateLimitAspect.java:33-36, 52-55).
      • The limiter is in memory, which fits one replica (ADR-0023 D5).
    • Roles:
      • UserRole declaration order is the rank (enums/UserRole.java).
      • WebSecurityConfig.roleHierarchy() builds hasRole implications from that order (filter/WebSecurityConfig.java:81-88).
      • The role is stored as a string (entity/User.java:56-57, EnumType.STRING).
    • Permission bits: generic (READ, WRITE, EXEC, DELETE, ADMIN; enums/Permission.java). Admins get every bit.
    • Cache: Guava with expireAfterWrite (cache/CredentialsVersionCache.java:24-25).

docs.title: Decision Drivers
docs.text:
1. Autopilot must start from an app report with no extra click (owner's request: label autopilot by default).
  2. Least privilege: the server holds the smallest possible GitHub credential.
  3. Abuse control: reports start paid runs, and autopilot:auto can reach prod.
  4. Public repo: no personal data in issues.
  5. Follow existing patterns. Add no new library and no new infrastructure.

docs.title: Who creates the issue
docs.text: Option Pros Cons Verdict A. Fine-grained PAT of the owner, server calls the GitHub REST API Issue sender is the owner, so autopilot starts with no workflow change; one repo, Issues only; no new infra Every ADMIN acts as the owner toward autopilot; PAT on the server Chosen B. GitHub App (bot identity) Separate, revocable identity; clean audit on GitHub The workflow must trust a bot (rewrite ADR-0022 D2 and the job if); App setup and key storage; more moving parts for one feature Rejected for v1 C. Create the issue without autopilot; the owner adds the label Keeps the owner as the only gate Loses the "autopilot by default" requirement Rejected D. gh CLI on the server Familiar Needs a CLI and auth state on the VM; shells out with user text Rejected

docs.title: Access for a future CONTRIBUTOR
docs.text: Option Pros Cons Verdict New role CONTRIBUTOR between USER and ADMIN roleHierarchy() already derives ADMIN > CONTRIBUTOR > USER from enum order; endpoints just say hasRole('CONTRIBUTOR') Inserting it moves ordinal(). That is safe only because roles are stored as strings and ranked by outranks. Chosen (later) New permission bit REPORT Fine-grained Bits are generic verbs today, so this starts a per-feature bit pattern. ALL_BITS changes, and stored admin masks need a migration. Rejected

docs.title: D1. GitHub client
docs.text:
• Interface: GitHubIssueClient in the client package, implemented with java.net.http.HttpClient and Jackson, like HttpRedirectProbe. It has two calls:
    • POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues with title, body and labels;
    • GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number} for the state.
  • Config: AppProperties.github with token, owner and repo. The token comes from the env var GITHUB_REPORT_TOKEN.
  • Token rules:
    • Fine-grained PAT, this repo only, Issues read/write.
    • Never logged, never returned to the browser, masked by @AuditLog.
  • Timeouts: connect 5 s, request 10 s.

docs.title: D2. Labels and trust (amends ADR-0022 D2)
docs.text:
• Labels on every issue: autopilot plus one type label: bug, enhancement or report.
  • Auto labels: autopilot:auto and autopilot:auto-merge are accepted only from SUPER_ADMIN. The server checks this and returns 403 to an ADMIN; hiding the option in the UI is not the check.
  • Trust change:
    • Because the PAT is the owner's, an ADMIN report starts autopilot.
    • The owner-only check in ADR-0022 D2 now means "the owner, or an admin through the app". Admin accounts are granted only by the SUPER_ADMIN.
  • Report text is data, exactly like issue text today (ADR-0022 D3). The headless denylist and the ADR-0025 merge checks still apply.

docs.title: D3. Abuse limits
docs.text:
• Per user: @RateLimited(permit = 5, windowInSeconds = 3600) on create and on retry (NFR-4). It is in memory, so a restart resets it; that is acceptable.
  • Global daily cap on reports that carry autopilot: 10 per rolling 24 h, counted from the stored reports, so it survives a restart.
    • Over the cap: the issue is still created, but without autopilot.
    • The user is told that the owner can add the label.
  • Audit: @AuditLog on create and on retry. Each stored report keeps its reporter.

docs.title: D4. Storage and status
docs.text:
• Table: app_report, added by a Liquibase migration in db/changelog/sql/. Columns:
    • id, reporter_id (FK to users);
    • type, title, description;
    • context (path, app version, user agent, screen width);
    • labels, status (CREATED / FAILED), issue_number, issue_url, error;
    • created_at, updated_at.
  • Write path:
    1. Save the report as FAILED.
    2. Call GitHub.
    3. On success, set CREATED with the issue number and URL.
    4. On failure, keep FAILED with a short error (no token, no response body). Retry repeats steps 2 and 3.
  • Duplicates: the issue body ends with <!-- app-report:{id} -->. A response lost after GitHub created the issue can lead to a duplicate on retry; the marker lets the owner find and close it. The risk is accepted.
  • Status: read through from GitHub when the list loads:
    • one GET per issue on the page, in parallel on virtual threads;
    • cached in Guava for 5 min;
    • a failure shows unknown.
    • Superseded for issues with a stored state by D7: the list reads the state from the table and calls GitHub only for rows that have none.
  • List scope: every admin sees all reports, newest first, paged, with the reporter's display name. The issues are public anyway.

docs.title: D5. Issue body (public repo)
docs.text:
• Content, in order:
    1. the description as typed;
    2. a "Context" section: page path without the query string, app version, user agent, screen width;
    3. the footer "Reported in-app by <display name> · report #<id>".
  • Never in the body: the email, IDs other than the report id, or tokens.
  • Form warning: the form says that the text will be public.

docs.title: D6. Future CONTRIBUTOR
docs.text:
• v1: the endpoints use hasRole('ADMIN').
  • When CONTRIBUTOR is added:
    • insert it into UserRole between USER and ADMIN;
    • change the endpoints to hasRole('CONTRIBUTOR');
    • add a migration if the role column has a check constraint;
    • leave the auto-label rule (SUPER_ADMIN only) unchanged.

docs.title: D7. Issue state by webhook (amendment, 2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The owner asked for the closed state to be pushed to the app and stored, and to tell "done" from "closed, not planned".

  • Endpoint: POST /v1/funny-app/webhooks/github, added to WHITE_LIST_PATH (utils/AppConstant.java:45), so no JWT. GitHub is the only intended caller.
  • Authentication: the HMAC-SHA256 signature in X-Hub-Signature-256 over the raw body, with the shared secret from the env var GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
    • Compared in constant time (MessageDigest.isEqual) before the body is parsed.
    • Missing or wrong signature → 401. Secret not configured → 503, so the endpoint is off until the owner sets it.
    • The secret is never logged; the delivery id (X-GitHub-Delivery) is logged at INFO.
  • Events: only X-GitHub-Event: issues with action closed or reopened. ping and every other event or action → 204 and nothing stored.
  • Storage: new columns on app_report: github_state (OPEN/CLOSED), github_state_reason (completed, not_planned, duplicate, reopened, or null), github_state_at (the issue's updated_at from the payload), plus an index on issue_number.
    • The row is found by issue_number among CREATED reports. An issue that was not created by the app → 204, nothing stored.
    • Out-of-order deliveries: an event is applied only when its updated_at is newer than the stored github_state_at.
  • List: a row with a stored state uses it, with no GitHub call. A row without one (created before D7, or no event yet) keeps the D4 read-through.
  • Missed deliveries: GitHub does not retry a failed delivery on its own. The stored state can then stay stale until the next event or a manual redeliver from the repo's webhook settings. Accepted.
  • Owner setup: repo Settings → Webhooks → payload URL above, content type application/json, secret, "Issues" events only; GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET in the VM's env file, then restart.

docs.title: Options considered for D7
docs.text: Option Pros Cons Verdict A. Repo webhook, HMAC-verified, state stored on app_report Push, no polling; state_reason comes with the event; one public endpoint A new unauthenticated endpoint (guarded by HMAC); a second secret; GitHub does not retry Chosen B. Scheduled job polls GitHub for open reports No public endpoint Uses API quota; state is late by up to the poll interval; another job Rejected C. Keep read-through only, add state_reason to the GET Smallest change Nothing stored; still one call per row on a cold cache Rejected: the owner wants the state stored

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• One click from seeing a problem to an autopilot run, and the issue carries its context.
  • Small footprint:
    • no new library, no new infrastructure, no workflow change;
    • one new client, one table, one controller.
  • Least-privilege credential: easy to rotate by replacing the env var.

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• The owner-only gate of ADR-0022 is wider. Any ADMIN can start paid runs, capped at 10 a day. An admin account compromise now reaches autopilot; prod is still reachable only through autopilot:auto, which is SUPER_ADMIN only.
  • The PAT lives on the server alongside other secrets. A server compromise leaks it, limited to creating and reading issues in one repo.
  • Status calls add latency to the list: up to one GitHub call per row on a cold cache.
  • D7 adds a public endpoint. Its only guard is the HMAC secret; a leaked secret lets anyone set report states (display only, no other effect). Rotate it in both GitHub and the env file.
  • The per-user limit is in memory. It resets on deploy, which is acceptable at one replica. Moving to Redis follows ADR-0003 if the app scales out.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• An integration test against a stubbed GitHub (local HttpServer, like HttpRedirectProbeTest) checks:
    • the labels for ADMIN, for SUPER_ADMIN with auto labels, and over the daily cap;
    • FAILED and retry;
    • the marker in the body.
  • Permission tests:
    • USER gets 403;
    • ADMIN sending an auto label gets 403;
    • SUPER_ADMIN gets 201.
  • A prod check by the owner: a report from the app creates issue N with autopilot, and the plan job starts.

docs.title: Links
docs.text:
• PRD: PRD-in-app-report
  • GitHub REST: create an issue, POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues
  • Patterns: client/HttpRedirectProbe.java, aop/RateLimitAspect.java, filter/WebSecurityConfig.java:81-88

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Date Change 2026-10-20 Proposed 2026-10-20 Accepted by the owner 2026-10-21 D7: issue state by HMAC-verified webhook, stored on app_report (owner request)

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-10-21) · Date: 2026-10-21 · Deciders: nguyenhuuca · Tags: agents, ci, workflow, quality Related: builds on ADR-0022 (headless runs) and ADR-0025 (auto gates, never for .claude/); input from scripts/agent-metrics.mjs (docs/reports/agent-metrics-2026-10.md)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• scripts/agent-metrics.mjs now measures the agent's work: escaped defects, reverts, review rounds, blocked runs, flaky tests, CI failures, cost.
  • Today a bad signal only turns into a better rule when the owner runs a retro by hand. The owner wants the agent to improve itself from the metrics, without being asked each time.
  • First real signal: 62526c97 fixed a defect from the dynamic-cron-jobs run. Existing job bodies caught and logged every exception, so the new scheduler recorded SUCCESS on failure. Plan review, code review and QA ×2 all passed it.
  • Risks of an agent that edits its own rules:
    • Goodhart: it can make the numbers look better (weaker tests, lower gates, a changed metrics script) instead of the work.
    • Drift: one bad rule makes every later run worse, and nobody notices.
    • Bloat: rules only grow, each run gets slower and more expensive.
    • Injection: issue, PR and commit text could be turned into rules.

docs.title: Decision Drivers
docs.text:
1. Every change to the agent's rules must come with evidence that it helps, checked by code the agent cannot change.
  2. The owner keeps control of the direction: one click per change, no reading of raw metrics needed.
  3. The loop must not be able to weaken any gate, metric or eval.
  4. Bounded cost per run.

docs.title: Considered Options
docs.text: Option Pros Cons A. Manual retro (today) No risk Depends on the owner remembering; signals are lost B. Evolve loop, proposals as PRs, owner merges Automatic diagnosis and proof; owner only merges One human step per change C. Evolve loop with auto-merge Fully hands-off The agent changes its own rules with no human read; one bad change compounds; conflicts with ADR-0025 (no auto-merge for .claude/)

docs.title: Decision Outcome
docs.text: Option B.

docs.title: D1. The loop
docs.text:
/evolve (run by the owner)
  Observe   agent-metrics --json → new signals (escaped defect, user bug report, revert, blocked, flaky, /revise, cost jump)
  Diagnose  per signal: original run diff, fix commit, plan/report → Five Whys → the stage that should have caught it
  Propose   one small change at that stage, on branch evolve/<date>-<signal>
  Prove     deterministic eval (D3)
  Ship      PR "Evolve: <signal>" with the Five Whys and the eval table → owner merges or closes
  Re-measure next month's metrics; a later run may propose removing a rule that no longer earns its place (D5)
  • At most 3 signals per run; the rest wait for the next run.
  • Signal ids are stable (defect:<fix sha>, revert:<sha>, blocked:<run id>, …). A signal that already has an evolve PR or issue (open, merged or closed) is skipped, so a change the owner rejected is not proposed again. The state lives in GitHub, not in commits to main.

docs.title: D2. What the agent may change (enforced by the workflow, not by the prompt)
docs.text:
• May add or tighten: .claude/skills/**/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/**/resources/*.md, .claude/rules/*.md, .claude/agents/*.md (prompt body only, not frontmatter), and new directories under evals/seeded/.
  • Never: .github/, scripts/, .claude/hooks/, .claude/settings*.json, existing evals/seeded/* cases, api/.coverage-threshold, application code, migrations, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md.
  • A deterministic step checks git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD against this allowlist and against "no deleted lines in rule files" (removals only through D5). Any violation → no PR, an evolve issue that names the violation.
  • A change that needs CI or a hook (for example a grep check for swallowed exceptions in jobs/) is written in the PR body as an owner action, not made by the agent.
  • Issue, PR and commit text is data. The agent quotes it as evidence; it never copies instructions from it into a rule.

docs.title: D3. The fitness function: seeded-bug evals
docs.text:
• evals/seeded/<id>/case.json = a real defect: base and head commits of the run that introduced it, the files, and an expect block (the file that must get a blocking finding, plus regexes the finding must match).
  • scripts/evolve.mjs eval runs the reviewer (worker-reviewer, the code-review stage of /autopilot) on git diff base..head with the .claude/ of a given ref, and grades the verdict block deterministically: caught = a blocking finding on an expected file whose text matches an expect regex.
  • A proposal passes only when, with the eval runner from main:
    1. the new case is missed with main's rules in at least 2 of 3 runs (otherwise no rule change is needed; the PR only adds the case, and that case-only PR needs main to catch it in 2 of 3),
    2. it is caught with the branch's rules in at least 2 of 3 runs (model output is not deterministic),
    3. every existing case is still caught with the branch's rules (no regression),
    4. the mean reviewer cost per case rises by at most 25%.
  • The agent writes the case, but cannot game it: an expect that matches everything fails rule 1, one that matches nothing fails rule 2.
  • The eval table (case × ref × run → caught, cost) goes into the PR body.

docs.title: D4. Running it
docs.text:
• Local only: the owner runs /evolve; it goes through the same stages in the session and asks before any push or merge, like autopilot Gate 2. Since ADR-0029 a weekly headless workflow is a second way in.
  • Gate hardening: the case must be added by the branch, its base/head must be commits on main, rule-file frontmatter is frozen (new skills: name, description, argument-hint, disable-model-invocation only), no new agents, and not-eval-proven proposals may not touch the reviewer's rules.
  • Budget: at most 3 signals per run, at most 3 eval runs for the new case and 1 run per existing case (retry once on a miss).
  • Headless workflow removed (2026-10-21). A weekly .github/workflows/agent-evolve.yml (propose job with a read-only token, ship job that checks and opens the PR) was built and then removed by the owner. Its first real run showed that headless Claude Code treats .claude/ files as sensitive and asks for permission on every edit, which CI cannot grant, so the agent could not write a single proposal; a packaging bug then closed the month's signal with a wrong "no proposal" issue (#50). Running it headless again needs a new decision (for example: the agent writes encoded file copies outside .claude/ and the ship job applies them).

docs.title: D5. Pruning
docs.text:
• Every rule line added by Evolve ends with <!-- evolve:<case id> -->.
  • Quarterly (or when total rule size grows by more than 20% since the last prune), a run may propose removing one such line. It passes only when its case is still caught without it (D3 rule 2) and nothing regresses. This is the only path that deletes rule lines.

docs.title: D6. Compress: removing text, not only adding it (amendment 2026-10-21)
docs.text:
Adding rules alone makes every session pay for more context (CLAUDE.md + always-loaded rules ≈ 37 KB, loaded by every session and worker). Evolve may also cut:

  • Signal: compress:<YYYY-MM>, at most one a month, after the defect signals. It carries lint hints from scripts/evolve.mjs lint-rules: exact duplicate lines across rule files, dead path references, the always-loaded size.
  • What may be cut: duplicated text (keep one home, point to it), dead references, text that contradicts its source of truth, stale claims.
  • Paths: the D2 paths plus CLAUDE.md, existing files only, removals allowed. Protected, never cut or edited: AGENTS.md, .claude/rules/security.md, the evolve skill, verdict.md, frontmatter, and any line carrying a safety rule (push, gates, merge, deny, secrets, tokens, prod, smoke, security, Core Principles, "never …"), matched by a fixed pattern in scripts/evolve.mjs.
  • Gate (gate --kind compress):
    • C1: the touched files shrink, and the always-loaded context drops ≥ 5% or the touched files lose ≥ 1 KiB;
    • C2: no new duplicate lines or dead references;
    • C3: every seeded case is still caught with the compressed rules (and there is at least one case).
  • Always a draft PR. With a small eval set the gate cannot prove that behavior outside it is unchanged, so the owner reads every removed line.
  • Rewriting a skill to work better (not just shorter) is a rule proposal: it needs a seeded case that the old text misses.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Good: every escaped defect becomes a regression eval for the agent, and each rule change has before/after evidence. The eval set grows with real bugs, never with invented ones.
  • Good: the owner's job shrinks to reading a short PR (Five Whys + eval table) and merging or closing it.
  • Cost: about one agent run (~$1–3) plus the evals (one Sonnet review per case run, ~$0.10–0.20) per /evolve run with signals; with no new signal it stops after the metrics step.
  • Limit: only stages a reviewer can be tested on are proven by D3. Changes to plan review or QA rules are proposed with the Five Whys only and marked "not eval-proven" in the PR.
  • Limit: keyword grading can miss a correct finding worded differently; the 2-of-3 rule and the owner's read cover that.
  • Risk: a merged rule could still hurt cases not in the eval set. The monthly metrics and D5 pruning are the backstop; rollback is git revert of the evolve PR.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• First case evals/seeded/2026-10-19-swallowed-job-exceptions (from 62526c97): missed with today's rules, caught after the Evolve change, in 2 of 3 runs.
  • The allowlist step rejects a test branch that edits scripts/agent-metrics.mjs.
  • After two months: escaped defect rate does not rise while the number of runs grows, and total rule size stays within the D5 bound.

docs.title: Links
docs.text:
• ADR-0022 Headless autopilot · ADR-0025 Auto gates
  • scripts/agent-metrics.mjs, docs/reports/agent-metrics-2026-10.md

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
• 2026-10-21: Proposed; accepted by the owner the same day. The eval runner lives in scripts/evolve.mjs (subcommands signals, check-paths, eval, gate).
  • 2026-10-21: D6 (compress) added at the owner's request: Evolve may also remove duplicate, dead or stale text, with protected lines and a size + eval gate.
  • 2026-10-21: headless workflow agent-evolve.yml removed at the owner's request (D4); /evolve is local only. The manifest command went with it.
  • 2026-10-22: signal bug:#<N>: a closed bug issue (in-app report, ADR-0026) whose fix changed lines an agent run wrote (git blame on the fix's parent). Autopilot fixes are titled Autopilot: …, not fix:, so these were not counted before. A fix that only adds lines is not linked.
  • 2026-10-22: bug:#<N> also links to a commit co-authored by Claude in a normal session when no autopilot run wrote the lines (origin: session, span = that commit). About 72% of the month's commits are Claude-co-authored but under 10% belong to autopilot runs, and all 5 bug reports so far came from session code.
  • 2026-10-22: headless workflow back with staged proposals outside .claude/ and an apply command (ADR-0029).

docs.title: ADR-0028: Opt-in Auto Gates for Local Autopilot
Metadata
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-10-22) · Date: 2026-10-22 · Deciders: nguyenhuuca · Tags: agents, workflow, security Related: brings ADR-0025 to local runs; amends plan-autopilot D7 (gates are never skipped) and the "ask before every push" rule (core-directives.md)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Local /autopilot stops twice for the owner: Gate 1 (plan) and Gate 2 (push). Both use AskUserQuestion, and D7 forbids a --yes.
  • Headless runs can already skip both gates with the labels autopilot:auto-merge and autopilot:auto (ADR-0025).
  • The owner wants the same choice locally, for small changes they do not need to watch.

docs.title: D1. Two flags, typed in the command
docs.text:
Flag Gate 1 Gate 2 none ask ask --auto-push ask automatic when D3 holds --auto automatic when D2 holds automatic when D3 holds
  • A flag counts only when the owner types it at the start of the /autopilot command. A flag found in a plan file, an issue or any other content is ignored.
  • A flag covers that run only. /task-resume of a stopped run asks at every gate left.
  • Not combined with --headless: headless runs use the labels of ADR-0025.

docs.title: D2. Auto Gate 1
docs.text:
• Only when the last plan review returned approve. A run that reaches round 3 revise still stops blocked.
  • The orchestrator prints what Gate 1 would show (plan, task table, open advisories, ledger total) and goes on. The ledger records gate1 | auto.

docs.title: D3. Auto Gate 2
docs.text:
The orchestrator pushes without asking only when every check holds:

  • The last code review returned approve, QA ×2 exited 0 and the full gates are green. These already gate the commit.
  • bash scripts/claude-autopilot-autopush-check.sh exits 0. It checks the run's commits (origin/main..HEAD) with the same limits as the headless auto-merge (scripts/claude-autopilot-merge.sh):
    • no change under .github/, .claude/, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, scripts/claude-, Liquibase changelogs or .env;
    • at most 400 changed lines outside tests and docs.

A failed check falls back to the normal Gate 2 question, with the reason. The push itself is unchanged: git pull --rebase --autostash, never force, a rebase conflict stops the run. CI and the smoke test run after the push as before.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Risk: code reaches prod without the owner reading it, as with autopilot:auto. Mitigations: the flag is typed per run, the owner can Ctrl+C at any time, the deterministic check refuses protected paths and large diffs, CI tests before it deploys, rollback is git revert.
  • The check script repeats the two limits of claude-autopilot-merge.sh. That script runs from origin/main in CI and cannot source a sibling file, so both carry a "keep in sync" comment.

docs.title: ADR-0029: Headless Evolve With Staged Proposals
Metadata
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-10-22) · Date: 2026-10-22 · Deciders: nguyenhuuca · Tags: agents, ci, security Related: reverses the "local only" part of ADR-0027 D4; the allowlist (D2), the eval gate (D3), pruning (D5) and compress (D6) stay as they are

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• The first weekly agent-evolve.yml (2026-10-21) wrote nothing. Headless Claude Code treats .claude/ files as sensitive and asks permission on every edit, and CI cannot answer.
  • The same run hit Refusing to create empty bundle while packaging, then still filed a "no proposal" issue for compress:2026-10 (#50, closed by the owner).
  • The owner wants the loop back in CI on a weekly schedule, with the same checks as a local run.

docs.title: D1. The agent stages file copies; it never touches .claude/ or git
docs.text:
In --headless mode the agent writes the full new content of every file it would change under evolve-out/<slug>/tree/:

Repo path Staged path .claude/agents/worker-reviewer.md evolve-out/<slug>/tree/dot-claude/agents/worker-reviewer.md.staged CLAUDE.md evolve-out/<slug>/tree/CLAUDE.md.staged evals/seeded/<id>/case.json evolve-out/<slug>/tree/evals/seeded/<id>/case.json.staged
  • No staged path has a .claude segment or a file name Claude Code treats specially, so Write needs no permission.
  • A file cannot be deleted this way. Rule files are never deleted (ADR-0027 D2), and compress removes lines inside files.
  • The agent holds a read-only token, as before. Its tools: Read, Glob, Grep, read-only git diff/show/log/rev-parse/ls-files, and Write/Edit scoped to evolve-out/**. It cannot write .git/ or .gitattributes (a planted git helper would run under the allowed git commands), cannot read /proc or /sys, has no shell readers (cat, grep, head, tail) and no web tools. Git runs with GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null.

docs.title: D2. A manifest row for every signal
docs.text:
evolve-out/manifest.json is an array with one row per signal:

  • a proposal: {signal, slug, case, kind, body, message}, where kind is rule, case-only, not-eval-proven or compress;
  • no proposal: {signal, kind: "none", body}, where body explains why.

The ship job files a "no proposal" issue, which closes the signal, only for a none row. A signal with no row, or a row without a tree/ (agent crash, turn limit, broken artifact), is left for next week's run. A row whose staged files are invalid becomes a "rejected (staging)" issue and closes the signal.

docs.title: D3. The ship job builds the branch; the agent's files are data
docs.text:
node scripts/evolve.mjs apply --dir <proposal>/evolve-out/<slug> --base <main sha> --branch evolve/<slug> --message <file>:

  • accepts only regular files ≤ 64 KiB whose decoded path matches the Evolve allowlist or a new case path (ADR-0027 D2), and rejects .., symlinks and an empty tree;
  • writes the commit with git plumbing (temporary index, commit-tree, update-ref), so the ship job's working tree, and the evolve.mjs it runs, stay on main.

Then check-paths and gate run unchanged. A pass becomes a PR labelled evolve (draft for compress and not-eval-proven). A fail becomes an issue. Nothing is merged: the owner merges.

docs.title: D4. Schedule and cost
docs.text:
• The workflow runs every Monday at 09:00 Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, or on workflow_dispatch (owner only, optional since).
  • It handles at most 3 signals per run (ADR-0027 D4 budget). The agent step costs about $1–5 a week (approximate). Weeks with no new signal cost $0, because the agent does not start.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The local /evolve flow is unchanged. Headless is a second way in, with the same gate.
  • The ship job still pushes evolve/* branches with a write token. The PR is the owner's Gate 2.
  • Everything published (issue and PR bodies, gate tables) passes a token-shape redaction (sk-ant-, gh?_, github_pat_, JWT) first.
  • PRs opened with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger other workflows, and the repo setting "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" must be on (it was for the 2026-10-21 version).
  • Not yet proven: that headless Write to evolve-out/ raises no permission prompt. The first workflow_dispatch run checks it; if it fails, disable the workflow again.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: • 2026-10-22: accepted.

docs.title: ADR-0030: Granted Autopilot Labels for Contributors and Admins
Metadata
docs.text:
Status: Accepted (2026-10-23) · Date: 2026-10-23 · Deciders: nguyenhuuca · Tags: api, security, agents Related PRD: PRD-contributor-autopilot-permissions · Amends: ADR-0026 (auto labels SUPER_ADMIN only, D6 future CONTRIBUTOR) · Supersedes: N/A · Superseded By: N/A

Tech Strategy: ✅ Follows Golden Path (Spring Security roles, bitwise permissions of ADR-0015, Liquibase)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Today only the owner can skip the gates from a report. autopilot:auto and autopilot:auto-merge are accepted from SUPER_ADMIN only (ReportServiceImpl.java:103,163; ADR-0026 "Auto labels"). Every other report needs the owner at Gate 1 and Gate 2. The owner is the bottleneck (PRD Problem Statement).
  • There is no report-only role. To send a report, a person must be ADMIN, which opens every admin tab (WebSecurityConfig.java:54: /admin/** → hasAnyRole("ADMIN","SUPER_ADMIN")). ADR-0026 D6 planned a CONTRIBUTOR role but kept auto labels SUPER_ADMIN-only.
  • The issue identity is always the owner's. The server creates issues with the owner's PAT (ADR-0026 D1), so the workflow cannot tell who asked for a label. Whatever the server puts on the issue, the headless workflow trusts (ADR-0025). The server is the only place this rule can be enforced.
  • Permission bits today:
    • five bits, ALL_BITS = 0b11111 (Permission.java:15);
    • every admin gets all of them by default (UserRole.defaultPermissions(), UserRole.java:19-20);
    • a 2026-10-18 migration backfilled admins to 31 (202610180003-admin-default-permissions.sql);
    • a role change overwrites the whole mask (AdminAccountServiceImpl.java:53).
  • @HasPermission checks are flag-gated. They run only while the Harness flag permission_enforcement_enabled is on (PermissionServiceImpl.java:71). It has been on in prod since 2026-10-23, but it can be turned off without a deploy.
  • The JWT carries a copy of the permission mask (JwtProvider.java:116). It is stale until the next login.

docs.title: Decision Drivers
docs.text:
1. Remove owner clicks for people the owner trusts, chosen per account (PRD goal ≥ 50%).
  2. No silent privilege: nobody gets the power to skip gates by default, by a role change or by a migration.
  3. Instant revoke: a revoke must stop the next report, without waiting for a re-login.
  4. Not switchable by a feature flag: turning off the Harness flag must not open the auto labels to everyone.
  5. Least privilege for contributors: report endpoints only; no other admin tab.
  6. Small change: keep /admin/reports, keep the workflow, keep ADR-0025's checks.

docs.title: Option 1: Keep auto labels SUPER_ADMIN-only (status quo, ADR-0026)
docs.text: Pros Cons Smallest trust surface; the owner sees every run before prod Owner stays the bottleneck: 2 actions per report No code change Fails driver 1

docs.title: Option 2: Auto labels by role (e.g. every ADMIN may use them)
docs.text: Pros Cons Simple check: role >= ADMIN All-or-nothing: every admin, present and future, can ship to prod with no review No new bits Fails driver 2; cannot grant a contributor without making them ADMIN

docs.title: Option 3: Per-account permission bits granted by the SUPER_ADMIN, checked in the service (chosen)
docs.text:
Two new bits, AUTOPILOT_AUTO_MERGE and AUTOPILOT_AUTO, outside the role default mask. Only the SUPER_ADMIN can set them on a CONTRIBUTOR or ADMIN account. The report service checks them against the user row on every create and retry.

Pros Cons Per-person trust, off by default (drivers 1, 2) Two more bits and a second mask to keep apart from ALL_BITS DB read at request time, so a revoke is effective at once (driver 3) A granted account (or its stolen session) can ship to prod through autopilot:auto A plain service check, independent of the Harness flag (driver 4) A role change must preserve or clear the bits on purpose (D4)

docs.title: Option 4: Per-account bits, checked with @HasPermission
docs.text: Pros Cons Reuses the existing annotation Skipped while permission_enforcement_enabled is off: everyone could use the auto labels (fails driver 4) Reads the JWT copy of the mask, so a revoke waits for re-login (fails driver 3)

docs.title: Decision Outcome
docs.text:
Chosen Option: Option 3, per-account bits granted by the SUPER_ADMIN and checked in the service.

Rationale: it is the only option that meets drivers 1–4 together. Options 1 and 2 are the two extremes, and Option 4 fails on the flag and the stale JWT. The accepted trade-off: a non-owner can start an auto run that reaches prod. ADR-0026's comment "prod is still reachable only through autopilot:auto, which is SUPER_ADMIN only" no longer holds. Prod is now reachable by the owner and by the accounts the owner names.

docs.title: D1. Role CONTRIBUTOR
docs.text:
• Inserted in UserRole between USER and ADMIN (ADR-0026 D6).
  • roleHierarchy() then gives ADMIN > CONTRIBUTOR > USER. Roles are stored as strings and ranked by outranks, so the shift in ordinal() is safe.
  • The SUPER_ADMIN and ADMINs may assign and remove it, by the existing rank rule (AdminAccountServiceImpl.java:46,105).
  • defaultPermissions() for CONTRIBUTOR is 0. A contributor needs no base bit to report.

docs.title: D2. Endpoints stay at /v1/funny-app/admin/reports
docs.text:
• Owner decision: no path change, no frontend URL change.
  • In WebSecurityConfig, a matcher for /v1/funny-app/admin/reports/** with hasAnyRole("CONTRIBUTOR","ADMIN","SUPER_ADMIN") is placed before the general /admin/** rule.
  • AdminReportController moves from hasRole('ADMIN') to hasRole('CONTRIBUTOR').
  • Every other admin controller is unchanged. A test asserts that a CONTRIBUTOR gets 403 on each of them.

docs.title: D3. Two permission bits, outside the role default
docs.text:
• AUTOPILOT_AUTO_MERGE = 1 << 5 and AUTOPILOT_AUTO = 1 << 6.
  • ALL_BITS stays 0b11111 and keeps its meaning: the bits an admin gets by default. A new AUTOPILOT_BITS mask holds the two new bits. The valid-mask check in updatePermissions accepts ALL_BITS | AUTOPILOT_BITS.
  • No migration grants them. The 2026-10-18 backfill pattern is not repeated.
  • Who may change them: only the SUPER_ADMIN. An ADMIN's updatePermissions call that would change either bit is refused with 403. An ADMIN may still edit the other five bits as today.
  • What they allow:
    • AUTO_MERGE label: needs AUTOPILOT_AUTO_MERGE or AUTOPILOT_AUTO;
    • AUTO label: needs AUTOPILOT_AUTO;
    • SUPER_ADMIN: every label, as today.

docs.title: D4. Role changes keep or clear the bits on purpose
docs.text:
updateRole sets the new role's default bits, then:

  • keeps the target account's existing autopilot bits when the new role is CONTRIBUTOR or ADMIN;
  • clears them when the new role is USER.

Keeping them means an ADMIN cannot silently wipe a grant the SUPER_ADMIN made. Clearing them means a dormant grant cannot come back on a later promotion (owner decision, 2026-10-23).

docs.title: D5. The check is in ReportServiceImpl, against the DB
docs.text:
• create and retry already load the caller from the DB (currentUser()). The label check reads permissions from that row. It does not use the JWT claim or @HasPermission.
  • The existing pattern is kept: the label stored on the row is applied only when the current caller may use it (callGitHub, ReportServiceImpl.java:163). A retry by someone else, or after a revoke, drops the auto label.
  • A label the caller may not use → 403 error.report.autoLabelForbidden (same code as today).

docs.title: D6. One shared daily cap
docs.text:
• The 10 per rolling 24 h cap now counts every non-SA report that carries autopilot: ADMIN and CONTRIBUTOR together (owner decision).
  • The count query and the partial index idx_app_report_autopilot_cap change from reporter_role = 'ADMIN' to reporter_role IN ('ADMIN','CONTRIBUTOR'). The index change is a new Liquibase changeset.
  • Over the cap, the issue is created without autopilot and without an auto label (unchanged).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive:

  • Trusted reporters ship small fixes without the owner, so up to 2 owner actions are saved per report.
  • Contributors get the Report menu without any other admin power.
  • A revoke is effective on the next request, and turning off the Harness flag does not open the labels.

Negative:

  • The owner-only reach to prod (ADR-0026 "Consequences") is widened to the accounts the owner grants.
  • Two kinds of permission bits now exist (role-default and granted). Code that builds or validates masks must use the right one.
  • The cap is shared: a busy contributor can use up the daily runs of the admins.

Risks:

  • A granted account or stolen session ships bad code to prod. Mitigations: grants are per account and off by default; headless runs keep plan review, code review, QA ×2 and the auto-merge check (protected paths, ≤ 400 changed lines, ADR-0025); shared cap of 10; instant revoke; rollback is git revert.
  • The new bits leak into a default. Mitigation: tests on defaultPermissions(), on role change (D4) and on updatePermissions by an ADMIN (D3).
  • A CONTRIBUTOR reaches another admin endpoint through matcher order. Mitigation: a test sweeps every admin controller with a CONTRIBUTOR token.
  • The cap-index changeset touches a Liquibase changelog, which the headless auto-merge refuses (ADR-0025 protected paths). So this feature itself must land through a normal, owner-merged run.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• [ ] Security review of the trust change (/security-auditor or swarm-review with focus security)
  • [ ] Tests: CONTRIBUTOR gets 403 on every non-report admin endpoint; ADMIN cannot change the autopilot bits; a role change keeps or clears them per D4; a revoke takes effect with an old JWT; the cap counts ADMIN and CONTRIBUTOR
  • [ ] Tech Strategy alignment confirmed (no new library; Liquibase for the index)
  • [ ] Related plan document created: docs/plans/plan-contributor-autopilot-permissions.md
  • [ ] Prod check by the owner: grant AUTOPILOT_AUTO_MERGE to a contributor, send a report with "Auto-merge", and see the issue get autopilot:auto-merge
