docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Status: Built 2026-10-19 (autopilot) · 985ba5b5 BE + e7b53b4f FE Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-19 ADR: ADR-0023. The ADR is needed because this adds a new API pattern and a new table (D1–D6 live there; this plan does not repeat them). Size: Small (1–2 days). There is no PRD, because there is a single admin-only capability with no user-facing product decision.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Move the six job schedules in AppScheduler from hardcoded @Scheduled annotations (AppScheduler.java:69, 79, 91, 107, 117, 127) to the scheduled_job table. An admin can then list jobs, and a SUPER_ADMIN can change cron, zone and on/off, or run a job now, from a new Admin tab, all without a deploy.

docs.title: Facts the tasks rely on
docs.text:
• Jobs and current schedules (AppScheduler.java):

    Job Line Schedule Zone scheduleMakePoem :69 0 45 10 * * * VN logStats :79 fixedRate 5 min — syncDriveVideos :91 0 */15 * * * * — notificationDigest :107 0 */15 * * * * — notificationRetention :117 0 30 3 * * * VN cleanUpOldVideos :127 0 0 3 30 2 * —

    cleanUpOldVideos never fires, and its body is a no-op (:130-132). The wrong log is at :71 and the wrong comment at :91.

  • Existing test: AppSchedulerTest.java asserts the @Scheduled cron of the notification jobs (:326-334). These assertions move to the migration/registry tests, because the annotations are removed.

  • Scheduling setup: @EnableScheduling is at FunnyApp.java:17. There is no custom TaskScheduler bean, and virtual threads are on (application.yaml:46).
  • Liquibase:
    • db.changelog-master.yaml:1-4 uses includeAll sql/, ordered by filename, so no master edit is needed.
    • Migrations are plain SQL.
    • Table + seed example: sql/202605010001-init_permissions.sql:4-24.
    • Latest file: sql/202610190001-suggestion-rereview-count.sql.
  • Entity style:
    • entity/VideoSuggestion.java:23-29 uses Lombok @Getter @Setter @NoArgsConstructor.
    • @UpdateTimestamp Instant is used in entity/BaseDomain.java:20-26.
  • Admin controller pattern:
    • web/AdminDriveSyncController.java:30-56: class-level hasRole('ADMIN'); reads use @HasPermission(perm = Permission.ADMIN).
    • Mutations use @PreAuthorize("hasRole('SUPER_ADMIN') and @permissionServiceImpl.hasPermission(authentication.details.permissions, ADMIN)") + @AuditLog + @RateLimited (:53-57).
    • Errors use CustomException.of(HttpStatus, subCode, key) (:47), with keys in i18n/messages.properties and messages_vi.properties.
  • Security config: the /v1/funny-app/admin/** role guard is at WebSecurityConfig.java:54. PATCH is already in CORS (:139), so no change is needed.
  • Error mapping: in RestExceptionHandler.java, CustomException maps to its own status (:225-235).
  • Test style:
    • Plain Mockito: web/AdminControllerTest.java:42-46.

  • Webapp:

docs.title: Plan: HLS Streaming for Selected Videos
Overview
docs.text: Status: Ready Date: 2026-10-24 PRD: PRD-hls-streaming ADR: ADR-0031 Spec: spec-hls-streaming (rules are cited as BR-n / FR-n / EC-n) Sequence: sequence-hls-streaming (flows 1–6) Size: Medium. 7 tasks: 5 backend, 2 frontend, about 2,000 LOC including tests.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
• The SUPER_ADMIN turns HLS on per Drive video.
  • A single-job worker stream-copies the video into video-cache/hls/{fileId}/.
  • The API offers hlsUrl only when the Harness flag hls_streaming_enabled is on and the rendition is READY.
  • The player uses HLS and falls back to Range.

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• Backend:
    • one Liquibase changeset, entity + enum, repository queries, app.hls.* config;
    • an ffprobe/ffmpeg client and HLS storage helper;
    • the worker;
    • admin toggle endpoints and admin DTO;
    • the downloader hook and delete cleanup;
    • public playlist and segment endpoints;
    • hlsUrl in the DTO.
  • Frontend: hls.js, the useHlsSource hook with fallback, the swiper preload rule, and the admin HLS column.
  • Tests for every BR, EC and acceptance criterion in the spec that can be automated.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Everything out of scope in the PRD:
    • auto-transcode at ingest, backfill;
    • re-encode, ABR, DRM;
    • per-user flag targeting;
    • FFmpeg in the Docker image.
  • Any change to the Range endpoint, VideoCache or the download flow beyond the BR-10 hook.

docs.title: Architecture Changes
docs.text:
See the spec's API, Database and Frontend sections and the sequence diagrams.

New Package Notes HlsStatus enum enums/ Next to VideoStatus HlsErrorCode enum enums/ BR-9 codes, stored as their name in hls_error HlsStorage service/impl/ (@Component) Paths, id/segment validation, tmp → publish rename, delete, usable space, directory listing for the sweep FfmpegHlsClient client/ ffprobe + ffmpeg through the existing ProcessFactory (client/ProcessFactory.java:8-9), timeout watchdog, kill HlsTranscodeWorker service/impl/ Copies the VideoImportWorker pattern HlsPlaybackService (+ impl) service/ BR-13 lookup for the playlist endpoint, flag read for DTOs

docs.title: Key Decisions
docs.text:
All recorded in ADR-0031 (D1–D8) and the spec's Open Questions (owner decisions of 2026-10-24).

Explorer findings that shape the tasks:

  • Atomic claim to copy. VideoImportJobRepository.claimNextDue() (:37-50) is a single native statement: UPDATE … WHERE id = (SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1) RETURNING id. It returns Optional<Long>. Startup reset is resetInterrupted() (:62-75). The HLS claim must also set updated_at = now(): native updates do not fire @UpdateTimestamp (BaseDomain.java:26), and incrementViewCount (VideoSourceRepository.java:41-45) does not touch it.
  • Process handling.
    • Only the start step is shared: ProcessFactory / DefaultProcessFactory (env allowlist, stdin from the null device).
    • The timeout watchdog and kill live privately in YtDlpClientImpl (:220-289).
    • FfmpegHlsClient takes ProcessFactory and has its own small run/kill. We do not refactor YtDlpClientImpl (Two Hats rule).
    • Tests use FakeProcess.finished(...) / hanging(...) (test client/FakeProcess.java:29-35).
    • FfmpegServiceImpl (thumbnails) calls ProcessBuilder directly and stays as it is.
  • Locks.
    • DriveVideoDownloaderImpl does not claim DriveFileLocks. Its callers do: VideoStorageServiceImpl.java:141/151 and DriveSyncServiceImpl.java:193/209. So the BR-10 hook after moveIntoPlace (DriveVideoDownloaderImpl.java:70) already runs under the lock.
    • DriveFileLocks is non-blocking and non-reentrant: tryClaim / release / isHeld (cache/DriveFileLocks.java:18-28).
  • Not-found errors.
    • AdminVideoServiceImpl throws IllegalArgumentException, which maps to 400 (:86-87).
    • The spec asks for 404, so the new HLS methods use CustomException.of(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, 404, "error.video.notFound"). That key already exists (VideoReactionServiceImpl.java:60).
    • Existing methods are not changed.
  • Security.
    • AdminController has class-level @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") (:51). The new methods add the method-level SUPER_ADMIN expression from AdminDriveSyncController.java:55; the method level wins.
    • /video-stream/** is in ALLOW_ALL_METHOD (AppConstant.java:72-84), so the public HLS paths need no security change.
    • CORS already allows PUT and DELETE (WebSecurityConfig.java:141).
  • DTO callers.
    • Converter.toVideoDto is called from StreamVideoServiceImpl.java:113 (via toDto, used at :89, :97 and by the list) and VideoCollectionServiceImpl.java:190 (method ref).
    • Both must pass the per-request flag value.
    • ShareServiceImpl / YouTubeVideoServiceImpl build YouTube DTOs and are not touched.
  • Frontend.
    • VideoPlayer.jsx has no onError handler (:189-206). A failed source spins forever today, so the fallback adds the first error path.
    • The only other <video> is the hidden preload in VideoSwiper.jsx:222-236.
    • There is no dynamic import() in src yet. hls.js will be the first split chunk; Vite does this without config.
    • AdminVideoTable.jsx has no role check yet. Use useAuth().user.role + isSuperAdmin (utils/roles.js:5), as DriveSyncPanel.jsx:90 does.
    • Tests use the real i18n (src/test-setup.js). VideoSwiper.actions.test.jsx:7 mocks VideoPlayer.
  • hls.js version: pin 1.7.3 (published 2026-09-11), exact version, no caret.
  • BeanConstructorTest (BeanConstructorTest.java:22-40): HlsTranscodeWorker and FfmpegHlsClient will have a test constructor, so the public one needs @Autowired.

docs.text:

Owner, after deploy, with the flag still OFF:

  1. In the admin table, turn HLS on for one H.264 video. It should reach READY in under 30 s. Open …/video-stream/hls/{fileId}/playlist.m3u8 in Safari: it plays.

docs.title: Problem Summary
docs.text:
Videos are shown in a flat list with no trending signal. Five gaps must be closed:

# Gap Severity 1 recordAccess() is commented out — no access data is written High 2 No hot score computation logic High 3 No API endpoint for trending videos High 4 No cache pre-warming for hot videos Medium 5 Frontend has no hot badge or trending section Medium

docs.title: Architecture Summary
docs.text:
Stream request
    → VideoAccessServiceImpl.recordAccess()  [async, fire-and-forget]
        → upsert VideoAccessStats

AppScheduler.recomputeHotScores()  [every 30 min]
    → HotVideoServiceImpl.computeScores()
        → query VideoAccessStats + ShareLink (last 24h)
        → normalize + apply weighted formula
        → update video_sources (hot_score, is_hot, hot_rank)
        → refresh StatsCacheImpl
        → pre-warm VideoCacheImpl for top 10

GET /api/videos/trending
    → VideoController.getTrending()
        → HotVideoService.getTopN()
            → StatsCacheImpl (TTL 30 min)

GET /api/videos?sort=hot
    → VideoController.getVideos()
        → VideoService.getVideosToStream(sort=hot)
            → query ORDER BY hot_score DESC

Core scoring logic: 

double hotScore(double hits, double shares, double hoursAgo, HotVideoProperties cfg) {
    double recency = Math.exp(-cfg.getDecayLambda() * hoursAgo);
    return cfg.getWeightHits()    * hits
         + cfg.getWeightShares()  * shares
         + cfg.getWeightRecency() * recency;
}

Min-max normalization applied to all videos before computing weighted sum.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Status: Done (QA-1 verified on prod by owner; recorded 2026-10-18). Approved 2026-10-14. Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-14 Related PRD: PRD-i18n Related ADR: ADR-0020

Owner decisions (2026-10-14):

  • Use react-i18next.
  • Default language comes from the browser.
  • Scope covers user UI, API errors, emails and Admin.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Every user-facing string on the frontend and backend comes from per-language resources (vi, en), with one switcher, a persisted preference, and localized errors and emails.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
webapp/src/i18n/
  index.js                     # i18next init: resources, detector (localStorage 'lang' → navigator), supportedLngs [vi,en], fallback en
  format.js                    # relativeTime(date), compactNumber(n), formatDate(d): Intl.* with i18n.language
  locales/vi/*.json            # common, feed, library, auth, comments, notifications, settings, admin, errors
  locales/en/*.json
  __tests__/parity.test.js     # identical key sets per namespace, no empty values
components/common/LanguageSwitcher.jsx   # "VI | EN", aria-pressed; in header + Settings
  • main.jsx imports ./i18n before rendering.
  • A languageChanged handler does three things:
    • Sets document.documentElement.lang.
    • Writes localStorage.lang.
    • When logged in, PATCHes /user/settings { locale }.
  • api/client.js adds Accept-Language: i18n.language to every request.
  • After login (AuthContext), if settings.locale is set and differs from the current language, the app calls i18n.changeLanguage(settings.locale).
  • Components call const { t } = useTranslation('<ns>'). Interpolation uses t('library.removeFrom', { title }), and plurals use t('library.videoCount', { count }).

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Turn the Library tab (today a ComingSoon placeholder) into:

  1. My collections: a logged-in user creates private, named collections and adds videos to them from the feed.
  2. Public collections: ADMIN / SUPER_ADMIN curate collections that everyone can view, including guests.

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• One migration: video_collections + video_collection_items
  • BE:
    • entities and repos

    • optional-auth public reads
  • FE:
    • api/collections.js

docs.title: Key Decisions
docs.text: Decision Choice Why Data model Collection items reference video_sources directly. There is no bookmarks table. One concept instead of two. A "bookmark" is an item in "Xem sau". Visibility visibility is PRIVATE or PUBLIC. Only users with the ADMIN permission bit (ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN) can create a PUBLIC collection or set one to PUBLIC. A normal user who tries gets 403. Covers the curated-content need without a separate table. Who manages a public collection Any ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN can rename it, add or remove items, change its visibility, or delete it. All of these are audit-logged. It is editorial content. It must not be orphaned when its creator loses the admin role. Private collection access Owner only. Admins cannot see them. A foreign or private id returns 404, not 403. Privacy, and no id enumeration. Default collection is_default = true is always PRIVATE (CHECK constraint). It cannot be renamed, made public or deleted. A predictable "save for later". Video delete ON DELETE CASCADE on video_id Admin delete is a hard deleteById. Hidden or unpublished video The row stays in the DB but is excluded from item lists for everyone. unavailableCount is returned only to people who can manage the collection (owner, or an admin for a public one). For everyone else it is null. Unhiding the video brings it back. Viewers learn nothing about hidden videos. Public reads GET /collections/public and GET /collections/{id}/videos are added to OPTIONAL_AUTH_PATH, with the same pattern as /videos/*/reaction. Guests can browse. A bad token is treated as a guest. Card state (is the video saved?) GET /collections/membership?videoId=X when the modal opens. There is no global ids preload. The feed cache is untouched. Caps 50 collections per user, 500 items per collection, name 1–60 chars. Names are unique per owner and case-insensitive. Public names are unique globally. Bounded payloads. No two public collections with the same name. Service style Interface in service/, impl in service/impl/ Matches VideoReactionService and AdminCommentService

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
api/src/main/resources/db/changelog/sql/202610130001-create-video-collections.sql

CREATE TABLE video_collections (
    id          UUID         PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id     BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,  -- owner / creator
    name        VARCHAR(60)  NOT NULL,
    visibility  VARCHAR(10)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PRIVATE' CHECK (visibility IN ('PRIVATE', 'PUBLIC')),
    is_default  BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT false,   -- "Xem sau"
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT ck_video_collections_default_private CHECK (NOT is_default OR visibility = 'PRIVATE')
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_video_collections_user_name    ON video_collections(user_id, lower(name));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_video_collections_public_name  ON video_collections(lower(name)) WHERE visibility = 'PUBLIC';
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_video_collections_user_default ON video_collections(user_id) WHERE is_default;
CREATE INDEX idx_video_collections_public ON video_collections(updated_at DESC) WHERE visibility = 'PUBLIC';

CREATE TABLE video_collection_items (
    collection_id UUID        NOT NULL REFERENCES video_collections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    video_id      BIGINT      NOT NULL REFERENCES video_sources(id)     ON DELETE CASCADE,
    added_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (collection_id, video_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_video_collection_items_video ON video_collection_items(video_id);

There is one known edge case: ON DELETE CASCADE on user_id deletes a public collection when its creator account is deleted. The plan accepts this, and the delete-account copy does not mention it. Revisit if editorial loss becomes a problem.

The master changelog uses includeAll: sql/, so no master edit is needed.

docs.title: API (/v1/funny-app/collections)
docs.text:
Method Path Auth Body / Query Returns GET /collections JWT — ResultListInfo<CollectionDto>: my collections. Creates "Xem sau" if it is missing. Admins also get the public collections, flagged canManage. GET /collections/public optional — ResultListInfo<CollectionDto>: public collections with itemCount > 0 (admins also see empty ones) POST /collections JWT {name, visibility?} CollectionDto (201). 403 if a non-admin asks for PUBLIC. 409 for a duplicate name or the cap. PATCH /collections/{id} JWT {name?, visibility?} CollectionDto. 400 on the default collection. 403 if a non-admin sets PUBLIC. DELETE /collections/{id} JWT — 204. 400 on the default collection. GET /collections/{id}/videos optional page,size A page of visible VideoDto. Works for a public collection, or for a private one if you are its owner. Otherwise 404. PUT /collections/{id}/videos/{videoId} JWT — 204, idempotent. 404 if the video is not visible or you cannot manage the collection. DELETE /collections/{id}/videos/{videoId} JWT — 204, idempotent GET /collections/membership JWT videoId ResultListInfo<UUID>: ids of the manageable collections that contain the video

CollectionDto has these fields:

  • id, name, visibility, isDefault
  • ownerName: display name only, never the email
  • itemCount, unavailableCount (null unless canManage)
  • coverVideoId, canManage, updatedAt

Endpoint rules:

  • Writes carry @RateLimited(permit = 30). The two public GETs carry @RateLimited(permit = 60).
  • @AuditLog is applied to create, rename, delete and visibility change, and to any write on a PUBLIC collection.
  • The admin check reads the caller's role from the DB (ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN), the same way AdminAccountServiceImpl.actorRole does. A token issued before a demotion therefore cannot manage public collections.
  • PATCH, PUT and DELETE are already in WebSecurityConfig.setAllowedMethods. Verify only.

FE-1 api/collections.js and hooks/useCollections.js 0.5d BE-3 contract Hook tests: mine and public lists, create, toggle an item, with invalidation FE-2 AddToCollectionModal and the "Lưu" button in VideoSwiper 1d FE-1 A checkbox toggle adds or removes the video. Inline create adds the video to the new collection. A guest sees the login hint. An admin sees public collections with a badge. Buttons show aria-busy. FE-3 LibraryView (public section, my section, detail, create/rename/delete, ?l= deep link) 1.5d FE-1 A guest sees public collections and can play them. "Xem sau" is pinned first and cannot be deleted. The "Công khai" toggle shows only for admins. Delete uses useConfirm. A ?l= link opens the collection for a guest. QA-1 Local E2E and prod smoke 0.5d BE-3, FE-2, FE-3 Admin creates a public collection and adds videos. A guest opens the ?l= link and sees them. Hiding a video in admin removes it for the guest, and the admin sees the unavailable count. A user creates a private one, and another user's GET returns 404. Deleting a video removes its item.

docs.text: Risk Mitigation The default collection is created twice in a race The partial unique index uq_video_collections_user_default blocks it. Catch DataIntegrityViolationException and re-read. A demoted admin keeps managing public collections Resolved: the role is read from the DB on every request, not from the JWT. Public endpoints get scraped or hammered @RateLimited, paginated videos (max size 50), no emails in the DTO N+1 when listing collections with counts and cover One aggregate query: GROUP BY collection_id with FILTER counts for visible and unavailable items Rolling deploy The new tables are additive.   2. Run DROP TABLE video_collection_items; DROP TABLE video_collections;.
  3. Remove the Liquibase changeset row.

No existing data is touched.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Login endpoint & lockout (1 d) — PW-2 (after PW-1)
docs.text:
• [ ] POST /user/login in UserController (@RateLimited(permit = 10), @AuditLog), PasswordLoginRequest {@Sensitive email, @Sensitive password}
  • [ ] Service PasswordLoginService.login:
    • flag off → 404
    • find user; if null / password null / DEACTIVATED / locked_until > now → run a dummy BCrypt match (timing) → throw INVALID_CREDENTIALS
    • BCrypt match fail → failed_login_count++; at 5 → locked_until = now + 15m, reset count → INVALID_CREDENTIALS
    • success → reset count/lock; MFA → existing MFA_REQUIRED flow; else JWT
  • [ ] All failures → identical 401 {"error":{"message":"INVALID_CREDENTIALS"}} via CustomException(UNAUTHORIZED)
  • [ ] Remove legacy branch in UserController.signIn (joinSystem) — /user/join = magic link only; delete/deprecate joinSystem + toEntity

docs.title: Plan: Bitwise Permission System — Full Wiring
docs.text: Relates to: 202605010001-init_permissions.sql, HasPermission.java, Permission.java, PermissionServiceImpl.java Size: Medium (1–2 days) Decision type: Two-Way Door (additive columns, replaceable auth layer) Blocks nothing — @HasPermission not yet used on any endpoint

docs.title: Problem Summary
docs.text:
The permission system has been partially built. Four issues prevent it from working end-to-end:

# Issue Severity 1 SQL seed bit_value is misaligned with Permission enum High — wrong users get wrong permissions 2 User entity has no permissions field (column exists in DB, entity doesn't) High — permissions never read 3 No custom UserDetails impl — authentication.principal.permissions always fails High — @HasPermission throws NPE 4 @HasPermission SpEL calls hasPermission(long, Permission) but passes Permission[] High — wrong method signature

docs.title: Design Decision: int over long
docs.text:
All permission fields use int (not long). Rationale:

  • 32 bits = 32 possible permissions — far more than this app needs
  • No L suffix noise in enum
  • PostgreSQL INT instead of BIGINT — cleaner schema
  • Since all files are uncommitted, now is the right time to align

Affects: Permission.java, PermissionService.java, PermissionServiceImpl.java, User.java, UserDetailDto.java, AppUserDetails.java, SQL column type.

docs.title: Issue 1 — SQL bit values wrong
docs.text:
Permission enum (source of truth, updated to int):

Enum Bit Value READ 1 << 0 1 WRITE 1 << 1 2 EXEC 1 << 2 4 DELETE 1 << 3 8 ADMIN 1 << 4 16

Current SQL seed (wrong):

(3, 'USER_DELETE', 'Delete User', 4, ...)   -- 4 = EXEC, not DELETE
(4, 'ADMIN_FULL',  'Admin Full',  8, ...)   -- 8 = DELETE, not ADMIN
-- EXEC (bit_value=4) is missing entirely

docs.title: Issue 2 — User.java entity missing permissions field
docs.text: users table has permissions BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (added by migration), but User.java entity has no field for it.

docs.title: Issue 3 — No custom UserDetails
docs.text:
UserServiceImpl.loadUserByUsername() returns Spring's generic User: 

return new org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.User(..., authorities);
Spring's User has no permissions field → authentication.principal.permissions throws PropertyNotFoundException at runtime.

docs.title: Issue 4 — Wrong method in SpEL expression
docs.text:
@HasPermission annotation: 

@PreAuthorize("@permissionServiceImpl.hasPermission(authentication.principal.permissions, #perms)")

  • #perms is Permission[] (array — from Permission[] perms())
  • hasPermission(long, Permission) takes a single Permission
  • Result: MethodResolutionException at runtime

docs.title: Step 1 — Fix SQL seed data
docs.text:
File: api/src/main/resources/db/changelog/sql/202605010001-init_permissions.sql

Change bit_value column type to INT and fix seed values:

CREATE TABLE permissions
(
    id          INT PRIMARY KEY,
    code        VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name        VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    bit_value   INT          NOT NULL UNIQUE,   -- was BIGINT, now INT
    description TEXT,
    group_name  VARCHAR(50),
    is_active   BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    created_at  TIMESTAMP             DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

INSERT INTO permissions (id, code, name, bit_value, description, group_name)
VALUES (1, 'READ',   'Read',   1,  'Read data',         'GENERAL'),
       (2, 'WRITE',  'Write',  2,  'Modify data',       'GENERAL'),
       (3, 'EXEC',   'Exec',   4,  'Execute actions',   'GENERAL'),
       (4, 'DELETE', 'Delete', 8,  'Delete data',       'GENERAL'),
       (5, 'ADMIN',  'Admin',  16, 'Full admin access', 'ADMIN');

ALTER TABLE users
    ADD COLUMN permissions INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;  -- was BIGINT

code values match Permission enum names exactly. Since this file is not yet committed, edit in place (no fixup migration needed).

docs.title: Step 2 — Switch Permission enum to int
docs.text:
File: api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/enums/Permission.java

private final int bit;

READ(1 << 0), WRITE(1 << 1), EXEC(1 << 2), DELETE(1 << 3), ADMIN(1 << 4);

Permission(int bit) { this.bit = bit; }
public int getBit() { return bit; }

docs.title: Step 3a — Update PermissionService and PermissionServiceImpl signatures
docs.text:
Files: service/PermissionService.java, service/impl/PermissionServiceImpl.java

Change all long userPermissions / long userPerm → int:

boolean hasPermission(int userPermissions, Permission perm);
boolean hasAllPermissions(int userPerm, Permission[] perms);
boolean hasAnyPermission(int userPerm, Permission[] perms);

Bitwise operations (&) work identically on int.

docs.title: Step 4a — Add permissions field to User.java entity
docs.text:
File: api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/entity/User.java

@Column(name = "permissions", nullable = false)
private int permissions = 0;

docs.title: Step 5 — Create AppUserDetails.java (custom UserDetails)
docs.text:
New file: api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/config/AppUserDetails.java

package com.canhlabs.funnyapp.config;

import com.canhlabs.funnyapp.entity.User;
import org.springframework.security.core.GrantedAuthority;
import org.springframework.security.core.authority.SimpleGrantedAuthority;
import org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.UserDetails;

import java.util.Collection;
import java.util.List;

public class AppUserDetails implements UserDetails {

    private final User user;

    public AppUserDetails(User user) {
        this.user = user;
    }

    public int getPermissions() {
        return user.getPermissions();
    }

    public Long getId() {
        return user.getId();
    }

    @Override
    public Collection<? extends GrantedAuthority> getAuthorities() {
        return List.of(new SimpleGrantedAuthority("ROLE_" + user.getRole().name()));
    }

    @Override public String getPassword()  { return user.getPassword(); }
    @Override public String getUsername()  { return user.getUserName(); }
    @Override public boolean isAccountNonExpired()   { return true; }
    @Override public boolean isAccountNonLocked()    { return true; }
    @Override public boolean isCredentialsNonExpired(){ return true; }
    @Override public boolean isEnabled()             { return true; }
}

docs.title: Step 6 — Update UserServiceImpl.loadUserByUsername()
docs.text:
File: api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/service/impl/UserServiceImpl.java

Replace the return that builds new User(...) with:

return new AppUserDetails(userEntity);  // userEntity is the User loaded from DB

docs.title: Step 7 — Fix @HasPermission SpEL expression
docs.text:
File: api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/aop/HasPermission.java

Change SpEL to use hasAllPermissions (AND semantics — user must have ALL listed permissions):

@PreAuthorize("@permissionServiceImpl.hasAllPermissions(authentication.principal.permissions, #perms)")

Or use hasAnyPermission for OR semantics. Decision: use hasAllPermissions since perms is an array and the common case is "user must have all of these".

docs.title: Step 8 — Update UserDetailDto
docs.text:
File: api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/dto/UserDetailDto.java

Add: 

private int permissions;

Update AppUtils.getCurrentUser() to populate it from AppUserDetails.

docs.title: Step 9 — Demo usage in AdminController
docs.text:
Add @HasPermission to one endpoint to validate end-to-end:

@GetMapping("/stats")
@HasPermission(perms = {Permission.ADMIN})
public ResponseEntity<ResultObjectInfo<AdminStatsDto>> getStats() { ... }

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:

  • [ ] Permission enum uses int with 1 << n (no L suffix)
  • [ ] PermissionService / PermissionServiceImpl use int for all permission params
  • [ ] User.java has permissions (int) field mapped to permissions column
  • [ ] AppUserDetails wraps User and exposes getPermissions() as int
  • [ ] loadUserByUsername() returns AppUserDetails
  • [ ] authentication.principal.permissions resolves correctly in SpEL
  • [ ] @HasPermission(perms = {Permission.ADMIN}) on a method enforces access

docs.text: # File Action 1 db/changelog/sql/202605010001-init_permissions.sql Fix seed data (5 rows, correct bit values), BIGINT → INT 2 enums/Permission.java long bit → int bit, 1L << n → 1 << n 3 service/PermissionService.java long → int in all method signatures 4 service/impl/PermissionServiceImpl.java long → int in all method params 5 entity/User.java Add permissions int field 6 config/AppUserDetails.java Create — custom UserDetails with int getPermissions() 7 service/impl/UserServiceImpl.java Return AppUserDetails from loadUserByUsername() 8 aop/HasPermission.java Fix SpEL: hasPermission → hasAllPermissions 9 dto/UserDetailDto.java Add permissions int field 10 web/AdminController.java Add @HasPermission on getStats() as demo

docs.title: Feature Flag Gate (Harness FF)
docs.text:
The bitwise permission enforcement is controlled by a Harness FF boolean flag permission_enforcement_enabled.

Flag state Behavior OFF (default) All permission checks return true — only role guard applies ON Bitwise check enforced via PermissionServiceImpl

Default = false (permissive) — existing @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") still protects all endpoints while the flag rolls out. If Harness is unreachable at startup, false keeps the app working.

docs.title: Flag target
docs.text: Uses current authenticated user (SecurityContextHolder) as target identifier; falls back to "system".

docs.title: Additional files
docs.text: # File Action A pom.xml Add io.harness:ff-java-server-sdk:1.9.3 B application.yaml Add harness.ff.api-key: ${FF_API_KEY:} C utils/AppConstant.java Add inner class Flags with PERMISSION_ENFORCEMENT constant D service/FeatureFlagService.java New interface: isEnabled(String flag, boolean defaultValue) E service/impl/FeatureFlagServiceImpl.java @PostConstruct init CfClient, @PreDestroy close, no-op when key blank F service/impl/PermissionServiceImpl.java Inject FeatureFlagService, short-circuit all 3 methods when flag OFF

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Migrate webapp/ from ~4,400 lines of vanilla JS + jQuery to React 19 + Vite. No backend changes. Feature parity only — no new features. Migration follows a bottom-up approach: infrastructure → auth → video core → social → layout → CI/CD → QA.

docs.title: Task 1: Initialize Vite + React project
docs.text:
Acceptance criteria:

  • webapp/ contains a working Vite + React 19 project
  • npm run dev starts local dev server
  • npm run build produces webapp/dist/
  • Old files (js/, index.html, css/) moved to webapp/legacy/ (kept for reference, not deployed)

Steps:

  1. Run npm create vite@latest . -- --template react inside webapp/
  2. Install dependencies: npm install react-router-dom @tanstack/react-query react-bootstrap bootstrap react-swipeable @fortawesome/react-fontawesome @fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons @fortawesome/free-brands-svg-icons
  3. Install dev deps: npm install -D vitest @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom @testing-library/user-event jsdom
  4. Create project structure (see below)
  5. Move legacy files: mkdir legacy && mv index.html js/ css/ manifest.json legacy/
  6. Copy manifest.json to public/manifest.json
  7. Copy icons to public/icons/

Project structure: 

webapp/
├── public/
│   ├── manifest.json
│   └── icons/
├── src/
│   ├── api/          # API client + endpoint functions
│   ├── components/   # Reusable UI components
│   │   ├── auth/     # Login, MFA, Profile, MagicLink

docs.title: Task 2: API client layer
docs.text:
Acceptance criteria:

  • All 14 API endpoints implemented as async functions
  • JWT + guestToken headers injected automatically
  • Error shape normalized: { message, status } on failure
  • REACT_APP_API_BASE_URL (or VITE_API_BASE_URL) used for base URL

  3. Create src/api/videos.js — list, privateList, share, delete
  4. Create src/api/comments.js — list, post, delete

docs.title: Task 4: AuthContext + useAuth hook
docs.text:
Acceptance criteria:

  • JWT, user, guestToken stored in/read from localStorage
  • useAuth() provides: { user, isLoggedIn, login, logout, setGuestToken }
  • Session validation on app mount (calls GET /user/me)

Steps:

docs.title: Task 6: MagicLink handler

docs.title: Plan: Disable the Reopen Button While the Request Is Pending
Overview
docs.text: Status: Done 2026-10-19 (autopilot, headless, issue #26) Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-19 Related plan: plan-suggestion-rereview (added the Reopen button) ADR: none. One attribute on one button; no API, schema or behavior change on the server. Size: Small. This plan is the only artifact.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In the admin Suggestions tab the Reopen button only sets aria-busy while its mutation runs, so it can still be clicked. A second click opens the confirm dialog again, and confirming sends a second POST /admin/video-suggestions/{id}/reopen. Disable the button while that row's request is pending, and add a test.

docs.title: Verified Facts (read 2026-10-19)
docs.text: Fact Where The Reopen button has aria-busy={isBusyFor(reopen, s.id, v => v?.id)} and no disabled webapp/src/components/admin/AdminSuggestionTable.jsx:260-270 reopenRow awaits the confirm dialog, then calls reopen.mutate({ id: s.id }, ...) AdminSuggestionTable.jsx:179-188 isBusyFor is true only while mutation.isPending and the variables match the row id webapp/src/utils/mutationBusy.js:5-10 The Approve / Reject modal submit buttons use disabled={saving} aria-busy={saving} (saving = mutation.isPending) AdminSuggestionTable.jsx:65,101,294,303 The Approve / Reject row buttons only set aria-busy; they open a modal rather than send a request, so they cannot double-send AdminSuggestionTable.jsx:240-257 Existing reopen tests live in describe('reopen'); the API is mocked with suggestionsApi.reopen webapp/src/components/admin/__tests__/AdminSuggestionTable.test.jsx:133-175

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• D1: compute const reopening = isBusyFor(reopen, s.id, v => v?.id) for the row and set disabled={reopening} next to the existing aria-busy={reopening}. The disabled state is per row, the same scope as aria-busy, so reopening one suggestion does not block another.
  • D1b: one useReopenSuggestion instance serves the whole table and keeps only the latest variables, so the per-row flag is exact for one request at a time. reopenRow therefore also returns early when reopen.isPending, so a second request cannot start while one is running.
  • D2: Approve / Reject row buttons are left alone. The issue asks for Reopen, and those open a modal whose submit button is already disabled while pending.
  • Because reopenRow awaits the confirm dialog, the dialog's backdrop covers the table until the user answers, so the only gap that matters is "mutation pending", which D1 closes.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
ID Task Acceptance criteria Depends on RB-1 AdminSuggestionTable.jsx: disabled on the Reopen row button while isBusyFor(reopen, s.id, ...), plus an early return in reopenRow when reopen.isPending While suggestionsApi.reopen is unresolved the button has disabled and aria-busy="true"; after it resolves the button is enabled again; no other file changes — RB-2 Test in describe('reopen') of AdminSuggestionTable.test.jsx With reopen mocked as a never-resolving promise: click Reopen, confirm, assert the button is disabled and aria-busy; click it again and assert no second dialog opens (queryByRole('dialog') is null) and suggestionsApi.reopen was called exactly once with 2. The test fails without RB-1 RB-1

Gates: npm run test and npm run lint in webapp/. No backend change, so no mvn verify.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation disabled removes the button from the tab order, so focus is lost after the click Same as the modal buttons; the button comes back when the list refetches A second click between mutate() and the re-render that applies disabled (TanStack batches notifications, so the DOM updates a tick later) The window is tiny, and the confirm dialog must be answered again before a second mutate; D1b's isPending guard in reopenRow closes it once the re-render lands

docs.title: Plan: Notify the Reporter When the Report's Issue Is Closed
docs.text:
Status: Done, deployed 2026-10-21 (RN-1..RN-3, 801dcb9f, b3030e52); owner check of the bell pending · ADR: none (follows ADR-0017 notifications and ADR-0026 D7 webhook) · Parent: plan-report-webhook-state

Started as an autopilot lite run; promoted to full mode when the diff passed ~100 LOC (tests excluded). Implementation note: ReportClosedEvent carries (issueNumber, reason) instead of the report id; the listener looks the report up by issue number, so the webhook needs no extra query.

Request: "notify user tao report khi issue duoc close". Lite: ~90 LOC non-test, follows the existing notification pattern (ADR-0017 user notifications; SuggestionNotificationListener), no ADR.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• When the GitHub webhook APPLIES a closed state to a CREATED report (ADR-0026 D7), the report's reporter gets an in-app notification REPORT_CLOSED (bell + SSE unread count), and it is included in the email digest like other notifications.
  • Payload: snippet = report title, reason = stored state_reason (completed / not_planned / duplicate, or absent).
  • Not sent for: reopened; STALE or UNKNOWN_ISSUE outcomes (so a redelivery never notifies twice); reporter deleted (reporter_id null) or DEACTIVATED.
  • Group key report:<reportId>:REPORT_CLOSED: closing again while the first is unread collapses into one row (existing upsertGrouped, repo/NotificationRepository.java:35-56).
  • Click on the notification opens the Report page (nav key report).
  • Failures never affect the webhook response: listener is async and catches everything (same as service/notification/SuggestionNotificationListener.java:61-69).

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text: ID Task ~LOC Acceptance criteria RN-1 NotificationType.REPORT_CLOSED (enums/NotificationType.java:3-9; column is VARCHAR(30) with no CHECK, db/changelog/sql/202610030001-create-notifications.sql:4). New record event/ReportClosedEvent(int issueNumber, String reason) (reason captured at publish time, so a quick reopen cannot change it). GitHubWebhookServiceImpl.handle (service/impl/GitHubWebhookServiceImpl.java:60-82) publishes it via ApplicationEventPublisher only when outcome = APPLIED and state = CLOSED; the listener finds the report with the new repo method Optional<AppReport> findFirstWithReporterByStatusAndIssueNumber(...) with @EntityGraph("reporter") (like repo/AppReportRepository.java:26-28). New service/notification/ReportNotificationListener with @Async @TransactionalEventListener(phase = AFTER_COMMIT, fallbackExecution = true) (the webhook has no outer transaction), which loads the row, skips null/DEACTIVATED reporter, calls upsertGrouped(userId, "REPORT_CLOSED", "report:<id>:REPORT_CLOSED", null, null, null, {"snippet": title, "reason": reason?}) and publisher.unreadChanged(userId) ~55 Unit tests: webhook publishes the event on APPLIED+CLOSED only (not on reopened, STALE, UNKNOWN_ISSUE, IGNORED); listener upserts with the right type, group key and payload and pings SSE; skips a deleted or deactivated reporter; never throws (repo exception swallowed and logged). Single-constructor beans (BeanConstructorTest passes) RN-2 Digest text: NotificationDigestService.describe (service/notification/NotificationDigestService.java:126-143) handles REPORT_CLOSED → mail.digest.item.reportClosed / reportClosedReason in i18n/messages.properties and messages_vi.properties (next to :101-102) ~12 NotificationDigestServiceTest: a REPORT_CLOSED row renders "Your report "T" was closed" and with reason "(completed)" in en and vi RN-3 FE: utils/notificationText.js:5-22 returns notifications:reportClosed with title and a translated reason (report:stateReason.* from the D7 work, fallback raw value); new helper notificationNav(n, isAdmin) in utils/notificationText.js returns 'history' for suggestion approved/rejected (moved from AppShell.jsx:102-104), 'report' for REPORT_CLOSED when the user is admin, else null (a demoted reporter: the report nav is admin-only, AppShell.jsx:158,379); openNotification (:101-117) uses it; keys in {en,vi}/notifications.json (next to :14) ~20 notificationText.test.js: text with and without reason, unknown reason falls back; i18n parity test passes; notificationNav unit tests: REPORT_CLOSED → report for admin, null for non-admin; suggestion types → history; others → null; npm run test + npm run lint pass

docs.title: Not in scope
docs.text:
• Notifying on reopen, on comments or on PR merge.
  • Email right away (the digest job sends it, as for every other notification).
  • Notifying anyone other than the reporter.

docs.title: Plan: Report Issue State by GitHub Webhook
Overview
docs.text: Status: Done (WH-1..WH-5; prod-checked 2026-10-21) Date: 2026-10-21 ADR: ADR-0026 D7 · Spec: spec-in-app-report v1.3 (BR-9, BR-10, FR-8, EC-14..EC-17) · Parent plan: plan-in-app-report Size: Small feature on top of In-App Report. 4 implementation tasks (~230 LOC non-test), plus owner setup (WH-5).

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: GitHub pushes closed / reopened issue events to the app; the app verifies the HMAC signature and stores the state and its reason on app_report. The report list uses the stored state and calls GitHub only for rows that have none. The badge shows the reason ("Closed · completed" / "Closed · not planned").

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text: Spec v1.3: BR-9 (changed), BR-10, FR-8, the webhook endpoint, the modified app_report table, ReportDto.githubStateReason, EC-14..EC-17 and the webhook acceptance criteria.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Other issue events (comments, labels, PR links) and in-app notifications.
  • Back-filling the state of existing reports (they keep the read-through path until their next event).
  • Storing the read-through result.
  • Automatic redelivery of missed events (GitHub has none; the owner can redeliver by hand).

docs.title: Architecture Changes
docs.text:
api.github.com ──POST (HMAC)──► GitHubWebhookController ──► GitHubWebhookService ──► AppReportRepository.applyGithubState (conditional UPDATE)
ReportPage (FE) ──► AdminReportController ──► ReportServiceImpl.list ──► stored state, else GitHubIssueClient + GitHubIssueStateCache (as today)

Layers stay web → service → repo; service → config for the secret. No new library.

docs.title: Key Decisions
docs.text:
• No new ADR. ADR-0026 D7 (2026-10-21) covers the endpoint, the secret, the columns and the ordering rule.
  • Public path: add POST /webhooks/github to WHITE_LIST_PATH (api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/utils/AppConstant.java:45-54). That list is used both by WebSecurityConfig (filter/WebSecurityConfig.java:55) and by JWTAuthenticationFilter.shouldNotFilter (filter/JWTAuthenticationFilter.java:104-110), so no JWT is needed and none is parsed.
  • Raw body, capped: the controller reads HttpServletRequest.getInputStream().readNBytes(MAX_BODY + 1) with MAX_BODY = 1 MiB and returns 413 above it, before the HMAC check. Check order: 503 (no secret, body not read) → 413 → 401 → 400 → 204, pinned by a controller test that posts a raw body (CWE-770; issues payloads are tens of KB). No filter in api/ reads the request body first (no ContentCachingRequestWrapper; filter/ holds only the JWT filter, provider and security config).
  • Signature: HmacSHA256 (JDK javax.crypto.Mac) over the raw bytes; compare sha256=<hex> with MessageDigest.isEqual. Verify before any JSON parsing. Header format checked against GitHub's "Validating webhook deliveries" page.
  • Secret config: add webhookSecret to AppProperties.Github (config/AppProperties.java:118-126) with isWebhookConfigured(), and webhook-secret: ${GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET:} under app.github (api/src/main/resources/application.yaml:144-147). The name contains secret, which is on the masking list (application.yaml:168-169), and it never enters a DTO.
  • Transaction: the repo method is @Modifying @Transactional @Query(...); the service is not transactional otherwise (Spring Data needs a transaction for a modifying query, else TransactionRequiredException).
  • Ordering and races: one JPQL @Modifying update, WHERE status = CREATED AND issueNumber = :n AND (githubStateAt IS NULL OR githubStateAt < :at). Zero rows → existsByStatusAndIssueNumber tells stale from unknown-issue. This makes EC-14 and EC-16 hold under concurrent deliveries without locks.
  • Reason whitelist: state_reason is kept only when it is one of completed, not_planned, duplicate, reopened; anything else is stored as null (fits VARCHAR(16), no 500 after a valid signature).
  • State mapping: GitHubIssueState (entity enum) maps to GitHubIssueClient.IssueState by name (OPEN→OPEN, CLOSED→CLOSED) in resolveStates; toDto keeps taking the state as a string (:291).
  • List: ReportServiceImpl.resolveStates (service/impl/ReportServiceImpl.java:197-229) skips the GitHub call when row.getGithubState() != null. toDto (:291-310) adds githubStateReason from the row (null for read-through rows).
  • Migration: new file api/src/main/resources/db/changelog/sql/202610210001-app-report-github-state.sql, picked up by includeAll: sql/ (db/changelog/db.changelog-master.yaml:2-3). Additive, nullable columns only, so a rolling deploy is safe. Latest file today: 202610200001-create-app-report.sql.
  • Controller style: like web/AdminReportController.java:30-40 (@RestController, AppConstant.API.BASE_URL, setter injection), but without @PreAuthorize, @HasPermission or @RateLimited, since there is no user.
  • FE badge: StateBadge (webapp/src/components/report/ReportPage.jsx:34-40) appends · <reason> when githubStateReason is set, from new i18n keys stateReason.* next to state (webapp/src/i18n/locales/en/report.json:52, vi/report.json:52).

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text: ID Task Depends on ~LOC (non-test) Acceptance criteria WH-1 Migration 202610210001-app-report-github-state.sql (spec "Modified Tables"); new enum enums/GitHubIssueState { OPEN, CLOSED } (kept out of client so entity does not depend on client); AppReport fields githubState (@Enumerated(STRING)), githubStateReason, githubStateAt (entity/AppReport.java:90-97 area); repo methods applyGithubState(...) (conditional update, returns int) and existsByStatusAndIssueNumber (repo/AppReportRepository.java:15-28); applyGithubState is @Modifying @Transactional — ~40 Migration SQL matches the spec; columns nullable; applyGithubState carries @Modifying and @Transactional (checked by a reflection test, since the repo is mocked elsewhere); mvn verify passes; entity maps the new columns (checked by the WH-2 service test with a mocked repo and by BeanConstructorTest still passing) WH-2 AppProperties.Github.webhookSecret + yaml; GitHubWebhookService (verify(signatureHeader, body), handle(event, deliveryId, body) → outcome enum APPLIED/IGNORED/STALE/UNKNOWN_ISSUE); GitHubWebhookController POST /v1/funny-app/webhooks/github returning 204/400/401/503; WHITE_LIST_PATH entry WH-1 ~130 Unit tests: valid signature + closed/completed → repo update called with CLOSED, completed, payload updated_at; wrong, missing or malformed signature → 401 and repo untouched; blank secret → 503; ping and issues/labeled → 204 IGNORED; other repository.full_name → IGNORED; zero rows updated + exists → STALE, + not exists → UNKNOWN_ISSUE; bad JSON with valid signature → 400; issues event without issue.number → 400; body over 1 MiB → 413 and no HMAC/parse; unknown state_reason (e.g. something_new_and_long) → stored as null. @WebMvcTest (or the AdminReportControllerPermissionTest style) proves the path needs no JWT. Logs carry delivery id, event, action, issue number, outcome; a test with a fake secret and body asserts neither appears in the captured log WH-3 ReportServiceImpl.resolveStates uses the stored state (mapped by name to IssueState); ReportDto.githubStateReason (dto/admin/ReportDto.java); toDto fills it WH-1 ~25 ReportServiceImplTest: a CREATED row with stored CLOSED/not_planned → DTO has both and client.state is never called; a row without a stored state → read-through as before (existing tests stay green); FAILED rows → both null WH-4 FE StateBadge shows the reason; i18n stateReason.{completed,not_planned,duplicate,reopened} in en and vi report.json WH-3 ~20 ReportPage.test.jsx: a CLOSED row with githubStateReason: 'not_planned' renders "Closed · Not planned"; a row without a reason renders "Closed" only; unknown reason falls back to the raw value; i18n parity test passes; npm run test and npm run lint pass WH-5 Owner setup + prod check (not run by agents): repo Settings → Webhooks (URL https://canh-labs.com/api/v1/funny-app/webhooks/github, application/json, random secret, Issues only); GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET in /opt/funnyapp/.env, restart; close and reopen a test issue created from the app WH-2..WH-4 deployed — GitHub "Recent Deliveries" shows 204 for ping and for the close; the Report list shows "Closed · completed" without waiting for the 5-min cache

docs.title: Merge order
docs.text:
• WH-1 → WH-2 and WH-3 (independent of each other) → WH-4. Every unit merges to main on its own: WH-1 is dark (unused columns); WH-2 adds the endpoint, which returns 503 until the secret is set; WH-3 reads the columns, which stay null until events arrive.
  • Backend before frontend: WH-4 reads githubStateReason, which is absent (undefined) until WH-3 is deployed, and the badge then shows "Closed" as today.

docs.title: Files to Modify
docs.text: Path Action Task api/src/main/resources/db/changelog/sql/202610210001-app-report-github-state.sql Create WH-1 api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/entity/AppReport.java Modify WH-1 api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/repo/AppReportRepository.java Modify WH-1 api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/config/AppProperties.java, api/src/main/resources/application.yaml Modify WH-2 api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/service/GitHubWebhookService.java (+ impl/), web/GitHubWebhookController.java Create WH-2 api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/utils/AppConstant.java Modify WH-2 api/src/main/java/com/canhlabs/funnyapp/service/impl/ReportServiceImpl.java, dto/admin/ReportDto.java Modify WH-3 webapp/src/components/report/ReportPage.jsx, webapp/src/i18n/locales/{en,vi}/report.json Modify WH-4 Tests: service/impl/GitHubWebhookServiceImplTest.java, web/GitHubWebhookControllerTest.java, ReportServiceImplTest.java, ReportPage.test.jsx Create / Modify WH-2..WH-4

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
• Unit: HMAC verify with a known vector (secret + body → expected hex computed in the test with Mac), every outcome of handle, resolveStates with stored vs missing state.
  • Web slice: the webhook path answers without an Authorization header; the admin paths still need one (regression).
  • Not covered by automated tests: the conditional UPDATE against PostgreSQL (no DB test infra in api/, same accepted gap as the parent plan); it is checked in WH-5 by closing an issue twice (redelivery → stale in the log).
  • Gates: mvn -f api/pom.xml verify (coverage ≥ api/.coverage-threshold), npm --prefix webapp run test, npm --prefix webapp run lint.

docs.title: Rollback Plan
docs.text:
• Unset GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET (endpoint → 503) or delete the webhook on GitHub: the list falls back to stored-or-read-through, and stored states simply stop updating.
  • Revert WH-3 to return to read-through only. The columns can stay (nullable, unused).

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Secret leak lets anyone set display states Separate secret from the PAT; rotate in GitHub and the env file; effect is display only (ADR-0026 D7 consequences) Missed delivery leaves a stale state Owner redelivers from "Recent Deliveries"; accepted in ADR-0026 D7 A proxy changes the body and breaks the signature Nginx passes the body unchanged by default; WH-5 checks the ping delivery returns 204

docs.title: Plan: Max Re-review Count Comes From the API (Issue #28)
Overview
docs.text: Status: Planned 2026-10-19 (autopilot, headless, issue #28) Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-19 Related plan: plan-suggestion-rereview, plan-suggestion-transitions ADR: none. docs.title: Objective
docs.text: The limit on re-review requests lives in two places: SuggestionTransition.MAX_REREVIEWS = 2 (BE) and REREVIEW_MAX = 2 (FE). Changing one makes the "Re-review requested n/2" text wrong. Make the BE the only source: SuggestionDto gets maxRereviews, and the card reads it. The value stays 2, and no behavior or DB change.

Overview
docs.text: Status: Done 2026-10-19 (autopilot, headless, issue #30; merge deploys) Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-19 Related plan: plan-suggestion-rereview (added the modal) ADR: none. Frontend-only behavior of one component; no API, schema or dependency change. Size: Small. This plan is the only artifact.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: RereviewModal (the "Request re-review" dialog in "My suggestions") closes only on a backdrop click or the Cancel button, and keyboard focus stays on the button behind it. Make Escape close it (unless the request is pending) and focus the message textarea when it opens.

docs.text: Fact Where RereviewModal renders a backdrop whose onClick is rereview.isPending ? undefined : onClose, and a Cancel button disabled={rereview.isPending} webapp/src/components/history/SuggestionCard.jsx:32,51 The component has no useEffect, no useRef and no keydown handling; the file imports only useState SuggestionCard.jsx:1,17-59 The textarea has id="rereview-msg-{id}" and no ref SuggestionCard.jsx:40-47 The parent passes an inline onClose={() => setRereviewOpen(false)}, a new function on every parent render SuggestionCard.jsx:152 Reference pattern: a window keydown listener in useEffect, ignored while pending, removed on cleanup, deps [onCancel, pending] webapp/src/components/common/ConfirmModal.jsx:21-26 ConfirmModal focuses its confirm button inside that same effect ConfirmModal.jsx:22 Tests use renderCard, openDialog() (clicks "Request re-review", returns the dialog) and a mocked suggestionsApi.requestRereview webapp/src/components/history/__tests__/SuggestionCard.test.jsx:9-26,31 The existing cancel test closes via the Cancel button and asserts no API call SuggestionCard.test.jsx:99-104 jest-dom matchers (toHaveAttribute, toHaveValue) are already available in this test file SuggestionCard.test.jsx:59,95

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• D1 (Escape): add the ConfirmModal effect to RereviewModal: window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey) with if (e.key === 'Escape' && !rereview.isPending) onClose(), removed on cleanup, deps [onClose, rereview.isPending]. This is the same rule as the backdrop click and the disabled Cancel button.
  • D2 (focus): a useRef on the textarea and a separate useEffect(() => { messageRef.current?.focus() }, []). It is not merged into the Escape effect as ConfirmModal does, because onClose is a new function on every parent render: the Escape effect re-runs on each render, and a focus call inside it would pull focus back to the textarea whenever the parent re-renders (for example when the copied timeout state changes, or a query refetch re-renders the card).
  • D3: ConfirmModal and the other modals are not touched (out of scope in the issue). No new dependency, no CSS, no i18n key.
  • D4: no focus return to the opening button on close. The issue does not ask for it.

docs.title: Plan: Suggestion Re-review (Admin Reopen + User Request)
Overview
docs.text: Status: Built 2026-10-19 (autopilot) · BE 6c16388e, FE 29c1fd94; SR-QA-1 verified on prod by owner (2026-10-19) Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-19 Related plan: plan-video-suggestions (the flow this extends) ADR: none. This adds two state transitions and two endpoints that follow the existing approve/reject pattern, plus one additive Liquibase column. It is easy to undo (swarm-plan Artifact Requirements). Size: Small feature (~1 day). This plan is the only artifact.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
1. Admin "Đề xuất" tab: an admin can move a reviewed suggestion back to Pending ("Chờ duyệt"), then approve or reject it again with the existing buttons.
  2. User "My suggestions" (History): after a suggestion is rejected, its submitter can request a re-review, with an optional message. The suggestion goes back to Pending and shows up again in the admin queue and the pending-count badge.

docs.title: Verified Facts (exploration 2026-10-19)
docs.text: Area Fact Impact Entity VideoSuggestion (entity/VideoSuggestion.java:29) has status, rejectReason, rejectNote, reviewedBy, reviewedAt, importJobId. SuggestionStatus = PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED (enums/SuggestionStatus.java:4) Re-review needs no new status. Reopening = back to PENDING with the decision fields cleared Schema 202610150002-create-video-suggestions.sql:21: partial unique index on normalized_url WHERE status='PENDING' Reopening can collide with another pending suggestion for the same URL. Handle it like submit (D4) Duplicate rule submit (VideoSuggestionServiceImpl.java:114-131) rejects when a PENDING suggestion exists for the URL, or an import job in BLOCKING_IMPORT_STATUSES (:54), and maps DataIntegrityViolationException to error.suggestion.duplicate Reuse the same check and the same mapping on reopen Lock / guard lockPending (:218) takes a PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock. Non-PENDING → 409 4093 error.suggestion.notPending; missing → 404 4042 Add a sibling lock helper for "reviewed" states Approve side effect Approve creates an import job (importService.createResolved, :239). The video appears when the job finishes (ImportStatus: PENDING, DOWNLOADING, UPLOADING, DONE, FAILED, CANCELLED) Reopening an APPROVED suggestion whose job is active or DONE would leave a video or job behind it → allow it only when the job is FAILED or CANCELLED (D1) Admin API AdminVideoSuggestionController (web/AdminVideoSuggestionController.java:30) has class-level hasRole('ADMIN') + per-method @HasPermission(perm=ADMIN). POST /{id}/approve :54, /{id}/reject :64 New POST /{id}/reopen follows the same annotations User API VideoSuggestionController (web/VideoSuggestionController.java:40-57): POST /suggestions @RateLimited(10) + @AuditLog, GET /mine @RateLimited(60); null-user check → 401 4011 New POST /suggestions/{id}/rereview follows the same pattern Notifications SuggestionReviewedEvent → SuggestionNotificationListener.onReviewed (service/notification/SuggestionNotificationListener.java:62) sends APPROVED / REJECTED Re-approve and re-reject reuse it unchanged. No new notification type (D5) Admin UI components/admin/AdminSuggestionTable.jsx: approve/reject buttons only when status === 'PENDING' (:215-234); ModalShell modals (:27); hooks hooks/useAdminSuggestions.js invalidate ['admin','suggestions'] (:19-29); API api/suggestions.js:21-24 Add a Reopen button for REJECTED rows and for APPROVED rows with a failed or cancelled job. Reuse useSuggestionMutation User UI components/history/SuggestionCard.jsx (status chip :66), SuggestionStatusChip.jsx:15-19 shows the reject reason; hook hooks/useSuggestions.js keys ['suggestions','mine-infinite',…] (:31) Add a "Request re-review" action on REJECTED cards. docs.title: Design Decisions
docs.text:
• D1 — What an admin can reopen.
    • REJECTED → PENDING is always allowed.
    • APPROVED → PENDING is allowed only when its import job is FAILED or CANCELLED. Any other job state, or a missing job, gets 409 error.suggestion.cannotReopen. This prevents a live video or a running download from sitting behind a "pending" suggestion. Re-approving then creates a fresh import job.
    • PENDING gets 409 error.suggestion.alreadyPending.
    • Race with an import retry (POST /admin/video-imports/{id}/retry → VideoImportServiceImpl.retry :222 → VideoImportJobRepository.retryIfFinal :97, a conditional UPDATE … WHERE status IN ('FAILED','CANCELLED')): reopen locks the suggestion row (as lockPending), then locks the job row with a new @Lock(PESSIMISTIC_WRITE) findLockedById. It re-reads the job status under that lock and only then detaches the job (importJobId = null). A retry that runs at the same time blocks on the job row:
      • Retry commits first: reopen sees the job as active and returns 409 cannotReopen.
      • Reopen commits first: the retry still runs on the now-detached job. The suggestion stays PENDING. A later approve then hits the existing BLOCKING_IMPORT_STATUSES check in createResolved and returns 409 error.import.duplicateActive, so the system never creates a second job or a duplicate video. The admin can then reject it as DUPLICATE. This is accepted behavior: a retry after reopen is an explicit admin action on the import tab.
  • D2 — Reopen clears the decision. rejectReason, rejectNote, reviewedBy, reviewedAt, importJobId are set to null and status to PENDING. The trail stays in @AuditLog on both endpoints, and the old import job row is kept.
  • D3 — User re-review request.
    • Only the owner of a REJECTED suggestion can request one. Not the owner → 404, so other users' ids are not revealed. Not REJECTED → 409 error.suggestion.notRejected.
    • Each suggestion allows at most 2 user re-review requests: new column rereview_count INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0. Over the limit → 409 error.suggestion.rereviewLimit.
    • The user may add an optional message. It comes in a new RereviewSuggestionRequest DTO (dto/suggestion/, like SubmitSuggestionRequest.java:18) with @Size(max = 300), and the controller takes @Valid @RequestBody(required = false). The service applies the same handling as submit's note (VideoSuggestionServiceImpl.java:124): trim, and a blank becomes null. The message replaces note, so the admin sees why the user is asking again. The UI renders it as React text only, with no dangerouslySetInnerHTML (CWE-79). A test checks that markup is shown as literal text.
    • The cap is enforced in SQL so two concurrent calls cannot both pass. The update is … SET rereview_count = rereview_count + 1, status='PENDING' … WHERE id=:id AND user_id=:uid AND status='REJECTED' AND rereview_count < 2 after the suggestion lock. 0 rows updated → the service tells 404, 409 notRejected and 409 limit apart by re-reading the row.
    • Anti-abuse (CWE-770): 2 requests per suggestion, plus @RateLimited(10) per user on the endpoint. The daily submit quota already limits how many suggestions a user can create. Together these keep re-review traffic on the order of the user's own rejected suggestions.
    • The endpoint has @RateLimited(permit=10) + @AuditLog. It does not count toward the daily submit quota.
    • An admin reopen does not increase rereview_count.
  • D4 — Duplicates on reopen. Both paths run the submit duplicate check: another PENDING suggestion for the URL, or an import job in BLOCKING_IMPORT_STATUSES. They also map DataIntegrityViolationException from the partial unique index to 409 error.suggestion.duplicate. Both paths take the PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock.
  • D5 — No new notification type (accepted). Neither path sends a notification: an admin reopen tells nobody, and a user re-review request does not notify admins. The admin pending-count badge already shows the suggestion again. The next approve or reject sends the existing notification.
  • D6 — DTO. SuggestionDto gains rereviewCount and canRequestRereview. canRequestRereview is true when the status is REJECTED and the count is < 2, so the UI does not repeat the rule. The admin DTO gains canReopen, which applies the D1 rule on the server. For APPROVED rows the job statuses come from one batched query per page (findAllById(jobIds) → map), the same approach as the existing live-ref lookup (VideoSuggestionRepository.findLiveRefs :91). There is no per-row query (no N+1).

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation A user spams re-review requests Cap of 2 per suggestion + @RateLimited(10) Reopening an approved suggestion orphans a running import D1 allows it only for FAILED or CANCELLED jobs, checked on the server Race between two admins (reopen vs approve) Same PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock as approve/reject Race between reopen and an import retry Job row locked and re-read under lock (D1); a retry after reopen ends in 409 duplicateActive on approve, never a second job Concurrent re-review requests Conditional UPDATE with rereview_count < 2 (D3)

docs.title: Plan: One Place for Suggestion Status Transitions (Refactor)
Overview
docs.text: Status: Built 2026-10-19 (autopilot) · 08f16414 Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-19 Related plan: plan-suggestion-rereview (added reopen + rereview, which spread the rules out) ADR: none. This is an internal refactor inside one service: no API, schema or behavior change, and it is easy to revert. Size: Small (a few hours). This plan is the only artifact. Hat: Refactoring only (.claude/rules/code-quality.md Two Hats Rule). Behavior stays the same, and the existing tests must pass without edits.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Today the rule "which suggestion may move from which status to which" lives in five places:

  • lockPending;
  • reopen's inline checks;
  • requireRereviewable;
  • canReopen;
  • the canRequestRereview expression in the DTO mapping.

Move these rules into one type, so the service, the DTO flags and the tests all read the same table. The concurrency guards stay where they are: the row locks, the conditional UPDATE and the partial unique index handle races, not business rules.

docs.title: Verified Facts (read 2026-10-19, service/impl/VideoSuggestionServiceImpl.java after 6c16388e)
docs.text:
Transition Current rule location Rule Error when refused approve, reject lockPending :279-286 status == PENDING 409 4093 error.suggestion.notPending reopen (admin) reopen :228-238 PENDING → refuse; APPROVED → job status (read via findLockedById) ∈ REOPENABLE_JOB_STATUSES; REJECTED → OK 409 4095 alreadyPending; 409 4096 cannotReopen rereview (user) requireRereviewable :288-295 status == REJECTED and rereviewCount < MAX_REREVIEWS 409 4097 notRejected; 409 4098 rereviewLimit DTO canReopen canReopen :314-318 same as the reopen rule, as a boolean — DTO canRequestRereview toDto :419 same as the rereview rule, as a boolean — DB guard (stays) VideoSuggestionRepository.requestRereview :37-48 WHERE status = REJECTED AND rereview_count < :maxCount 0 rows → re-read at VideoSuggestionServiceImpl.java:268 runs the rereview rule again (third caller) DTO canReopen argument submit :132, mine :152, approve :197, reopen :247 pass false; reject :219 passes true; list computes canReopen(...) after approve the job is fresh (never reopenable); after reject REOPEN is always allowed; mine is the user view —

Duplicate and not-found checks (requireNoDuplicate, 404 4042) are not transition rules and stay in the service. These also stay unchanged, because they select data rather than allow a transition:

  • the APPROVED && importJobId != null filters in liveRefs (:324) and jobStatuses (:373);
  • the APPROVED filter in SuggestionNotificationListener.java:78.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• D1 — SuggestionTransition enum in enums/, next to SuggestionStatus. Values: APPROVE, REJECT, REOPEN, REREVIEW. Each value implements:
    • Optional<Refusal> check(SuggestionStatus status, ImportStatus jobStatus, int rereviewCount). It is a pure function with no repository and no entity, so it can be unit-tested as a table.
    • boolean allowed(...), which returns check(...).isEmpty(). The DTO flags use it.
  • D2 — Refusal is a nested record SuggestionTransition.Refusal(HttpStatus status, int subCode, String messageKey) in enums/. It is nested so that it does not need its own file. It carries today's exact codes and keys, The service turns it into an exception with one private helper, refuse(Optional<Refusal>). The helper throws error(r.status(), r.subCode(), r.messageKey()), the same error(...) factory that builds today's CustomException.
  • D3 — Constants move with the rules. MAX_REREVIEWS and REOPENABLE_JOB_STATUSES become constants of SuggestionTransition. The service passes SuggestionTransition.MAX_REREVIEWS to the repository's conditional UPDATE. The DB guard and the rule then share one number.
  • D4 — The service keeps the order of operations. Lock the suggestion first. The service locks and reads the job row with findLockedById only when the status is APPROVED and importJobId != null, exactly as at :231-234. PENDING, REJECTED and the non-owner paths never touch the job row. Then it runs check, then the duplicate check, then saves. Inside REOPEN.check the PENDING refusal (4095) comes before the job-status refusal (4096). The canReopen flag arguments at :132/152/197/219/247 keep their current values. list uses REOPEN.allowed. Only the if blocks are replaced. Lock order, transactions, events and error codes stay the same.
  • D5 — The target end state is not a GoF State pattern or Spring State Machine. Three statuses do not justify either.

docs.text:
ID Task Acceptance criteria Depends on ST-1 Add enums/SuggestionTransition.java + Refusal, and a table test SuggestionTransitionTest Every (transition × status) cell is covered, plus REOPEN × each ImportStatus incl. null, and REREVIEW at count 0/1/2. Each refusal returns today's status, subcode and key exactly — ST-2 Use it in VideoSuggestionServiceImpl: lockPending, reopen, requireRereviewable, canReopen, toDto flag; remove the now-unused constants and helpers VideoSuggestionServiceImplTest (incl. its findLockedById verify/never checks), VideoSuggestionControllerTest and AdminVideoSuggestionControllerTest pass unchanged (git diff shows no edits under those test files); mvn verify green with coverage ≥ threshold; no API, DTO or migration change ST-1

Both tasks fit in one commit (~150 changed LOC).

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation A subtle behavior change, e.g. a different error code for one combination The existing tests stay unedited and cover every error path. The table test pins each code The rule and the SQL guard drift apart They share the MAX_REREVIEWS constant (D3)

docs.title: Plan: Trivy Vulnerability Scan on JAR & Dependencies
docs.text: ADR: ADR-0010 Date: 2026-05-30 Status: Ready to implement Effort: ~30 minutes

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Production deployment uses JAR over SSH — Docker image is built but not yet used in production. The scan target is therefore the filesystem (api/ directory): Maven dependencies declared in pom.xml and resolved JARs in target/.

Trivy fs mode detects CVEs in Java libraries by scanning pom.xml and the compiled JAR — no Docker required.

docs.title: Current Pipeline
docs.text:
build ──→ test ──┬──→ deploy (SSH)
                 └──→ docker (not in prod)

docs.title: Target Pipeline
docs.text:
build ──→ test ──┬──→ scan (fs) ──→ deploy (SSH)
                 └──→ docker

scan runs after test (needs the compiled JAR from build) and blocks deploy on CRITICAL findings.

docs.title: Change: Add scan job to funnyapp-ci.yml
docs.text:
Add this job and update deploy to depend on it:

  scan:
    name: 🔍 Trivy Vulnerability Scan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [ build ]

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Download built JAR
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: built-jar
          path: api/target/

      - name: Cache Trivy DB
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/trivy
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-trivy-db
          restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-trivy-db

      - name: Scan filesystem for CVEs (CRITICAL gate)
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          scan-type: fs
          scan-ref: api/
          format: table
          exit-code: '1'
          severity: CRITICAL
          ignore-unfixed: true

      - name: Scan filesystem for CVEs (SARIF upload)
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        if: always()
        with:
          scan-type: fs
          scan-ref: api/
          format: sarif
          output: trivy-results.sarif
          severity: CRITICAL,HIGH
          ignore-unfixed: true

      - name: Upload results to GitHub Security tab
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        if: always()
        with:
          sarif_file: trivy-results.sarif
          category: trivy-fs

Update deploy job to wait on scan:

  deploy:
    name: 🚀 Deploy to Server
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [ test, scan ]   # <-- add scan here

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text: Scenario Result No CRITICAL CVEs ✅ scan passes → deploy proceeds CRITICAL CVE with fix available ❌ scan fails → deploy blocked CRITICAL CVE with no fix ✅ ignored (ignore-unfixed) → deploy proceeds HIGH CVE ✅ visible in GitHub Security tab, does not block deploy

docs.title: First-Run Checklist
docs.text:

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Implement ADR-0017: notifications table, Spring events after commit, owner-only REST API, SSE stream (header auth, in-memory publisher), FE bell with real-time badge + polling fallback, deep link to comment, email digest within the email budget, retention job.

docs.title: Verified Facts (exploration 2026-10-02)
docs.text: Area Fact Impact on plan Async @EnableAsync + @EnableScheduling on FunnyApp; no custom executor; spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true Verify applicationTaskExecutor is virtual-thread based (Boot ≥ 3.2 does this); otherwise add one @Bean Events No ApplicationEventPublisher / @EventListener anywhere First event-driven code — keep it small and documented Scheduler jobs/AppScheduler uses @Scheduled cron/fixedRate, try/catch per job, no ShedLock (single instance) Add digest + retention jobs in the same style Mail MailService (sendSimpleMail, @Async sendInvitation), EmailCacheLimiterImpl daily counter, app.email-setting.max-daily-emails: 200 Digest must check/increment the same limiter and use ≤ 50% of the budget Users UserRepo.findAllByUserName(email) returns User (status ACTIVE/DEACTIVATED); UserSettingsRepository has no finder by user Add findByUserId JWT JwtProvider.verifyToken checks exp but does not expose it; TTL 30 days; filter writes 401 JSON Stream does not close on expiry; emitter timeout 30 min forces re-auth on reconnect CORS origins *.canh-labs.com, localhost:*; all headers allowed fetch with Authorization to the stream works cross-origin Metrics Micrometer + /actuator/prometheus; no custom meters yet First custom gauge FE header AppShell.jsx right section: search, login/profile/logout, theme toggle Bell goes before the theme toggle (logged-in only), also in mobile header FE auth AuthContext exposes jwt, isLoggedIn, logout; client.js exports getBaseUrl-style base + createHeaders() Reuse for the stream fetch FE queries retry: 1, refetchOnWindowFocus: false globally Unread-count query overrides refetchOnWindowFocus: true Deep link AppShell reads ?v={id} on mount → jumpIndex; comment panel opened via onShowComments(video) Extend to ?v={id}&c={commentId} → open panel + highlight FE tests Only window.matchMedia mocked; client.test.js mocks fetch Stream tests need a ReadableStream helper

docs.title: Dependency Graph
docs.text:
NT-1 ──┬──► NT-2 ──┐
       ├──► NT-3 ──► NT-4 ──┐
       └──► NT-5            ├──► NT-7
NT-6 (contract-first) ──────┘

Suggested swarm: Builder A NT-1 → NT-2 → NT-5; Builder B NT-3 → NT-4 (after NT-1 lands); Builder C NT-6 in parallel. In practice NT-1..NT-5 share packages → one BE builder sequentially + one FE builder is safer.

docs.text: Risk Mitigation @Async not on virtual threads → platform pool saturation NT-2 verification step / explicit executor bean Event published inside a rolled-back tx AFTER_COMMIT phase only SSE parser bugs (chunk boundaries) Dedicated unit tests with split chunks Email budget shared with magic links 50% cap + stop run Native upsert with partial unique index syntax Manual review + prod E2E; ON CONFLICT (user_id, group_key) WHERE read_at IS NULL must match the index predicate exactly
