Related PRD: PRD-user-settings Related ADR: ADR-0016: User Settings Design Related Spec: spec-user-settings

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Implement the self-service Settings feature: a backend user_settings store with GET/PATCH preference endpoints and a soft-delete account endpoint, plus a frontend Settings view wired into the existing nav. Behavior is fully defined by the spec; this plan sequences the work and pins it to verified codebase patterns.

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• New user_settings table + JPA entity + repository (BIGINT PK/FK to users).
  • users lifecycle columns (status, deleted_at) + deactivated-user auth guard.
  • GET /user/settings (lazy-create defaults), PATCH /user/settings (atomic partial), DELETE /user/account (soft-delete + step-up verify).
  • Capability fields (passwordEnabled, mfaEnabled, mfaAvailable) on UserDetailDto//user/me.
  • Display-only accountStatus behind a feature flag.
  • Frontend Settings view (Account Identity, Notifications, Playback, Privacy, Danger Zone) wired via AppShell activeNav, settingsApi, React Query hooks, delete-account modal.
  • Unit + controller tests meeting the coverage gate.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Real subscription/billing integration & "View Billing History" (ADR R-2 — placeholder only).
  • Hard-purge scheduled job for deactivated accounts (ADR D3 — deferred).
  • Watch-history recording suppression logic (Watch History not yet implemented; incognitoEnabled is stored only — ADR-0013).
  • "Manage Connected Apps", livestream/DM notifications, Data Export pipeline (PRD out-of-scope).

docs.title: Architecture Changes
docs.text:
Frontend (webapp)                      Backend (api)
─────────────────                      ─────────────
AppShell (activeNav==='settings')      UserSettingsController  @RestController
  └─ SettingsPage.jsx                    GET   /user/settings   (no rate limit)
       ├─ useSettings()  ──GET──┐        PATCH /user/settings   @RateLimited(permit=20)
       ├─ useUpdateSettings()─PATCH┐     DELETE/user/account    @RateLimited(permit=3) @AuditLog
       └─ DeleteAccountModal ─DELETE┐         │
                                    └────►  UserSettingsServiceImpl
                                              ├─ AppUtils.getCurrentUser() → UserDetailDto
                                              ├─ Totp.verify(otp, secret)  (delete step-up)
                                              ├─ UserSettingsRepository (JpaRepository)
                                              └─ UserRepo (status/anonymize on delete)
                                            ┌────────────┴────────────┐
                                       user_settings (new)    users (+status,+deleted_at)

docs.title: Key Decisions
docs.text: Decision Rationale Frontend wiring via AppShell activeNav === 'settings', NOT a react-router /settings route Verified: app has no route-based views; a "Settings" nav button already exists rendering <ComingSoon>. Spec correction: "route /settings" → state-nav settings. Error responses are { status: "FAILED", error: {...} } via RestExceptionHandler Verified envelope differs from the spec's bare ResultErrorInfo. Spec correction: error body is wrapped under error. Frontend client.js already normalizes to { message, status }. Service uses @RequiredArgsConstructor (comment-style) or setter @Autowired (share-style) Both are accepted in the codebase; use @RequiredArgsConstructor for the new impl (simpler). Reuse Totp.verify(otp, user.getMfaSecret()) for delete step-up No new MFA code; mirrors UserServiceImpl.verifyMfa. Add confirmation to logging.masking.fields; otp already masked Spec security requirement; minimal config change. UserSettings PK = user_id BIGINT (1:1), entity @Id (not @GeneratedValue) Matches ADR schema; User.id is BIGINT IDENTITY. Note: differs from UUID entities like VideoComment.

      • deleteAccount(DeleteAccountRequest) — load user; if already DEACTIVATED → 409; if mfaEnabled require valid totp.verify(otp, secret) else 403; else require confirmation == userName else 400; set status=DEACTIVATED, deletedAt=now, anonymize userName → deleted_user_<id>, null password/mfaSecret.

docs.text:
Design source (do NOT re-fetch — already downloaded):

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Status: Draft Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-01 Related Trello: [9] Backend – Implement Like/Unlike and View Count APIs (like part only), [10] Frontend – Like/Unlike Button Decision class: Two-Way Door (new isolated table + endpoints, no change to existing schemas/APIs) → plan only, no ADR

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
VoteButtons.jsx calls POST /v1/funny-app/video/like and /video/unlike, but no backend endpoint exists → Spring returns 404 "No static resource v1/funny-app/video/like". The FE also has logic bugs:

  1. Dislike button calls unlike (dislike ≠ remove like).
  2. Toggling a vote off only changes local state — no API call.
  3. catch {} swallows errors, so the UI shows a vote the server never stored.
  4. video.upvotes / downvotes are never returned by /video-stream/list (VideoDto has no such fields), so counts always start at 0.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Authenticated users can like, dislike, or remove their reaction on a feed video (one reaction per user per video). Everyone sees like/dislike counts; logged-in users see their own reaction persisted across reloads.

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• Videos from the swipe feed (video_sources, GET /video-stream/list)
  • New table video_reactions, entity, repo, service, controller, DTOs
  • FE: api.put, api/reactions.js, useVideoReaction hook, rewrite VoteButtons
  • Unit tests BE (Mockito + @WebMvcTest) and FE (Vitest)

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• YouTube top-videos (youtube_video table — counts come from YouTube API)
  • Guest (unauthenticated) reactions
  • Reaction counts embedded in /video-stream/list (see Decisions)
  • View count tracking (other half of Trello [9])
  • Hot-score integration (future: like/dislike as a signal for priority)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
[VideoSwiper] → [VoteButtons]
                     ↓ useVideoReaction(videoId)   (React Query key ['reaction', videoId])
[api/reactions.js]
  GET    /v1/funny-app/videos/{videoId}/reaction   → summary (public; myReaction=null for guests)
  PUT    /v1/funny-app/videos/{videoId}/reaction   body {reaction: LIKE|DISLIKE}  (auth)
  DELETE /v1/funny-app/videos/{videoId}/reaction   (auth)  ← "unlike" / "un-dislike"
        ↓ Spring Boot
[VideoReactionController] → [VideoReactionService / Impl] → [VideoReactionRepository]
        ↓
[PostgreSQL: video_reactions]

All three endpoints return the same ReactionSummaryDto, so FE replaces its cache with the server truth after each mutation.

{ "videoId": 42, "likeCount": 10, "dislikeCount": 2, "myReaction": "LIKE" }

docs.title: Key Decisions
docs.text: Decision Choice Rationale Data model 1 row per (user, video) with reaction enum column Like ⇄ dislike is a single UPDATE; mutual exclusion enforced by PK Write API PUT (set) + DELETE (clear), video-centric URL Idempotent; client never tracks reaction IDs; matches REST + comments URL style (/videos/{id}/...) Upsert Native INSERT … ON CONFLICT (user_id, video_id) DO UPDATE in repository Race-free under concurrent clicks; no raw SQL in service layer Counts COUNT(*) … GROUP BY reaction on demand, index (video_id, reaction) Exact, simple; feed fetches one video at a time. Denormalized counters deferred until needed Counts not in list API Separate GET /reaction per active video Keeps /video-stream/list user-agnostic and cacheable; no change to VideoDto FK user_id → users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, video_id → video_sources(id) ON DELETE CASCADE Reactions are meaningless once user/video is gone Unauthed write AppUtils.getCurrentUser() in service → 401/403 Same as UserSettingsServiceImpl Rate limit @RateLimited(permit = 30) on PUT/DELETE Prevents click spam; consistent with other writes CORS PUT/DELETE already in setAllowedMethods (WebSecurityConfig.java:124) No change needed

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE video_reactions (
    user_id    BIGINT      NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id)         ON DELETE CASCADE,
    video_id   BIGINT      NOT NULL REFERENCES video_sources(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    reaction   VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL CHECK (reaction IN ('LIKE', 'DISLIKE')),
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, video_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_video_reactions_video ON video_reactions(video_id, reaction);

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
• Model: entity/VideoSuggestion, enums/SuggestionStatus and enums/SuggestionRejectReason (DUPLICATE, INAPPROPRIATE, LOW_QUALITY, COPYRIGHT, OTHER), plus repo/VideoSuggestionRepository.

  • service/VideoSuggestionService and its impl.

    User-facing:

    • submit(url, title, note)
      1. Parse the URL with ImportUrlValidator.parse (shared allowlist and normalization).
      2. Enforce the daily limit: countByUserIdAndCreatedAtAfter(now − 24h) ≥ app.video-suggestion.daily-limit (default 5) gives 429 error.suggestion.dailyLimit.
      3. Reject duplicates with 409 error.suggestion.duplicate when either:
        • a suggestion for the same normalizedUrl is pending, or
        • an import job for that URL exists with status in ACTIVE ∪ {DONE}.
      4. Save. The partial unique index is authoritative: DataIntegrityViolationException also maps to 409.
    • mine(status, page, size) returns the user's own suggestions, newest first, with an optional status filter and a size clamped to 50. Each has liveVideoId when its job's drive_file_id exists in video_sources. The modal uses page 0 with size 5, and History uses pages of 20.

    Admin:

    • list(status, page) lists suggestions, pending first.
    • approve(id, titleOverride)
      1. Require import to be enabled, otherwise 503 error.import.disabled.
      2. Lock the suggestion row and require PENDING, otherwise 409.
      3. Call VideoImportService.create(single item, scheduledAt = now, adminId). If that line result is an error (for example a duplicate active job), return 409 with the import's code.
      4. Set APPROVED, import_job_id, reviewed_*.
      5. Publish SuggestionReviewedEvent.
    • reject(id, reason, note) requires a note when the reason is OTHER, sets REJECTED, and publishes SuggestionReviewedEvent.
    • Controllers:
    • VideoSuggestionController /suggestions, authenticated:
      • POST with @RateLimited(permit=10) and @AuditLog.
      • GET /mine?status&page&size with @RateLimited(60).
    • AdminVideoSuggestionController /admin/video-suggestions, with @HasPermission(ADMIN) like the import controller:
      • GET ?status&page
      • POST /{id}/approve
      • POST /{id}/reject
      • GET /pending-count for the tab badge.
    • "Live" hook:
    • VideoStorageServiceImpl.saveInfo, after save, publishes VideoIngestedEvent(driveFileId, videoSourceId, videoId).
    • SuggestionLiveListener (AFTER_COMMIT + @Async, like the notification listeners) does the following:
      1. Finds the import job by drive_file_id.
      2. Finds the suggestion by import_job_id.
      3. Notifies SUGGESTION_LIVE with videoId.
    • A new video is PUBLISHED and visible by default, so "live" is accurate.
    • Notifications:
    • NotificationType gains SUGGESTION_APPROVED, SUGGESTION_REJECTED and SUGGESTION_LIVE. The type column is VARCHAR(30) with no CHECK, so no migration is needed.
    • The group key is suggestion:<id>:<type>, so they never collapse with each other.
    • The payload holds { title, reason }.
    • The digest gets new mail.digest.item.suggestion* keys in both properties files.
    • i18n: new error.suggestion.* keys in both properties files; the parity test keeps them in sync.
    • Config: app.video-suggestion.daily-limit: ${VIDEO_SUGGESTION_DAILY_LIMIT:5}.

FE-1 SuggestVideoModal, API and hooks, AppShell FAB rewiring (users get the modal, admins get Admin → Import), removal of ShareModal, videosApi.share/delete and the header upload icon 1d BE-2 contract Submitting shows the item as "Chờ duyệt" in the recent list. Duplicate and limit errors are translated. An admin's FAB opens the Import tab. There are no ShareModal references left. Tests run in vi with en render tests. FE-2 Admin SUGGESTIONS tab: table, filter, approve (title override), reject (reason and note), pending badge 1d BE-2 contract Approve moves the row to "Đã duyệt" and a job appears in the Import tab. Reject requires a reason, and a note for OTHER. The badge count updates. Tests pass. FE-3 Notification rendering for the three types and their click behaviour 0.5d FE-1, BE-3, FE-4 Titles are translated in vi and en. LIVE opens the video. APPROVED and REJECTED open History → My suggestions, where REJECTED shows the reason. FE-4 History page (HistoryView) replaces ComingSoon, with a "My suggestions" section: status filter, paging, live "Xem", reject reason, logged-out hint 0.5d BE-2 contract The History nav shows the user's suggestions with working filters and paging. A live item plays its video. A guest sees the sign-in hint. Tests run in vi with an en render test. QA-1 Local end-to-end and prod smoke 0.5d all A user suggests a link and an admin approves it. The job runs, the cron ingests the video, the user gets three notifications (approved, live, plus the digest email), and the video plays from the LIVE notification. A 6th suggestion in a day is blocked. A reject shows its reason.

The total is about 6.5 days, which makes this a Medium feature (PRD and plan).

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation VIDEO_IMPORT_ENABLED is false on prod, so approvals fail Approve returns a clear 503, and submissions still queue. Enabling import is an owner decision, and its default stays false. Spam, or links to inappropriate content Login is required, the daily limit is 5, admins approve every suggestion, and the reject reasons are logged with @AuditLog. The "live" event is missed (async after commit, JVM restart) mine() also computes liveVideoId from the DB, so the status stays correct even if a notification is lost. Concurrent approve of the same suggestion Row lock plus a PENDING check. The import's partial unique index blocks duplicate active jobs. The extra event changes the cron ingest It is publish-only. The listener runs after commit and asynchronously, so ingest latency and failure modes stay the same.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Status: Superseded by plan-watch-history-v2 (2026-10-15) Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-06-01 Beads Issue: N/A Related PRD: PRD-watch-history-opus Related ADR: ADR-0014: Watch History Design (Opus) Related Spec: Spec: Watch History (Opus)

Note: Generated with Claude Opus 4.8 as a model-comparison exercise against plan-watch-history.md. Same feature, independently derived. The key implementation divergences from the sibling plan are: BIGINT IDENTITY PK (not UUID), and a native ON CONFLICT upsert + single bulk-eviction query inside one transaction so the concurrency cases (EC-8, EC-9) hold by construction rather than relying on find-then-insert.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Implement Watch History end-to-end: fire-and-forget auto-record on play, /history page replacing ComingSoon, a "watched" badge on video cards, and delete/clear operations — all scoped to the authenticated user, with a hard 500-entry cap enforced atomically.

  • Backend: entity, repository (native upsert + bulk evict), service, controller, DTOs
  • Frontend: watchHistory.js API module, React Query hooks, WatchedBadge, HistoryPage, AppShell wiring

  • History-based recommendations

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
[VideoSwiper — on play event]
        ↓ fire-and-forget (no await), 30/min rate-limited
[api/watchHistory.js → POST /v1/funny-app/watch-history]
        ↓
[WatchHistoryController]
[WatchHistoryService.recordWatch — @Transactional]
        ├── native UPSERT ON CONFLICT (user_id, source_video_id)
        └── if row count > 500 → bulk DELETE oldest down to 500   (same tx)
[WatchHistoryRepository]
        ↓
[PostgreSQL: watch_history]

[Page load] → GET /watch-history/ids → useWatchedIds → Set<Long>
                                          ↓
[VideoSwiper card → WatchedBadge — Set.has(video.id)]   (0 extra calls)

[AppShell activeNav === 'history'] → HistoryPage → GET /watch-history

docs.title: Key Decisions (from ADR-0014 + Spec)
docs.text: Decision Choice Divergence from sibling plan Primary key BIGINT IDENTITY (matches users/video_sources) sibling used UUID Recording trigger Frontend fire-and-forget POST on play same Upsert Native INSERT … ON CONFLICT (user_id, source_video_id) DO UPDATE SET watched_at = now() sibling used find-then-insert (race on EC-9) Cap eviction Single bulk DELETE … WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT … LIMIT 500) style, same transaction as upsert sibling deleted one oldest row, non-atomic note Re-watch Upsert moves entry to top same Invalid videoId 200, recorded with video_id = null, source_video_id = videoId same Ownership user_id from JWT subject only — no client userId same intent, made explicit Rate limit @RateLimited(permit = 30) on POST sibling 30 too

docs.text:
• [ ] 1.1 Create api/src/main/resources/db/changelog/sql/202606010001-create-watch-history-table.sql 

    CREATE TABLE watch_history (
    id              BIGINT      GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id         BIGINT      NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    video_id        BIGINT               REFERENCES video_sources(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    source_video_id BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    watched_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT uq_watch_history_user_video UNIQUE (user_id, source_video_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_watch_history_user_watched ON watch_history(user_id, watched_at DESC);

  • [ ] 1.2 Register the changeset in db.changelog-master.yaml (follow existing <include file=...>/yaml pattern used for 202605010001).

docs.title: Phase 2: Entity (0.5 day)
docs.text:
• [ ] 2.1 Create api/.../entity/WatchHistory.java (extends BaseDomain, mirroring VideoSource)
    • @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY) Long id — BIGINT, matches User/VideoSource
    • @ManyToOne(fetch = LAZY) @JoinColumn(name="user_id") User user
    • @ManyToOne(fetch = LAZY) @JoinColumn(name="video_id") VideoSource video (nullable)
    • @Column(name="source_video_id", nullable=false, updatable=false) Long sourceVideoId
    • @Column(name="watched_at", nullable=false) Instant watchedAt
    • @Table(name="watch_history", uniqueConstraints=@UniqueConstraint(name="uq_watch_history_user_video", columnNames={"user_id","source_video_id"}))
    • Lombok per project style (@Getter @Setter @SuperBuilder @NoArgsConstructor @AllArgsConstructor)

docs.title: Phase 3: Repository (0.5 day)
docs.text:
• [ ] 3.1 Create api/.../repo/WatchHistoryRepository.java extends JpaRepository<WatchHistory, Long> 
    // Badges — page load
@Query("SELECT w.sourceVideoId FROM WatchHistory w WHERE w.user.id = :userId")
List<Long> findSourceVideoIdsByUserId(Long userId);

// List — newest first; JOIN FETCH video to avoid N+1
@Query("SELECT w FROM WatchHistory w LEFT JOIN FETCH w.video " +
       "WHERE w.user.id = :userId ORDER BY w.watchedAt DESC")
List<WatchHistory> findHistoryByUserId(Long userId);

// Native atomic upsert — single statement, satisfies EC-9
@Modifying
@Query(value = """
    INSERT INTO watch_history (user_id, video_id, source_video_id, watched_at)
    VALUES (:userId, :videoId, :sourceVideoId, now())
    ON CONFLICT (user_id, source_video_id)
    DO UPDATE SET watched_at = now(), video_id = EXCLUDED.video_id
    """, nativeQuery = true)
void upsert(Long userId, Long videoId, Long sourceVideoId);

// Bulk eviction — keep newest 500, delete the rest in one statement (EC-3, EC-8)
@Modifying
@Query(value = """
    DELETE FROM watch_history
    WHERE user_id = :userId
      AND id NOT IN (
        SELECT id FROM watch_history
        WHERE user_id = :userId
        ORDER BY watched_at DESC
        LIMIT 500
      )
    """, nativeQuery = true)
void evictOverCap(Long userId);

@Modifying
void deleteByUserIdAndSourceVideoId(Long userId, Long sourceVideoId);

@Modifying
void deleteByUserId(Long userId);
    > video_id in the upsert is the verified VideoSource.id or null when the id is unknown; source_video_id is always the input id.

docs.title: Phase 4: DTOs (0.5 day)
docs.text:
• [ ] 4.1 Create in api/.../dto/:
    • WatchHistoryDto — { Long id, Long sourceVideoId, Long videoId, String title, String poster, Instant watchedAt } (id/videoId may be null per Rule 3)
    • WatchHistoryIdsDto — { List<Long> videoIds }
    • RecordWatchRequest — { @NotNull @Positive Long videoId }

docs.title: Phase 5: Service (1 day) — the correctness core
docs.text:
• [ ] 5.1 Create api/.../service/impl/WatchHistoryServiceImpl.java (interface WatchHistoryService in service/, per project pattern)
    • Resolve user: SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication().getDetails() → UserDetailDto → getId(). Never read a userId from the request.

  • [ ] 5.2 Methods: 

    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
WatchHistoryIdsDto getWatchedIds();          // findSourceVideoIdsByUserId(currentUserId)

@Transactional(readOnly = true)
List<WatchHistoryDto> getHistory();          // findHistoryByUserId → map (null-safe title/poster)

@Transactional
void recordWatch(Long videoId);
// 1. Resolve videoId → VideoSource id (or null if not found). source_video_id = videoId.
// 2. repo.upsert(userId, resolvedVideoId, videoId)   // atomic, no duplicate (EC-9)
// 3. repo.evictOverCap(userId)                       // bulk, same tx (EC-3, EC-8)

@Transactional
void removeEntry(Long videoId);              // deleteByUserIdAndSourceVideoId — idempotent (EC-5)

@Transactional
void clearAll();                             // deleteByUserId

  • [ ] 5.3 Unknown videoId: recordWatch must not throw — resolve video_id = null, persist silently, return 200 path (EC-2).

  • [ ] 5.4 Contract validation via Contract.require(videoId != null && videoId > 0, ...) for the service-layer guard (controller @Valid is the first gate).

Why native upsert + bulk evict: a find-then-insert approach races under two concurrent new-video plays (sibling plan's EC-8/EC-9 gap). ON CONFLICT makes the insert atomic against the unique constraint, and a single DELETE … NOT IN (… LIMIT 500) is self-healing — after any interleaving the user converges to ≤ 500. Both run in one @Transactional.

docs.title: Data: one migration, 202610160001-create-watch-history.sql
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE watch_history (
  user_id      BIGINT      NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  video_id     BIGINT      NOT NULL REFERENCES video_sources(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  watched_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  position_sec INT         NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (position_sec >= 0),
  duration_sec INT                     CHECK (duration_sec > 0),
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, video_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_watch_history_user_recent ON watch_history (user_id, watched_at DESC);

Other migrations already reference users(id), so the foreign key works as written.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
WatchHistoryRepository uses native SQL, like VideoReactionRepository:

  • upsertWatched(userId, videoId): 

    INSERT INTO watch_history (user_id, video_id, watched_at)
SELECT :u, v.id, now() FROM video_sources v
WHERE v.id = :vid AND v.is_hide = false AND v.status = 'PUBLISHED'
ON CONFLICT (user_id, video_id) DO UPDATE SET watched_at = now()
    It returns the number of rows. 0 means the video is unknown or hidden.

  • trimToCap(userId, cap): 

    DELETE … WHERE user_id = :u AND video_id IN
  (SELECT video_id … ORDER BY watched_at DESC, video_id DESC OFFSET :cap)

  • updateProgress(userId, videoId, pos, dur) runs UPDATE … WHERE user_id = :u AND video_id = :vid. It never inserts.

  • Page query: a constructor-expression or projection that joins video_sources. It takes an optional lower(v.title) LIKE lower(:q) filter, with % and _ escaped. It returns videoId, title, fileId, viewCount, watchedAt, positionSec, durationSec. One query plus one count.
  • findSummary(userId) returns (video_id, position_sec, duration_sec), limit 500.
  • deleteOne(userId, videoId), deleteAll(userId).

WatchHistoryService / WatchHistoryServiceImpl:

  • recordWatch(userId, videoId):
    • If settingsRepo says incognito, it returns without writing.
    • Otherwise @Transactional upsert, then trim to app.watch-history.max-entries (default 500).
  • saveProgress(userId, videoId, pos, dur):
    • It is a no-op in incognito.
    • It clamps dur to 1..21600 and pos to 0..dur, and ignores non-finite or negative values.
  • list(userId, q, page, size):
    • size is clamped to 1..50.
    • q is trimmed, at most 100 characters, and a blank q means no filter.
    • The DTO includes completed = pos >= 0.9·dur || dur − pos <= 10.
  • summary(userId), remove(userId, videoId), clear(userId).

Hook into the view path.

  • In VideoViewController.record, when AppUtils.getCurrentUser() is non-null, call watchHistoryService.recordWatch(user.getId(), videoId) in addition to recordView. It is not gated by the 30-minute dedupe, so a re-watch still bumps watched_at.
  • Wrap it in try/catch and log at warn level. A history failure must never fail the view call (still 204).

WatchHistoryController, base /watch-history, authenticated. These paths are not in the public AppConstant list.

Method Path Body / params Response Rate GET /watch-history q?, page=0, size=20 {data: Page<WatchHistoryItemDto>} 60 GET /watch-history/summary — {data: [{videoId, positionSec, durationSec, completed}]} 30 PUT /watch-history/{videoId}/progress {positionSec, durationSec} 204 120 DELETE /watch-history/{videoId} — 204 20 DELETE /watch-history — 204 20
  • CORS needs no change: filter/WebSecurityConfig already allows PUT and DELETE.
  • Account deletion: UserSettingsServiceImpl.deleteAccount calls watchHistoryRepository.deleteAll(userId).
  • Config: add app.watch-history.max-entries: ${WATCH_HISTORY_MAX_ENTRIES:500}.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
• api/watchHistory.js: list(q, page, size), summary(), progress(videoId, pos, dur), remove(id), clear().
    • progress uses fetch with keepalive: true. Add a keepalive option to client.js request().
    • It is a no-op for guests.
  • hooks/useWatchHistory.js:
    • useWatchHistoryInfinite(q) under query key ['watchHistory', 'list', q].
    • useWatchHistorySummary(), enabled only when logged in, with staleTime of 60 s. It returns a Map<videoId, {positionSec, durationSec, completed}>.
    • Mutations useRemoveWatchEntry and useClearWatchHistory, which invalidate ['watchHistory'].
    • The view call invalidates the summary and list after it succeeds.
  • VideoPlayer.jsx:
    • After the view is sent, if the user is logged in, report progress: on pause, on active → false, on visibilitychange hidden, every 30 s while playing, and on unmount. Throttle to at most one call per 10 s, except on pause or unmount.
    • New prop startAt (seconds). On loadedmetadata, seek to it once when it is > 5 and < duration − 10.
  • Resume entry:
    • AppShell.playVideo(id, { startAt }) stores deepLinkStartAt next to deepLinkId.
    • PublicFeed passes it to the VideoPlayer of the deep-linked video only, once.
    • History cards call onPlayVideo(id, { startAt: completed ? 0 : positionSec }).
  • Badges:
    • WatchedBadge shows "Đã xem" when completed, otherwise a 3 px progress line.
    • It appears in the VideoPlayer meta overlay (feed and Library player) and on ExploreView cards. It reads from the summary map, with no request per card.
  • History page (HistoryView), per the Stitch design:
    • Top tab pills: "Lịch sử xem (N)" | "Đề xuất của tôi (N)". "Lịch sử xem" is the default tab. The tab is remembered in localStorage, wrapped in try/catch.
    • WatchHistorySection contains:
      • a search input (debounced 300 ms);
      • a controls row with the "Tạm dừng lịch sử" switch and a "Xoá toàn bộ" button. The switch PATCHes incognitoEnabled through the existing settings hook and invalidates settings. The clear button asks for confirmation through an app-modal.
      • When paused, a banner reads "Lịch sử đang tạm dừng".
      • Day groups Today / Yesterday / Earlier, computed in local time.
      • WatchHistoryCard:
        • thumbnail via thumbnailUrl(fileId), with a duration or "Đã xem hết" chip
        • title, view count (compactNumber)
        • "Đã xem {relativeTime}"
        • a progress bar
        • a "⋮" menu with "Xoá khỏi lịch sử"
      • "Xem thêm" paging.
    • Reuse the hist-* styles and add hist-watch-* classes, with light theme and ≤ 768 px rules.
  • i18n: add keys under the history namespace (vi and en) for the tab, groups, controls, confirm dialog, empty, paused and badge. The Settings incognito description is unchanged.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Extra write on every logged-in view on a 1 vCPU VM One upsert plus one bounded delete on an indexed key, in the same transaction. Measure the p95 of the view call in QA-1 (PRD target ≤ +10 ms). Progress heartbeats while many users watch 30 s interval, a 10 s client throttle, a 120/min server limit, and an UPDATE by primary key only. keepalive fetch is dropped on tab close Best effort by design. Pause and switch events already save most positions. Resume deep link races with feed loading startAt is applied on loadedmetadata of the deep-linked player only, once. Covered by FE-2 tests. Incognito toggled while a video plays The server checks the flag on every write, so the client state does not matter. Search on Vietnamese titles without accents Documented as OQ-2. Follow-up: unaccent.

docs.text: Decision Choice Recording trigger Frontend fire-and-forget POST on play Cap strategy Auto-evict oldest (sliding window, 500 entries) Re-watch Upsert — update watched_at, move to top Invalid videoId 200 silent ignore (not 404) State delivery GET /ids at page load → client-side Set.has() Uniqueness UNIQUE(user_id, source_video_id) — stable under ON DELETE SET NULL

    staleTime: Infinity,

    queryClient.invalidateQueries(['watchHistory', 'ids'])
  }
}

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Status: Done Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-10 Related ADR: ADR-0019 Admin Video Import Related Plan: plan-admin-video-import

Admin pastes one or many YouTube / Facebook video URLs; the server downloads them with yt-dlp, uploads them into the Google Drive folder that the existing sync cron reads, and the cron brings them into the app. Imports run now or at a scheduled time; progress is visible in the admin page.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: Adding a video today means: download it on a PC, upload it to Google Drive by hand, wait for the cron. For short clips (Reels, Shorts) this is slow and repetitive, and cannot be done from a phone.

docs.title: Goals & Success Metrics
docs.text: Goal Metric Target Faster content intake Admin time per video < 30 s (paste + submit) Reliable Imports ending DONE (valid public URL) ≥ 95 % Same ingest path Imported videos visible in app after upload ≤ 15 min (next cron)

docs.title: User Stories (Admin)
docs.text:
• US-1 Paste one URL, optionally a title, press "Tải ngay" → job starts immediately.
  • US-2 Paste many URLs (one per line, optional URL | Tiêu đề) → one job per line (bulk, max 20).
  • US-3 Choose "Hẹn giờ" and a date/time (Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh) → jobs start at that time.
  • US-4 See each job's status, phase (đang tải / đang upload) and percent, updating automatically.
  • US-5 Title auto-filled from the source when possible ("Lấy tiêu đề"); I can override it.
  • US-6 Cancel a pending/running job; retry a failed one; run a scheduled job now.
  • US-7 See whether a finished job is already in the app ("Đã lên app") or waiting for sync ("Chờ đồng bộ").

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Status: Draft Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-05-31 Version: 1.0 Beads Issue: N/A PR-FAQ: N/A Stakeholders: Product, Engineering, Design

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: Logged-in users who discover interesting videos during browsing have no way to save them for later. When they return to the app, they cannot find the videos again because there is no persistent watch-list — they must re-search, often unsuccessfully, and eventually churn.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
Quantitative Evidence:

  • No native save mechanism exists in the current UI — 100% of "watch later" intent is lost at session end
  • Re-search friction increases with catalog size; the app indexes YouTube content with growing volume

Qualitative Evidence:

  • User behaviour pattern: browse → find video → navigate away → forget → leave app
  • Common user expectation: every video platform (YouTube, Netflix, Twitch) provides a save/bookmark primitive; its absence is felt as a gap

docs.title: Goals & Success Metrics
docs.text: Goal Metric Target Drive return visits through saved content Bookmark-to-watch rate ≥ 40% of bookmarked videos are eventually played Feature adoption % of active users with ≥ 1 bookmark ≥ 20% within 30 days of launch Retention signal Session frequency for bookmarking users vs. non-bookmarking users Bookmarking users return ≥ 1.5× more often

docs.title: Authenticated User
docs.text:
• As a logged-in user, I want to bookmark a video from the video card or player page so that I can find it again later without searching.

    • Acceptance: A bookmark toggle button is visible on every video card and on the player page. Clicking it saves the video; clicking again removes it. State persists across sessions.

  • As a logged-in user, I want to see a visual indicator on video cards I have already bookmarked so that I know at a glance what I saved.

    • Acceptance: Bookmarked videos display a filled/highlighted bookmark icon. Non-bookmarked videos show an outline icon.

  • As a logged-in user, I want a dedicated /bookmarks page that lists all my saved videos so that I can browse and play them in one place.

    • Acceptance: Page shows all bookmarked videos in a grid, sorted by bookmark date (newest first). Each card supports remove-bookmark and play actions.

  • As a logged-in user, I want to organise my bookmarks into named folders/collections so that I can group content by theme (e.g. "Comedy", "Weekend Watch").

    • Acceptance: I can create, rename, and delete collections. I can add a bookmarked video to one or more collections. A default "All Bookmarks" view always exists.

docs.title: Functional Requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Notes FR-1 Authenticated users can add and remove bookmarks on any video Must Have Toggle action; idempotent FR-2 Bookmark state is persisted server-side, scoped to the authenticated user Must Have Stored in PostgreSQL FR-3 /bookmarks route shows all bookmarks for the logged-in user, newest first Must Have Uses ResultListInfo<T> wrapper FR-4 Video cards display a bookmark indicator reflecting current bookmark state Must Have Loaded via React Query FR-5 Users can create named collections (folders) to organise bookmarks Must Have v1 includes full CRUD for collections FR-6 Users can add a bookmark to one or more collections Must Have Many-to-many: bookmark ↔ collection FR-7 Users can remove a bookmark from a collection without deleting the bookmark Should Have Unlinks from collection, bookmark persists in "All Bookmarks" FR-8 Users can delete a collection (bookmarks are not deleted, just unlinked) Should Have FR-9 Bookmark count per video visible to the bookmarking user only Nice to Have Not a social/public counter

docs.title: Non-Functional Requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Target NFR-1 Bookmark toggle API response time < 200 ms p99 NFR-2 Bookmarks page load (list query) < 500 ms p99 for up to 500 bookmarks NFR-3 Security All bookmark endpoints require valid JWT; users can only read/write their own bookmarks NFR-4 Data integrity Deleting a VideoSource record does not silently orphan bookmarks — handle via FK constraint or soft-delete NFR-5 Scalability Single-user bookmark cap of 500 to prevent unbounded growth (enforced at API layer)

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• Add / remove bookmark toggle on video cards and player page
  • Visual bookmark indicator (filled vs. outline icon) on video cards
  • Dedicated /bookmarks page listing all saved videos, sorted by bookmark date
  • Named collections (folders): create, rename, delete
  • Add / remove a video from a collection
  • "All Bookmarks" default view (always present, cannot be deleted)
  • New bookmarks and bookmark_collections DB tables via Liquibase migration
  • Backend REST API: BookmarkController under BASE_URL/bookmarks
  • Frontend: new bookmarks.js API module + /bookmarks route in React Router

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Public or shareable bookmark lists
  • Collaborative / multi-user collections
  • Notifications for bookmarked videos (e.g., "trending now")
  • Bulk import / export of bookmarks
  • Social bookmark counts visible to other users

Assumption: "No v2 planned" means this feature ships as a self-contained, complete experience. No future extension points are required beyond clean API design.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Dependency Owner Status Risk VideoSource entity (video_sources table) Existing Stable Low — FK target for bookmarks User entity (users table) Existing Stable Low — FK target for bookmarks Liquibase migration for new tables Engineering To Do Low — standard pattern JWT authentication (Spring Security) Existing Stable Low — reuse existing filter chain React Query + React Router v7 Existing Stable Low — add new route and query

docs.title: Risks & Mitigations
docs.text: Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation VideoSource deleted while bookmarked M M Add ON DELETE SET NULL or soft-delete VideoSource; handle null in UI gracefully Users create thousands of bookmarks (no cap) L M Enforce 500-bookmark cap at API layer with a 409 Conflict response N+1 query on bookmarks page (fetching collections per bookmark) M M Use JOIN fetch or batch loading in repository; test with 100+ bookmarks Bookmark state stale in UI after toggle L L React Query invalidateQueries on mutation ensures fresh state

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• [ ] Should the bookmark icon appear on the video player page header or as an overlay button on the video?
  • [ ] Is there a maximum number of collections per user? (Suggest: 50)
  • [ ] Should bookmarks survive account deletion, or cascade-delete with the user?

docs.title: Data Model (Sketch)
docs.text:
bookmarks
  id            BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY
  user_id       BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
  video_id      BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES video_sources(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
  UNIQUE (user_id, video_id)

bookmark_collections
  id            BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY
  user_id       BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
  name          VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()

bookmark_collection_items
  collection_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES bookmark_collections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
  bookmark_id   BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES bookmarks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
  PRIMARY KEY (collection_id, bookmark_id)

Assumption: Integer (BIGSERIAL) primary keys are used to match the existing users and video_sources schema, rather than UUIDs used in newer migrations.

docs.title: API Endpoints (Sketch)
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/v1/bookmarks List all bookmarks for current user POST /api/v1/bookmarks Add a bookmark ({ videoId }) DELETE /api/v1/bookmarks/{id} Remove a bookmark GET /api/v1/bookmarks/collections List all collections POST /api/v1/bookmarks/collections Create a collection PUT /api/v1/bookmarks/collections/{id} Rename a collection DELETE /api/v1/bookmarks/collections/{id} Delete a collection POST /api/v1/bookmarks/collections/{id}/items Add bookmark to collection DELETE /api/v1/bookmarks/collections/{id}/items/{bookmarkId} Remove bookmark from collection

docs.title: PRD: Contributor Role and Autopilot Permissions for Reports
Overview
docs.text: Status: Draft Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-23 Version: 1.1 Tracking: N/A (added to docs/tracking.md after approval) PR-FAQ: N/A. This extends an internal tool (PRD-in-app-report); it is not a new user-facing initiative. Stakeholders: nguyenhuuca (owner, SUPER_ADMIN), admins, contributors Builds on: ADR-0026 In-App Report (D6 "Future CONTRIBUTOR"), ADR-0025 Auto Gates, ADR-0015 Bitwise Permissions

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
The owner is the bottleneck for every autopilot run that comes from a report.

  • Only the SUPER_ADMIN can put autopilot:auto or autopilot:auto-merge on a report (ReportServiceImpl.java:103, ADR-0026 line 67). A report from anyone else gets plain autopilot, so the owner must comment /approve at Gate 1 and merge at Gate 2 before a fix reaches prod.
  • There is no role for a trusted person who should send reports but not manage the site. The only way to give someone the Report menu today is ADMIN, which also opens every admin tab: videos, accounts, jobs and drive sync (WebSecurityConfig.java:54, AppShell.jsx:160-161).

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
Quantitative Evidence:

  • Each plain autopilot report needs 2 owner actions (Gate 1 /approve, Gate 2 merge) before it ships (ADR-0022, ADR-0025).
  • Admin reports are capped at 10 a day (ReportServiceImpl.java:59). At full use, that is up to 20 owner actions a day that this feature can remove for trusted reporters.

Qualitative Evidence:

  • Owner (2026-10-23): "the role contributor có thể có permission auto, auto-merge dựa trên SA cấp quyền cho … tùy theo permission được cấp mà trigger autopilot full auto hoặc auto."
  • ADR-0026 D6 already planned a CONTRIBUTOR role between USER and ADMIN for reports, but kept the auto labels SUPER_ADMIN-only. This PRD revisits that part.

docs.title: Goals & Success Metrics
docs.text: Goal Metric Target Remove owner clicks for trusted reporters Share of reports from granted non-SA users that pass both gates with no owner action ≥ 50% within 30 days of launch Keep prod safe Reverts or prod incidents traced to an auto / auto-merge run started by a non-SA report 0 in the first 30 days Least privilege CONTRIBUTOR accounts that can reach a non-report admin endpoint 0 (covered by tests)

docs.title: Owner (SUPER_ADMIN)
docs.text:
• As the owner, I want to give a person the CONTRIBUTOR role so that they can send reports without getting the admin tabs.
    • Acceptance: in the account table, the SUPER_ADMIN or an ADMIN can set a USER to CONTRIBUTOR and back. The CONTRIBUTOR sees the Report menu and no Admin menu.
  • As the owner, I want to grant or revoke auto-merge and auto per account (CONTRIBUTOR or ADMIN) so that only people I trust can skip my gates.
    • Acceptance: two toggles in the account's permission editor. Only the SUPER_ADMIN can change them. They are off for every account until granted, including existing admins.
  • As the owner, I want a revoke to take effect on the next report so that I can stop someone at once.
    • Acceptance: after a revoke, the next create or retry by that account gets 403 for an auto label, with no re-login needed.

docs.title: Contributor / Admin with a grant
docs.text:
• As a granted reporter, I want to pick an autopilot option on the report form, limited to what I was granted, so that my fix ships without waiting for the owner.
    • Acceptance: the form shows "No auto" (default), plus "Auto-merge" if granted auto-merge or auto, plus "Full auto" if granted auto. The issue gets the matching label.
  • As a reporter with no grant, I want my report to still start autopilot so that the owner only has to approve.
    • Acceptance: the form shows no autopilot option; the issue gets autopilot and the type label, as an ADMIN report does today.

docs.title: Contributor
docs.text:
• As a contributor, I want to see all reports and their GitHub state so that I know whether a problem was already reported and handled.
    • Acceptance: the Report list shows every report, as it does for admins today (owner decision, 2026-10-23). The issues are public on GitHub anyway.

docs.title: Functional Requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Notes FR-1 New role CONTRIBUTOR between USER and ADMIN in UserRole Must Have ADR-0026 D6. Roles are stored as strings and ranked by outranks, so inserting it is safe FR-2 CONTRIBUTOR can call only the report endpoints (create, list, retry). Every other /admin/** endpoint stays ADMIN or above Must Have The endpoints stay at /v1/funny-app/admin/reports (owner decision). Today /admin/** is hasAnyRole("ADMIN","SUPER_ADMIN") (WebSecurityConfig.java:54), so /admin/reports/** needs its own rule placed before it, and AdminReportController.java:32 moves to hasRole('CONTRIBUTOR') FR-3 The SUPER_ADMIN and ADMINs can set or remove the CONTRIBUTOR role Must Have Owner decision. Already allowed by the rank rule: an ADMIN may assign roles lower than its own (AdminAccountServiceImpl.java:46,105). An ADMIN still cannot touch the autopilot bits (FR-5) FR-4 Two new permission bits: AUTOPILOT_AUTO_MERGE and AUTOPILOT_AUTO Must Have AUTOPILOT_AUTO implies auto-merge when checked (owner decision Q6). They are stored as independent bits FR-5 Only the SUPER_ADMIN can set or clear the two autopilot bits, on CONTRIBUTOR or ADMIN accounts Must Have updatePermissions (AdminAccountServiceImpl.java:73) must reject a change to these bits by an ADMIN FR-6 New bits are not granted by default: not by defaultPermissions(), not by a role change, and not by a backfill migration of existing admins Must Have UserRole.defaultPermissions() returns ALL_BITS today. ALL_BITS must not grow to include them, or a split mask must be used FR-7 Report create and retry accept autoLabel when the caller holds the right bit at request time: AUTO_MERGE needs AUTOPILOT_AUTO_MERGE or AUTOPILOT_AUTO; AUTO needs AUTOPILOT_AUTO. Otherwise 403 error.report.autoLabelForbidden Must Have Read from the user row in the DB, not from the JWT claim (JwtProvider.java:116), so a revoke is immediate. SUPER_ADMIN keeps every option FR-8 A CONTRIBUTOR or ADMIN report with no auto label gets autopilot + type label (current ADMIN behaviour) Must Have Owner decision Q4b FR-9 Daily cap: one shared cap of 10 per rolling 24 h across all non-SA reports that carry autopilot (ADMIN and CONTRIBUTOR). Over the cap, the issue is created with neither autopilot nor an auto label Must Have Owner decision Q4c. The cap query and its index count only reporter_role = 'ADMIN' today (ReportServiceImpl.java:197, 202610200001-create-app-report.sql:27-28) FR-10 Report form shows the autopilot options allowed by the caller's bits; no option when there is none Must Have ReportPage.jsx:52,88 shows it only to SUPER_ADMIN today. The server check in FR-7 is the real gate FR-11 Account table: role choice includes CONTRIBUTOR; permission editor shows the two autopilot toggles to the SUPER_ADMIN only Must Have AdminAccountTable.jsx:11,68, utils/permissions.js FR-12 Report menu visible to CONTRIBUTOR, ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN; Admin menu stays ADMIN and above Must Have AppShell.jsx:160-161,382 use isAdmin for both today FR-13 Report list: CONTRIBUTOR sees all reports, like admins Must Have Owner decision; no change to list() FR-14 Issue body says who reported by role: "the SUPER_ADMIN", "an ADMIN" or "a CONTRIBUTOR" Should Have ReportIssueContent.java:45. Still no email, name or id (BR-7) FR-15 Grant, revoke and role changes are written to the audit log Must Have Reuse @AuditLog; no new screen (history UI is out of scope) FR-16 Role change keeps the autopilot bits when the new role is CONTRIBUTOR or ADMIN, and clears them when the new role is USER Must Have Owner decision. updateRole overwrites the whole mask today (AdminAccountServiceImpl.java:53). Keeping prevents an ADMIN from silently wiping a SA grant; clearing on USER stops a dormant grant from coming back on a later promotion

docs.title: Non-Functional Requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Target NFR-1 Performance Report create p95 stays < 3 s (PRD-in-app-report NFR-1). The permission check adds no extra DB call beyond loading the current user NFR-2 Security: authZ Server-side checks for every rule (FR-2, FR-3, FR-5, FR-7); hiding UI is never the check. Tests prove a CONTRIBUTOR gets 403 on every non-report admin endpoint NFR-3 Security: least privilege New bits default to off everywhere (FR-6); revocation is effective on the next request (FR-7) NFR-4 Compatibility Existing accounts keep their role and current bits; existing JWTs keep working. No change to the headless workflow or its labels NFR-5 i18n All new UI strings in en and vi (ADR-0020) NFR-6 Coverage LINE coverage stays ≥ api/.coverage-threshold

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• CONTRIBUTOR role (backend enum, security rules, account table, navigation)
  • Two autopilot permission bits, grantable by the SUPER_ADMIN to CONTRIBUTOR and ADMIN accounts
  • Report create/retry: auto-label check by bit instead of by role; shared daily cap across ADMIN and CONTRIBUTOR
  • Report form and list changes for contributors
  • ADR amending ADR-0026 (auto labels from non-owner accounts)

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• A history screen for grants and revokes (v1 relies on @AuditLog)
  • Self sign-up or "request access" for contributors; the SUPER_ADMIN assigns role and bits
  • Notifying a person when they are granted or revoked
  • Auto-revoking a grant after a revert of a run they started
  • A per-user cap or a separate cap for auto-labelled reports (owner chose one shared cap)
  • Any change to .github/workflows/autopilot.yml, the auto-merge script, or the ADR-0025 checks

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Dependency Owner Status Risk In-app report (ReportServiceImpl, AdminReportController, ReportPage.jsx) nguyenhuuca Live (ADR-0026) Low Bitwise permissions + PermissionService (Permission.java, ADR-0015) nguyenhuuca Live Med: ALL_BITS and defaultPermissions() grant every bit to admins today Harness flag permission_enforcement_enabled nguyenhuuca On in prod since 2026-10-23 13:31 UTC Med: with the flag off, @HasPermission checks are skipped. FR-7 must not depend on that flag Headless autopilot + auto labels (ADR-0022, ADR-0025) nguyenhuuca Live Low: unchanged; it trusts any label on an issue created with the owner's PAT GitHub PAT of the owner on the server (ADR-0026 D1) nguyenhuuca Live Med: every granted account acts as the owner toward autopilot

docs.title: Risks & Mitigations
docs.text: Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation A granted non-owner account (or a stolen session) ships bad code to prod through autopilot:auto M H Grants are per account, off by default, SUPER_ADMIN-only, revocable at once (FR-5/6/7). Headless runs keep plan review, code review, QA ×2 and the auto-merge check (protected paths, LOC limit). Shared daily cap of 10 New bits leak to all admins through ALL_BITS / defaultPermissions() or the 2026-10-18 backfill pattern M H FR-6, with tests on role change and on updatePermissions CONTRIBUTOR reaches other admin endpoints because /admin/** is matched by role M H FR-2 and NFR-2 tests over every admin controller Permission checks skipped when the Harness flag is turned off L H The auto-label check is a plain service check, not @HasPermission, so it does not depend on the flag Stale JWT claim keeps a revoked grant alive M M FR-7 reads the bits from the DB at request time Prompt injection in a contributor's report text M M Unchanged from ADR-0022 D3: issue text is data, denylist paths are refused, the merge script blocks protected paths Inserting CONTRIBUTOR shifts ordinal() L M Roles are stored as strings and ranked by outranks (ADR-0026 D6). Check for any ordinal() use or DB check constraint on role

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• [x] May an ADMIN make a USER a CONTRIBUTOR? Yes (FR-3)
  • [x] Report endpoint path? Keep /admin/reports with a path-specific rule (FR-2)
  • [x] Can contributors see all reports? Yes (FR-13)
  • [x] Do the autopilot bits survive a role change? Kept between CONTRIBUTOR and ADMIN, cleared on USER (FR-16)

docs.title: PRD: HLS Streaming for Selected Videos (Feature Flag)
Overview
docs.text: Status: Approved Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-24 Version: 1.0 Tracking: docs/tracking.md row "HLS Streaming" PR-FAQ: N/A. A learning feature on an existing playback path, not a new user-facing initiative. Stakeholders: nguyenhuuca (owner, SUPER_ADMIN), viewers of Drive videos Replaces: the removed ADR-0006 and plan-hls-migration.md (deleted 2026-10-24 in 196e9f54: they predated the Drive force sync, admin delete and the React player)

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
Drive videos (VideoSource.sourceType = 'google_drive') play only through HTTP Range on the raw .full file (GET /v1/funny-app/video-stream/stream/{fileId}, built in Converter.java:73-74). The owner wants to learn and try HLS (.m3u8 playlist + .ts segments) on the real app, without risking playback for everyone and without filling the disk.

This is a learning feature. There is no measured pain point with Range playback today.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
Quantitative Evidence:

  • None. There is no playback-failure or latency data pointing at Range. The owner's goal is to try HLS.
  • Disk on the prod VM is nearly full (owner, 2026-10-24). An HLS copy costs about 1× the .full size per video, so converting every video is not possible.

Qualitative Evidence:

  • Owner: "work for fun"; "Hiện tại tranh hết disk. Chỉ video nào được chọn mới thực hiện HLS."
  • A review of the old plan (2026-10-24) found that HLS for every video at ingest time no longer fits: there are two download paths (scheduler and admin force sync), an admin delete action (#58), and a 350-line VideoPlayer.jsx with resume and watch history.

docs.title: Goals & Success Metrics
docs.text: Goal Metric Target Switch playback without a deploy Toggling Harness flag hls_streaming_enabled changes what the player uses for READY videos ON → HLS, OFF → Range, at the next video-list fetch (≤ 5 min staleTime, or a reload); 0 playback errors caused by the switch Every selected video gets HLS Videos the SUPER_ADMIN turned HLS on for, by status 100% READY, or ERROR with a reason (unsupported codec, low disk) and Range fallback No harm to the VM Disk and CPU incidents caused by transcoding 0 (one job at a time, disk guard)

docs.title: Viewer (guest or signed in)
docs.text:
• As a viewer, I want a video to keep playing whichever path it uses, so that the switch is invisible to me.
    • Acceptance: with the flag ON, a READY video plays through HLS (hls.js on Chrome/Firefox/Android, native on Safari/iOS). If HLS fails, the player falls back to the Range URL at the same position. Resume position and watch history work the same on both paths.
  • As a viewer swiping through reels, I want HLS videos to start like the others, so that swiping stays smooth.
    • Acceptance: VideoSwiper creates the HLS instance for the active slide only and destroys it when the slide changes. No polling per slide.

docs.title: SUPER_ADMIN
docs.text:
• As the SUPER_ADMIN, I want to turn HLS on for one video, so that I choose which videos use disk for segments.
    • Acceptance: a toggle on the row in AdminVideoTable starts a transcode. The row shows PENDING → PROCESSING → READY or ERROR with a reason.
  • As the SUPER_ADMIN, I want to turn HLS off for a video, so that I get the disk space back.
    • Acceptance: turning it off deletes video-cache/hls/{fileId}/ and sets the status to NONE. The .full file is not touched.
  • As the SUPER_ADMIN, I want one global switch, so that I can turn HLS off for everyone at once if something breaks.
    • Acceptance: Harness flag hls_streaming_enabled OFF → the API stops returning hlsUrl, so every client uses Range. Segments stay on disk.

docs.title: Functional Requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Notes FR-1 VideoSource gets an HLS status (NONE, PENDING, PROCESSING, READY, ERROR) and an error reason; default NONE Must Have Liquibase SQL changeset in api/src/main/resources/db/changelog/sql/ (includeAll) FR-2 SUPER_ADMIN-only endpoints under /v1/funny-app/admin/videos/{id}/hls to turn HLS on and off Must Have ADMIN can see the status but not change it, like the Drive force sync (ADMIN views, SUPER_ADMIN acts) FR-3 Turning HLS on queues a transcode. A single worker runs one job at a time Must Have 1 vCPU VM, see the deadlock memory FR-4 Before transcoding, ffprobe checks the codecs. Only H.264 video + AAC/MP3 audio (or no audio) are stream-copied (-c copy). Anything else → ERROR "unsupported codec" Must Have No re-encode in v1 FR-5 Disk guard: if free space < .full size + 1 GB, the job fails with ERROR "not enough disk" before FFmpeg starts Must Have FR-6 Output is video-cache/hls/{fileId}/playlist.m3u8 + seg_N.ts, about 6 s each, VOD playlist. READY only when FFmpeg exits 0 and the playlist exists. A failed job removes its partial output Must Have FR-7 Turning HLS off, or deleting the video (#58 admin delete), removes video-cache/hls/{fileId}/ Must Have The .full file and the Range endpoint stay FR-8 Public endpoints serve the playlist and segments with correct MIME types. Segment names are validated against a strict regex (no .., /). Segments get long immutable cache headers Must Have Same whitelist as /video-stream/** (AppConstant.java:74-75), no token in the URL FR-9 The video DTO includes hlsUrl only when flag hls_streaming_enabled is ON and the status is READY. Otherwise it is null and the client uses Range Must Have Flag read through FeatureFlagService with default false FR-10 VideoPlayer and VideoSwiper play hlsUrl when present (hls.js lazy-loaded, native HLS on Safari), keep resume position and watch history, and fall back to the Range URL on a fatal HLS error Must Have FR-11 AdminVideoTable shows an HLS status column for Drive videos, with an on/off toggle for the SUPER_ADMIN and the error reason on ERROR Must Have Read-only for ADMIN FR-12 A job left in PROCESSING after a restart is reset to PENDING and picked up again at startup Should Have FR-13 Log each job's duration and output size; log the total HLS disk use after each job Nice to Have Structured log, no new metric

docs.title: Non-Functional Requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Target NFR-1 Performance Stream-copy transcode of a 500 MB video < 30 s on the prod VM; playlist and segment responses < 50 ms (static file) NFR-2 Availability Range playback is never affected: the flag OFF, any ERROR, or a missing segment directory all fall back to Range NFR-3 Security Segment and fileId validation against path traversal (CWE-22). The FFmpeg command is built from a list of arguments, never a shell string (CWE-78). On/off endpoints are SUPER_ADMIN-only NFR-4 Resources At most one FFmpeg process at a time; HLS storage only for selected videos NFR-5 Bundle hls.js loaded with a dynamic import only when an hlsUrl is played; it is not added to the main chunk

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• Per-video HLS on/off by the SUPER_ADMIN, with status in AdminVideoTable
  • Stream-copy transcoding with a codec check, disk guard and a single-job queue
  • Public playlist and segment endpoints
  • Global Harness flag hls_streaming_enabled (on/off for everyone)
  • HLS playback with Range fallback in VideoPlayer and VideoSwiper
  • Cleanup of the HLS directory on toggle off and on video delete

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Automatic transcoding at ingest (scheduler or force sync) and bulk backfill: the disk is nearly full
  • Deleting .full files, removing the Range endpoint or the Guava chunk cache: Range is the fallback
  • Re-encoding HEVC/VP9/other codecs to H.264
  • Several quality levels (ABR), AES-128 encryption or DRM
  • Flag targeting per user or by percentage
  • CDN configuration for segments
  • Adding FFmpeg to the Docker image (prod runs on the VM; tracked as a risk)

docs.title: PRD: Hot Video Priority & Trending Feed
Overview
docs.text: Status: Approved Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-02-28 Version: 1.0 Beads Issue: N/A PR-FAQ: N/A Stakeholders: Backend Team, Frontend Team, Product

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: All videos are displayed in a flat, unordered list. Users have no signal about which videos are trending or popular — leading to poor content discovery and lower engagement. Users who want to watch something good must manually browse without any curation.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
Quantitative Evidence:

  • No trending signal exists — 100% of content discovery is manual browsing
  • VideoAccessStats table exists and tracks hitCount + lastAccessedAt, but recordAccess() is commented out — zero access data is being written
  • ShareLink table tracks share events but is not used for ranking
  • VideoCacheImpl already promotes videos with ≥5 cache hits — evidence that popularity signals are valuable

Qualitative Evidence:

  • Users who want to watch "something good" have no starting point other than scrolling
  • Hot content buried in a flat list reduces the chance of viral spread
  • Pre-caching popular videos is already partially designed in VideoCacheImpl — the infrastructure anticipates this need

docs.title: Goals & Success Metrics
docs.text: Goal Metric Target Improve content discovery Average session duration +15% Increase video consumption Videos watched per session +20% Reduce hot video latency Time-to-first-frame for hot videos < 500ms (from ~2s via pre-cache) Drive trending engagement User click-through on hot badges > 30%

docs.title: Viewer
docs.text:
• As a viewer, I want to see a "Trending Now" section at the top of the home page so that I can quickly find popular content without browsing.
    • Acceptance: A "🔥 Trending Now" section shows top 5 hot videos above the main feed.
  • As a viewer, I want hot videos to be visually marked so that I know at a glance which content is currently popular.
    • Acceptance: Video cards with isHot = true display a 🔥 badge.
  • As a viewer, I want hot videos to start playing faster so that I don't wait when choosing trending content.
    • Acceptance: Top 10 hot videos are pre-warmed in cache; first-frame latency < 500ms.

docs.title: Content Viewer (API consumer)
docs.text:
• As an API consumer, I want a dedicated /api/videos/trending endpoint so that I can build trending feeds in any client.
    • Acceptance: GET /api/videos/trending?limit=N returns top N videos sorted by hotScore DESC.
  • As an API consumer, I want to sort the main video list by hotness so that I can offer multiple sort options without a separate endpoint.
    • Acceptance: GET /api/videos?sort=hot returns all videos sorted by hotScore DESC; existing calls without sort are unchanged.

docs.title: Functional Requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Notes FR-1 Activate recordAccess() — async upsert of VideoAccessStats on every stream Must Have Must not block stream response FR-2 Implement hot score formula: weighted hits (60%) + shares (25%) + recency decay (15%) Must Have Min-max normalised across active videos FR-3 GET /api/videos/trending?limit=N endpoint (default 10, max 50) Must Have Served from StatsCacheImpl, TTL 30 min FR-4 Extend GET /api/videos?sort=hot — backward compatible Must Have No change to calls without sort param FR-5 Scheduled job: recompute hot scores every 30 minutes Must Have Runs in AppScheduler FR-6 Pre-warm VideoCacheImpl for top 10 hot videos after each recomputation Should Have Goal: first-frame < 500ms FR-7 Frontend: "🔥 Trending Now" section at top of home page (top 5 videos) Must Have FR-8 Frontend: "🔥 Hot" badge on video cards where isHot = true Must Have Show when hotScore ≥ top 20% threshold

docs.title: Non-Functional Requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Target NFR-1 recordAccess() latency overhead < 5ms (async, fire-and-forget) NFR-2 Trending API response time < 100ms (served from cache) NFR-3 Score recomputation time < 10s for 10,000 videos NFR-4 Additional memory overhead < 50MB NFR-5 Backward compatibility GET /api/videos without sort param — unchanged behaviour NFR-6 Resilience DB write failure in recordAccess() must not fail the stream request

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• Activate VideoAccessServiceImpl.recordAccess() (upsert VideoAccessStats)
  • Hot score algorithm with configurable weights (app.hot-video.* in application.yaml)
  • New GET /api/videos/trending endpoint
  • sort=hot parameter on existing GET /api/videos
  • Liquibase migration: hot_score, is_hot, hot_rank columns on video_sources
  • Scheduled recomputation job every 30 minutes
  • Cache pre-warming for top 10 hot videos
  • Frontend: Trending Now section + 🔥 badge on video cards

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Personalised recommendations (per-user hot scores) — v2
  • Real-time score updates via WebSocket — v2
  • A/B testing framework for ranking algorithms — v2
  • Machine learning-based scoring — v3
  • Like/dislike counts (not present on VideoSource entity)

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Dependency Owner Status Risk VideoAccessStats entity + repo Backend ✅ Exists Low — just needs recordAccess() uncommented ShareLink table Backend ✅ Exists Low — read-only query for share count StatsCacheImpl Backend ✅ Exists Low — already used for stats VideoCacheImpl Backend ✅ Exists Low — preWarm() needs to be called AppScheduler Backend ✅ Exists Low — add new @Scheduled method Liquibase migration Backend ❌ Missing Medium — must land before entity changes VideoSource entity Backend ✅ Active table Low — add 3 columns

docs.title: Risks & Mitigations
docs.text: Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation recordAccess() creates DB bottleneck under high load Medium High Keep @Async + catch all exceptions; add write queue in v2 if needed Hot score biased toward old high-hit videos Medium Medium Apply 24h rolling window + exponential recency decay (e^(-0.1 × hoursAgo)) video_access_stats table grows unbounded Medium Medium Activate cleanUpOldVideos() in AppScheduler to purge rows older than window Scores stale up to 30 minutes after new viral video Low Low TTL is configurable; acceptable for v1 Cache invalidation on new video added Low Low TTL-based invalidation (30 min) sufficient for v1

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• [ ] Should /api/videos/trending be a public endpoint (no auth required)? — Owner: Backend — Due: Before FR-3 implementation
  • [ ] What threshold defines isHot — top 20% by score or a fixed score cutoff? — Owner: Product — Due: Before FR-2 implementation
  • [ ] Should shares from private share-links count toward the hot score? — Owner: Backend — Due: Before FR-2 implementation
  • [ ] Do we need a hot_score_history table for analytics / score trending over time? — Owner: Data — Due: v2 planning

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text:
-- Liquibase migration: 202602280001-add-hot-score.sql
ALTER TABLE video_sources ADD COLUMN hot_score  DECIMAL(5,4) DEFAULT 0;
ALTER TABLE video_sources ADD COLUMN is_hot     BOOLEAN      DEFAULT FALSE;
ALTER TABLE video_sources ADD COLUMN hot_rank   INT          DEFAULT NULL;

CREATE INDEX idx_video_sources_hot_score
    ON video_sources(hot_score DESC) WHERE is_hot = TRUE;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_video_access_stats_video_id
    ON video_access_stats(video_id);

docs.title: Hot Score Formula
docs.text:
hotScore = (0.60 × normalizedHits) + (0.25 × normalizedShares) + (0.15 × recencyBoost)

recencyBoost = e^(-0.1 × hoursAgo)

All inputs min-max normalised to [0, 1] across active videos.

docs.title: API Contract
docs.text:
GET /api/videos/trending 

Query params: limit (int, default=10, max=50)
Response: ResultListInfo<VideoDto>
  data[].videoId     String
  data[].title       String
  data[].embedLink   String
  data[].hotScore    Double
  data[].isHot       Boolean
  data[].rank        Integer  (1 = hottest)

GET /api/videos?sort=hot 

Same VideoDto structure, ordered by hotScore DESC

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Status: Approved (2026-10-14) Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-14 Related ADR: ADR-0020 Internationalization Related Plan: plan-i18n

Every screen, API error and email is available in Tiếng Việt and English. The first visit follows the browser language. Users can switch at any time, and a logged-in user's choice follows them across devices.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
The UI mixes the two languages today. Navigation is in English ("Home", "Library", "Settings") while actions are in Vietnamese ("Phát", "Xoá", "Lưu"). Other text is inconsistent too:

  • Relative times are always English ("2m ago").
  • The magic link email is English.
  • The password-change email is Vietnamese.
  • API errors come in either language.

Non-Vietnamese visitors cannot use most actions, and Vietnamese users get half-English screens.

docs.title: Goals & Success Metrics
docs.text: Goal Metric Target Consistent language Screens with mixed-language UI chrome 0 Complete translations Keys present in both vi and en 100% (enforced by CI parity test) Correct default First visit with a vi-* browser shows Vietnamese; any other shows English 100% (test) Persistent choice A logged-in user's language is restored on a new device Yes Localized email Magic link and password emails arrive in the user's language 100%

docs.title: Users & Stories
docs.text:
• Guest (any language): I see the site in my browser's language and can switch with one click from the header.
  • Logged-in user: I pick my language once, in Settings or the header, and it is used on every device and in emails.
  • Vietnamese user: every button, message, time ("2 phút trước") and email is in Vietnamese.
  • Admin: the admin pages follow the same language setting.

docs.title: Functional
docs.text:
1. Language switcher (VI / EN) in the header, available to guests and users, and in Settings, logged in only.
  2. First-visit default: a browser language starting with vi gives Vietnamese; any other gives English.
  3. Persistence:
    • localStorage for everyone.
    • user_settings.locale for logged-in users, applied after login.
  4. Coverage:
    • All user UI: feed, Explore, Library, auth, comments, notifications, Settings, modals and the mobile nav.
    • The Admin pages.
  5. Formatting: relative time, compact view counts, dates and plurals follow the selected language.
  6. API errors: user-visible errors come back in the request language (Accept-Language).
  7. Emails: the magic link and the password set/change/remove notices go out in the user's language, using the request language for brand-new users.
  8. Not translated: user content (video titles, comments, collection names) and the brand name "Funny Movies".
  9. <html lang> reflects the current language.

docs.title: Non-functional
docs.text:
• No visible flash of the wrong language on load. Resources are bundled, and detection runs before the first render.
  • The bundle grows by less than about 30 KB gzipped.
  • The CI parity tests fail on any missing key, in the frontend JSON or the backend properties.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Languages other than vi and en (the design allows adding them later).
  • Translating user-generated content or video metadata.
  • Right-to-left layouts.
  • Locale-specific URLs (/vi/...) and SEO hreflang.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• OQ-1: Should the header switcher be a globe icon with a menu, or a compact "VI | EN" toggle? Resolved: the "VI | EN" toggle beside the theme toggle.
  • OQ-2: Resolved: the English name for the "Xem sau" default collection is "Watch later".

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: See ADR-0020 Consequences: edge caching, large diff, missing keys.

docs.title: PRD: In-App Report (bug, enhancement, issue → GitHub issue)
Overview
docs.text:
Status: Approved (2026-10-20) Author: nguyenhuuca Date: 2026-10-20 Version: 1.0 Tracking: N/A (added to docs/tracking.md after approval) PR-FAQ: N/A. This is an internal admin tool, not a new user-facing initiative. Stakeholders: nguyenhuuca (owner, SUPER_ADMIN), admins Builds on: ADR-0022 Headless Autopilot, ADR-0025 Auto Gates

A new Report menu, placed just above Settings, lets an admin send a bug, an enhancement or an issue from inside the app. The server creates the GitHub issue with the autopilot label, so headless autopilot (ADR-0022) picks it up without anyone opening GitHub.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
An admin who finds a bug or has an idea while using the app has to:

  1. leave the app;
  2. open GitHub;
  3. write the issue by hand;
  4. add the autopilot label.

The issues end up thin: they rarely say which page, which build or which browser. Reports are also forgotten when the admin is on a phone or in the middle of another task. The autopilot loop is only as good as the issue it starts from, and today that issue is written from memory.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
Quantitative Evidence:

  • Recent autopilot issues (#34, #36, #38) were written by hand. Each one needed the owner to look up the file or the page first; for example, #34 cites three file:line locations.

Assumption: No usage numbers exist yet for how many reports are lost. The metric targets below are the baseline to measure against.

Qualitative Evidence:

  • Owner: "báo lỗi ngay trong app": a report should be sent from where the problem is seen, without leaving the app.
  • Observation: the issues that ran cleanly through autopilot:auto (#36 → PR #37 in ~5 minutes) were the ones with the page and the expected behavior spelled out.

docs.title: 38 ("update video title o tab vault video admin") was a one-line issue written on mobile. The plan job had to infer the page and the viewport.
Goals & Success Metrics
docs.text: Goal Metric Target Fast to report Time from opening Report to "issue created" < 1 minute (median) Issues carry their context Share of app-created issues that include type, page URL, app version and a non-empty description ≥ 90% Labels are always right Share of app-created issues with autopilot, plus the auto label only when a SUPER_ADMIN chose it 100%

docs.title: Admin (ADMIN)
docs.text:
• As an admin, I want a Report menu above Settings so that I can report a problem from any page.
    • Acceptance: the menu shows in the desktop sidebar and the mobile menu for ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN only. A USER does not see it, and the API returns 403 for a USER.
  • As an admin, I want to pick Bug / Enhancement / Issue, type a title and a description, and send them so that a GitHub issue is created for me.
    • Acceptance:
      • Title and description are required.
      • On success, the form shows the new issue number with a link.
      • The issue has the label autopilot plus a type label.
  • As an admin, I want the page I came from, the app version and my browser to be attached automatically so that I don't have to describe them.
    • Acceptance: the issue body has a "Context" section with the page URL (path only, no query string), app version, browser/OS and screen width.
  • As an admin, I want to see the reports I sent, with their GitHub status, so that I know what happened to them.
    • Acceptance: the Report page lists the reports with title, type, date, issue link and open/closed state. The state is read from GitHub when the list opens.

docs.title: Owner (SUPER_ADMIN)
docs.text:
• As the owner, I want to choose autopilot:auto or autopilot:auto-merge on a report so that a small fix goes all the way to prod with no further click (ADR-0025).
    • Acceptance: only a SUPER_ADMIN sees the auto-label choice. The API rejects an auto label sent by an ADMIN with 403.
  • As the owner, I want every report to be audited and rate-limited so that an admin account cannot flood the repo or start many paid autopilot runs.
    • Acceptance:
      • Each create is written by @AuditLog.
      • A user over the limit gets 429.
      • Admins see all reports; each row shows who sent it.

docs.title: Functional Requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Notes FR-1 Report nav item just above Settings, in the desktop sidebar (webapp/src/components/layout/AppShell.jsx:321-328) and the mobile menu (AppShell.jsx:150-152), visible to ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN only Must Have Same requiresAdmin pattern as the Admin item (AppShell.jsx:40) FR-2 Form with: type (Bug / Enhancement / Issue), title (required, ≤ 120 chars), description (required, ≤ 5,000 chars) Must Have i18n en + vi FR-3 Auto-attached context: the page path the user came from, app version, browser/OS (user agent), screen width Must Have Shown read-only in the form before sending FR-4 POST /v1/funny-app/admin/reports creates the GitHub issue through the GitHub REST API and returns its number and URL Must Have Not the gh CLI; the server has no gh FR-5 Labels on every issue: autopilot + one type label (bug / enhancement / report) Must Have FR-6 Auto-label choice (autopilot:auto, autopilot:auto-merge) shown to and accepted from SUPER_ADMIN only Must Have Server-side check, not just hidden in the UI FR-7 Every report is stored: id, reporter, type, title, issue number, issue URL, labels, created_at, status (CREATED / FAILED) Must Have Liquibase migration in api/src/main/resources/db/changelog/sql/ FR-8 GET /v1/funny-app/admin/reports lists reports (paged, newest first) with the GitHub open/closed state read when the list loads Must Have Short cache; on a GitHub failure the list still shows, with the state "unknown" FR-9 If GitHub is down or the token is missing, the report is saved as FAILED and the user sees a clear error and a Retry button Should Have Retry creates the issue for the same stored report FR-10 The form warns that the repo is public and the issue text is public Must Have FR-11 The issue body footer names the reporter by display name, never by email Must Have Public repo

docs.title: Non-Functional Requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Target NFR-1 Performance Create returns in < 3 s at p95, including the GitHub call. The list loads in < 1 s with the state cached. NFR-2 Availability A GitHub outage must not break the app: the report is stored as FAILED and can be retried (FR-9) NFR-3 Security: authZ @PreAuthorize ADMIN for create and list; SUPER_ADMIN for auto labels. Same pattern as AdminJobController.java:32,62 NFR-4 Security: abuse @RateLimited per user on create (e.g. 5 per hour) and @AuditLog on create and retry NFR-5 Security: secret GitHub token from an env var (e.g. GITHUB_REPORT_TOKEN). It must be a fine-grained PAT for this repo only, with Issues: read/write. It is never logged and never sent to the browser. NFR-6 Security: data routing The outbound call to api.github.com is documented (.claude/rules/security.md "Data Routing"). Only the fields in FR-3 and the user's text leave the system. NFR-7 Security: injection The issue text is user input. It is sent as JSON data and never interpolated into a command. Headless autopilot already treats issue text as data (ADR-0022 D3). NFR-8 Extensibility Access is checked so that a future CONTRIBUTOR role (or a permission bit) can be granted Report without changing the endpoints

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
• Report nav item above Settings (desktop + mobile), ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN only
  • Report form: type, title, description, auto-attached context, public-repo warning
  • Server-side GitHub issue creation with autopilot + type label; auto labels for SUPER_ADMIN only

Assumption: Screenshot upload and editing or deleting a report after it is sent are not in v1. Neither was picked for v1 or for later; edits are done on GitHub.
